1.e: "If an email is received into a mailbox, and this email cannot be matched to an existing ticket, a new ticket will be logged. Once the email has been processed … this email will be removed from your mailbox." "Users, and agents can update existing tickets via email."

2.e: Several mailboxes per instance: "sending an email to one of the mailboxes you have connected to your Halo instance". "The type of ticket (ticket type) that is logged from the email will be determined by the mailbox the email was sent into." Per mailbox: "If the email sender cannot be matched to a User" setting. Pick-up: "Can view Unassigned Tickets - For any team which the agent belongs they can view unassigned tickets." "Assign to me - Re-assigns a ticket from one agent to the agent logged in."

3.e: "Acknowledgement Email - An email sent out to user(s) automatically when a ticket is logged for them in Halo. This email is a confirmation that a ticket has been logged."

4.e: Recipient "Related Users of a Ticket: Will notify the end user of a ticket if the ticket triggers an event". Trigger "Ticket Status Changed". Approvals: "Inform the User of the outcome - … the end-user of the ticket will receive an email notification when the approval step is complete."

5.e: "Internal notes and @ notifications let agents discuss, advise and hand off". "Private Note … by default will be hidden from the user".

6.e: "Mention: Triggered when an agent is @ mentioned." To-do lists give "progress-tracking capabilities straight from the ticket interface". "Internal Conversations" create a linked ticket with a "Reply button in the action history".

7.e: "Can Re-assign Tickets - Similar to above and allows reassigning of tickets." Audit: enable "Display the Auditing Tab". "This will show all changes made to that ticket by both system and agents". Webhook/notification event "Ticket Reassigned". **Caveat:** audit-log immutability is not stated (see K.O. #17, Partial).

8.e: "Statuses are set on a ticket to track its progress. These can be created and customised to your needs". Per ticket type: "The "Allowed Values" tab dictates which statuses, actions, etc, are available for use on the ticket type."

9.e: Field types include "Single Selection" (drop-down) and "Date". "Ticket Types > edit a Ticket Type and go to Field List. Here you can add the custom field to the specific ticket type". Per client: "restricted to a particular Client, Site … or Organisation". Required fields exist: "The chosen ticket type must not have any mandatory fields on it" (Slack guide).

10.e: "Each process can contain numerous steps, steps are worked through in sequence". Approver options include "The Users Manager (in AD)" and "The Head of the Users default Department". "Here you can set the Fields Approvers must complete when approving the Step." **Note:** the manager option needs "Azure Active Directory (or Active Directory) integration".

11.e: "The parent-to-child relationship can be used to delegate subtasks or link related issues." "Child tickets can be created automatically using ticket templates." Template "Team/Agent - … you can assign Tickets using this Template to a given Team/Agent." Parent shows "a tab for "Child Tickets" with a count". Notes: "the text entered will then also be added to the children". "Statuses show in the "Ticket information" area on a ticket."

12.e: "Web Access Level" … "e.g. 'This users tickets' which will show that user only their tickets when viewing tickets in the self-service portal." Not verified: visibility of tickets where the user was only added (CC/follower).

13.e: "Can view Tickets that are assigned to other Agents - Similarly can view tickets for other agents in their teams." "Ticket type restrictions … similarly with the client restrictions." "the agent only has access to their associated client's information".

14.e: Included: "No-code Workflows". Rules: "Head to configuration > tickets > ticket rules > new, to create a new rule. Here, set the criteria…". Workflow step: "it will create the child ticket if the "Software" custom field is set to "Microsoft Project" at this stage". Zapier complement: see #50.

15.e: "based on priority, you can set different timed targets for response and resolution". Warnings: "First SLA Warning … Second SLA Warning". "Time-based warnings: Set warnings to trigger a specific number of hours before the deadline".

16.e: Included: "Custom Reports Dashboards Scheduled Reports SLA & KPI Reporting Real-time Widgets". "Your reporting suite comes with an extensive list of out-of-the-box reports." "Team queues give everyone visibility of incoming work".

17.e: "'Audit Log' with a table that shows all changes made to that ticket … and by who." Enabled "per ticket type". **Missing:** the vendor does not state that entries are immutable. Entries "can be redacted from the table by an administrator" (redactions are logged: "an entry is added as a record for each redaction"). Custom fields can be set to "Exclude from Audit/Change History". Agents can hold "Editing of Actions" and "Can Edit All Actions" permissions.

18.e: "Most of the time, the answer already exists - in a ticket resolved last month or an article in your knowledge base. On every new request, Halo surfaces both." "'Matched tickets' allow you to see tickets that share similar properties to the current ticket". Clusters get "an AI generated description and resolution". Cost: default Halo AI connection "Free to use". "no separate AI licence". **Caveat:** matching needs a "vector search database". Whether one is included with the default connection is not stated.

19.e: Auto Triage: "the AI model will then suggest a category, impact and urgency for the ticket, with which the ticket will be updated accordingly." "You do not need your own AI connection". Routing: "Set the assigned Agent based on matched tickets … based on the agent's default team". Included: "AI Triaging". **Note:** Auto Triage is preset only in HaloPSA trials created after September 2025. Otherwise the guide gives build steps.

20.e: "Knowledge base articles can be created automatically using AI, taking in the correspondence between the user and the agent of the ticket and creating a description and resolution for the article." "This is available both when using your own, or the Halo Default AI connection." Also "KB gap detection suggestions" and article duplication detection. **Missing:** no documented link to the existing external knowledge bases (Notion, Outline). See #22 and #51.

21.e: "Build native MCP servers directly inside Halo … Connect Claude, Copilot and Codex directly, choose which tools each agent can use". "The Model Context Protocol (MCP) HTTP endpoint allows AI assistants … to connect and dynamically invoke tools in the Halo API such as knowledge search, ticket logging and updating/executing runbooks." Guide list: "Connecting Claude to Halo's MCP Server".

22.e: No native Notion integration found (see note 5). Routes: (a) custom build on the REST API: "anything that is possible in the the Web Application will be possible to achieve in your integrations". (b) External MCP server in Halo AI: "Configuring connections to third-party MCP servers allows the AI to call external tools for other applications". Notion-side MCP/API not verified. The Zapier Halo–Notion pairing page returned 404.

23.e: Exists: Slack notifications, a "Create Ticket" shortcut, /halo create, /halo update {id} (note + status), and v2 ticket-linked channels ("Any new messages added to Slack will automatically be added here"). **Missing:** the shortcut and /halo commands need "an email address that matches an agent in Halo". Non-agent employees can only use the chatbot app (/startchat). No source documents replies or status changes going back to the requester privately in Slack.

24.e: API: "This page documents the authentication methods available, and the API endpoints and examples of how to call each of the endpoints". Webhooks: "Events: This is a list of events that trigger the webhook to be sent. These are basically the same as Halo Notification profiles … Like notifications you can put conditions on these." Marketplace: "Browse Integrations Show Native Only … Results: 100".

25.e: "you may wish to enable Google Sign-In on the agent application and end user portal". "A Single Sign-On module is available to setup single sign on in your Halo instance." 2FA: "you can allow Two-Factor(2FA) to be used or enforce this on all agents and/or users."

26.e: Trust Centre lists "ISO 27001:2022 Certificate", "ISO 27701:2019 Certificate", "2025 SOC2 Type 2 Report", "Web Application Penetration Test", "Security Documentation Package" (behind "Request access"). Security page: "SOC 2 Type 2 compliant … ISO 27001 compliant and details can be shared on request." DPA available. **Note:** NIS2 is not mentioned on these pages.

27.e: "AWS … data centres within the European Union … including backups, to ensure no data ever leaves the EU." Regions include "Frankfurt". AI: "For customers in the UK and EU, data is processed within the EU". **Missing (information not clear):** the same GDPR page also says EU data "will be based out of the UK". To confirm the location: "check with your dedicated account manager". OpenAI keeps unauthenticated chatbot data "for a period of 30 days" (location not stated). The sub-processor list gives only "Country of Origin United States" (AWS, Microsoft, Datadog …).

28.e: No retention-period or automatic-deletion setting for tickets or attachments was found in the guides read. Found only manual deletion ("Can Delete Tickets - As it describes.") and user anonymisation (see #57). Backup retention is documented ("stored for 3 days, 2 weeks, and 3 months respectively"), but that is not ticket retention.

29.e: "Your end users and the customers who access the portal are always free." "Approvers do not require a Halo licence, as they can approve from the end user portal or simply via email."

30.e: "Assisting your end users, an agent works across web chat, Teams, Slack, and your self-service portal, triaging and logging requests, guiding users through self-service, and escalating to the right person with full context." Ticket logging: "specify what ticket type or template is used when the user requests to log a ticket". Out-of-the-box agents "use the built in OpenAI connection". **Missing:** status check of the user's requests in chat is not verified. "Get My Tickets" and "Search Service Catalogue" are documented only as MCP toolset functions.

31.e: "End users access a branded portal where they can raise requests, report issues, check ticket status and browse a knowledge base". "The services can be configured to either show or be hidden to end-users in the self-service portal, and a ticket type can be linked to them to raise tickets". **Missing:** catalogue items that link out to other systems (e.g. Aboard) are not documented. The Service Catalogue guide (964) returned 404.

32.e: "End users access a branded portal…". "The portal can be configured separately for different departments or user groups." Agents can be limited to one client (K.O. #13, guide 1194). **Missing:** a separately branded portal per client, its setup effort, and reuse of existing data are not verified. Guide 1209 (multiple portals with different branding) returned 404.

33.e: Included: "Mobile Apps". PagerDuty (vendor page): "tickets, updates and notes automatically syncing between Halo and PagerDuty". Catalogue: "AlertOps Integrate with AlertOps to synchronise alerts. Alert Management Native".

34.e: "Clicking 'Add Follower' will open a new menu allowing you to search users, agents and site's users and add them to the followers list." "From v2.250+, notifications can be configured … to inform Agents/Users when a follower is added or removed." **Caveat:** following does not grant access: a user follower without access "will still not be able to access this ticket in the portal but they will receive ticket correspondence via email".

35.e: Native dev-tool link exists: "Azure DevOps Integrate with Azure DevOps to increase collaboration between customer service and development teams. Microsoft Native". **Missing:** no native Notion or GitHub integration found (note 5). Route: custom build on the REST API (see #22).

36.e: "Dynamic visibility restrictions will ensure this field only shows if another field meets certain criteria, such as it contains a specified value, or it is empty."

37.e: "administrators can grant access for other agents to be able to modify the configuration of the specific ticket type. This is a useful feature so that managers can edit the ticket type that their team uses without having to ask the administrator". Field visibility per field: "whether it shows for agents and/or users, and whether it is mandatory". **Note:** the editor must be an agent (licensed).

38.e: Ticket type: "The check-boxes below this can be amended as you need based on who you want to have access to this ticket type". Portal: "can be configured separately for different departments or user groups". **Missing:** no quote that limits a ticket type or form to one requester group (e.g. managers).

39.e: "It is also possible to add a To-Do list that will pre-populate in the ticket." Child templates "create a series of tasks that need to be completed on the raising of a new ticket", each with "Team/Agent". "When a task is marked as complete, the completion date, and who the task was completed by will show". **Missing:** due dates per checklist item or step are not documented.

40.e: "Can view Tickets that are assigned to other Agents - Similarly can view tickets for other agents in their teams. If this is denied, they can only see themselves in any of their teams." "Ticket type restrictions are the only ticket types accessible to the agent". **Missing:** these are per-agent settings. No per-ticket or per-ticket-type "assigned agent + manager only" rule is documented.

41.e: "Tickets: Configuration > Tickets > General Settings > … > Import Tickets". Related guide: "Ticket/Action Import - CSV/XLS/Spreadsheet Method". "Importing data via a spreadsheet allows you to create entities in your Halo instance". **Note:** import is in Configuration (admin area).

42.e: "This will generate a Ticket at a set time with a given interval (such as every month/year/week etc)." Repeat periods include "Monthly Quarterly 6 Monthly Yearly". "It is possible to pre-format the Scheduled Ticket with set Field Values."

43.e: Route 1, webhook (custom receiver): "Webhooks can be created in Halo to retrieve and post data to specific endpoints, for example to send data to an external application". Events work like notifications with conditions. Route 2, Zapier: "Ticket Updated Triggers when a ticket is updated in Halo." No native spreadsheet register found.

44.e: "Datadog Integrate with Datadog to generate tickets from alert webhooks. Alert Management Native". "Azure Monitor Integrate with Azure Monitor to create alerts". Solution pointer: "On every new request, Halo surfaces both" (matched tickets and KB). **Note:** the clients' monitoring tools are not known, so fit per client is not verified.

45.e: Requester: the user "Tickets" tab can show "every ticket ever logged". Period: "A dropdown named "Reporting Period"". Filters: "Adding a filter to the report results with conditions". Amount field type: "Money - A number with two decimal places". **Missing:** filtering reports or lists on custom fields (e.g. amount) is not stated explicitly.

46.e: Included: "Timesheets", "Time Tracking". "Log Time - Logs a quick time entry for the agent." Ticket screen: "Timer that tracks time spent viewing the ticket", shown separately from the "Service Level Agreement/SLA area".

47.e: Alerts: "Time-based warnings: Set warnings to trigger a specific number of hours before the deadline" (K.O. #15). Waiting tickets: ticket type setting "whether you enable SLA hold reminders". **Missing:** agent-set reminders on a ticket and a "time waiting" indicator are not documented in the guides read.

48.e: "The "Tickets" tab shows every ticket that user has raised. By default, it will only show tickets that are open and not on hold, but you can change this filter to view closed tickets, or every ticket ever logged".

49.e: Native Google Workspace: "import agents and users, assign roles to them". "A selection of Google Workspace fields can be mapped to system and custom fields in Halo". Approver "The Users Manager (in AD)" needs AD (K.O. #10). **Missing:** syncing the user's manager from Google Workspace is not documented.

50.e: Zapier app "Halo Service Solutions". Triggers "New Ticket", "Ticket Updated". Actions "Create Ticket", "Create Customer", "Create User". Halo page: "Build custom integrations between Halo and platforms available in Zapier."

51.e: No native Outline integration found (note 5). Route: custom build on the Halo REST API and webhooks, or an external MCP server (see #22). Outline-side API not verified.

52.e: "The HubSpot integration allows you to import customers, contacts, products, quotations and deals from HubSpot into Halo." "For some of these entities a bi-directional sync is available, including: customers, users, products, quotations and deals."

53.e: No native Productive integration found (note 5). Route: custom build on the Halo REST API and webhooks. A Zapier route was not checked. Halo has its own time logging (#46).

54.e: "ServiceNow webhooks allow you to have tickets in Halo create automatically when incidents, change requests, service requests … and problem tickets are raised in ServiceNow." "work notes and additional comments added to the tickets to sync across". "connect your customer's ServiceNow instance to Halo".

55.e: Native Google Calendar: "link agent calendars within Halo to their Google calendar. This allows you to import appointment from Google calendars into Halo." **Missing:** pushing ticket deadlines or tasks from Halo into Google calendars is not documented.

56.e: No native Aboard integration found (note 5). Routes: (a) custom build on the REST API. (b) Google Workspace "New User Onboarding" "allows a ticket to be created when new users are imported for the first time". This works only if new hires appear in Google Workspace; it is not an Aboard event. (c) Third-party Aquera (not marked Native) connects "HCM systems" for "joiner-mover-leaver (JML) workflows". Aboard support not verified.

57.e: "We've added features that will enable you to easily and completely delete all data linked to an individual user. There is functionality for data anonymisation within Halo". Export: "enhancing its data exporting capabilities to enable export even at the individual level". Automation not stated.

58.e: "HALO utilises six AWS regions – London, North Virginia, Frankfurt, Montreal, Cape Town and Sydney." "If Halo hosts your software, it will be on your own dedicated server". **Missing:** per-client regions inside one tenant are not documented, so separate instances would be needed (not confirmed). India is not among the listed regions.

59.e: "You can switch between views regardless of defaults by clicking the current view at the top (currently "Tickets by Team")". Custom lists: "My Lists". Dashboard widgets: "Tickets: This includes the types; List, Calendar, Kanban, and Gannt."

questions: #17: Can audit-log redaction be switched off or locked, so that entries cannot be changed after the fact? Can admins be prevented from setting "Exclude from Audit/Change History"? Are edits of actions (notes and replies) themselves recorded in the audit log?

#23: Can an employee **without an agent licence** raise a ticket from a Slack help channel or a slash command? Do they then receive the agent's replies and status changes **privately in Slack** (DM), with two-way sync? If yes, which app version and which guide?

#27: For a new EU customer, which AWS region hosts the tenant and the backups (Frankfurt?)? Does the GDPR page statement "will be based out of the UK" still apply? Where do the listed sub-processors (AWS, Microsoft, Datadog, NinjaOne …) process EU customer data? Where are unauthenticated chatbot conversations retained by OpenAI for 30 days? Can EU hosting be fixed contractually in the DPA?

Single tool: Can one Halo instance run internal ESM/ITSM desks (IT, People, Finance, Operations) and external client support (Platform, per-client restriction) together? Does the use-case choice in the trial or onboarding limit the configuration?
#10: Which directory sources can fill the "User's Manager" approver besides (Azure) Active Directory? Can a manually maintained manager field be used instead?

#26: Does Halo provide documentation tailored to NIS2 supply-chain assessments (e.g. a NIS2 statement or incident notification terms)? Under what terms (NDA) are the SOC 2 report and the "Security Documentation Package" released?
Pricing: What is the per-agent price with monthly billing, and the price in EUR? What is the typical cost of the required onboarding package for about 11 agents (an assumption)?
No page was blocked.
https://trust.usehalo.com/ returned empty text with tools/pw_text.js. It rendered after a longer wait (same Playwright and proxy, helper script in the scratchpad).
Old guide IDs usehalo.com/guides/1948 and /972 returned 404.
WebSearch was used only to find URLs. No secondary source is used for any verdict.
#28: Can Halo delete tickets and attachments automatically after a set retention period (per ticket type or client)? Where is this configured? Does deletion also cover backups?
#18 / #20: With the Default Halo AI connection, is a vector search database for ticket and article matching included at no extra cost? Or must we connect our own (e.g. Azure AI Search)?

#20 / #22 / #51: Can Halo AI (article creation, matching, conversational agents) use our Notion and Outline knowledge bases as sources without a custom build? For example through the "External MCP Servers" table or an import.
#22 / #51 / #53 / #56: Is there a native or vendor-supported integration with Notion, Outline, Productive or Aboard? Please send the full integrations list (the catalogue page showed only A–F).

#30: Can the end-user Virtual Agent (portal chat and Slack chatbot) return the status of the user's own tickets and point to the right service? Which "Conversational Agent Functions" are available to Virtual Agents?
#31: Can a service catalogue item link to an external system (e.g. expenses in Aboard) instead of raising a Halo ticket?
#32: How do we set up a separately branded portal per client on hosted Halo (self-service or via Halo support)? What is the lead time and cost? Can it reuse existing customer data?
#38: Can a ticket type or service be shown on the portal only to a specific requester group (e.g. managers)? Which setting does this?
#39: Can to-do items or template child tasks carry an owner and a due date (relative to ticket creation, e.g. onboarding day −5)?
#40: Can we restrict one ticket type (e.g. HR) so that only the assigned agent and a named manager see it, while the same agents still see all tickets in other queues?
#45: Can ticket lists or reports filter on custom fields (e.g. a Money field) together with requester and period, without writing SQL?
#47: Can an agent set a dated reminder on a ticket? Is "time waiting since last update" shown in ticket lists?
#49: Can the Google Workspace integration fill the user's manager (for "The Users Manager" approvals)? Or is this only available from (Azure) AD?
#55: Can Halo write ticket deadlines or appointments to agents' Google Calendars (Halo → Google), or only import from Google?
#58: Can one Halo tenant keep a given client's data in a different region (e.g. US, India)? Or would that need a separate instance? Is an India region available?
checks: Re-checked: “£69 per agent, per month (billed annually)”, region GB; “… access portal are always free” (https://www.usehalo.com/pricing).
Re-checked: “Approvers do not require a Halo licence, as they can approve from the end user portal or simply via email” (guide 2396).

Re-checked: the MCP endpoint lets AI assistants "invoke tools in the Halo API such as knowledge search, ticket logging and updating/executing runbooks" (guide 2597). #21 Meets stands: an external agent can act on tickets.
Note from the screen: the integrations catalogue loaded only entries A–F, so "no native integration found" for Notion, Outline, Productive, Aboard and GitHub is not proof of absence.

1.e: "a requester can send an email to a workspace’s support address to create a ticket in that workspace" … "Freshservice keeps all related tickets updated by syncing the requester’s replies across them." The plan grid lists "Channels - Email" and "Custom Mailbox" on all plans.

2.n: client use depends on the ESM/MSP question, note 4
2.p: Starter (grid: "Custom Mailbox" and "Channels - Email" on all plans; number of mailboxes per plan not stated)
2.e: "If you want to create multiple support addresses, click Add mailbox." … "Using Workflow Automator, you can automatically route tickets received in a specific mailbox to various groups or boards." Grid, all plans: Round Robin Ticket Assignment, "Distibute tickets evenly to balance workload among agents" (sic).

3.e: "You can also send an automatic response to your user telling them that you are looking into this issue" … "you can enable the requester email notification for the same."

4.p: Growth (approval steps); Starter for ticket notifications
4.e: Slack/Teams requesters "Get notifiied for tickets created or ticket status changes" (sic). For approvals: "Your action on the service request will be communicated to the requester." A workflow can also "notify the requester when the service request is rejected in any of the stages."

5.e: "Freshservice lets you add private notes to a ticket that are only visible to agents logged in to your service desk."

6.e: "Type the agents you wish to notify on this particular comment in the Notify to field". The plan grid lists "Task Management" on all plans. **Missing:** none of the pages read describes threads or an @mention syntax inside a ticket. Across workspaces: "Agents in a workspace can have conversations on a ticket only with the requester, not with agents in other workspaces … the current option is to assign them a task or a ticket."

7.e: "if a ticket that has been doing the rounds for some time just got reassigned to you, you would like to see everything that has transpired". Activities captured: "Changes to default fields", and the list can be exported ("export the list of activities using the Export button"). Owner changes are in ticket Activities, not in the Enterprise Audit Log (K.O. #17).

8.e: "You might want to create a field called “Waiting for Customer Response”. You can create these additional ticket statuses by clicking on the “Ticket Status” field." Requester-facing labels can differ, and the SLA timer can be switched off per status. **Missing:** none of the pages read states that a workspace or process can have its own list of statuses. Status is a default field ("Category, Subject, Description, Status … cannot be archived or deleted").

9.p: Growth (Business Rules, Service Catalog); basic fields on Starter
9.e: "You can define various field types, such as text, number and date fields, dropdown lists, and checkboxes … designate fields as mandatory or optional". "only the Ticket form fields can be configured at the workspace level." Business Rules for Forms ("Show", "Hide", "Mandate") are Growth+ in the grid.

10.p: Growth (Service Catalog is Growth+; the article's example is a service request)
10.e: "Set the action as Send Approval Mail to Reporting Manager … Set the next action as Send Approval Mail to the Department Head." Email approval: "the approver is required to include additional remarks … when rejecting"; "All the requests handled by email are also captured inside Freshservice".

11.p: Pro (Journeys show the status of each sub-ticket); plan for child tickets not stated
11.e: "Freshservice/FSBT allows you to link any type of ticket as a child ticket to any type of ticket. This capability helps foster cross-functional collaboration between different teams". "Enable the Capture details from the parent ticket checkbox". "Yes, two tickets that are present across workspaces can be linked to each other." Journey panel: "displays key ticket information, including the assigned agent, due date, ticket status, type".

12.e: "They can only view the tickets they raised or shared by other requesters." Department-wide visibility is opt-in per requester ("admin has to additionally enable it on a user level").

13.p: Starter (Workspaces); plan for Restricted Groups not stated
13.e: "Tickets associated with a restricted group are not visible to admins and agents outside that group, even when users have the 'Across all groups in the service desk' access level." Workspaces are on all plans in the grid. Restricted Groups cover "only tickets and data related to tickets".

14.e: Grid, Workflow Automator on all plans: "Automate processes – including multi-approval workflows – with a simple drag-and-drop interface. Use Workflow Execution Logs to monitor automations". An official Zapier app also exists (#50).

15.e: "for each priority level, choose the ticket response time, resolution time". Built-in "First Response SLA Reminder". "For custom pre-breach timings or group alerts, create a Time-based rule in Admin > Workflow Automator".

16.e: "Analytics widgets which include Ticket SLA Metrics, Average Resolution Time, Average First Response Time". The grid lists "Analytics Starter" on all plans and "Team Dashboard" from Pro.

17.e: "Audit Logs record administrative actions, security updates, as well as configuration changes." "Specific module events, including those for Tickets … can be monitored under the respective Activity section." "Freshservice retains audit log data for a duration of 6 months." **Missing:** none of the pages read states that entries cannot be edited. Ticket owner and approval changes are in ticket Activity, not in the Audit Log. Audit Log retention is 6 months.

18.p: Pro + Freddy AI Copilot add-on (USD 29/agent/month billed annually, USD 35 monthly); the grid does not offer Copilot on Starter or Growth
18.e: "Similar Incident Suggester Surface historical tickets with similar context for faster resolution." "Knowledge Content Recommendations Suggests relevant knowledge content when troubleshooting." Pricing: "AI Add-ons Freddy AI Copilot $29/agent/month" (Pro and Enterprise).

19.p: Pro + Freddy AI Copilot add-on (paid, as #18)
19.e: "Freddy AI categorizes incoming tickets into clear, customer-defined categories" … "It then routes tickets to qualified agents matched with skillset requirements and proficiency levels". "Plan availability: Available only on the 'Pro and Enterprise plans with Freddy AI Copilot add-on.'" Copilot also has a "Field Autofill Suggester Recommends field values". Routing between workspaces uses rule-based global workflows.

20.e: "Help Article Generator Creates draft knowledge articles from ticket context." Enterprise Search (Freddy AI Agent, Enterprise only) covers "Google Drive Searches organizational files stored in Google Drive. Confluence Retrieves information from Confluence quickly." **Missing:** Notion and Outline are not among the listed sources. Linking the drafts with the existing scattered knowledge base is not described.

21.e: "The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshservice." Example action: "Update status of the ticket ID 1001 to Resolved (1 action)". Setup options include "Claude Connector (Recommended)", Claude Code and Claude Desktop. "Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available."

22.e: The Notion for Freshservice app lets agents "fetch knowledge base resources from Notion, and utilise those resources as replies within the Freshservice service desk ticket conversations" and "search recommended knowledge base articles (fetched from Notion) based on the Subject details". **Missing:** showing Notion content to requesters or in a client's support space is not described. The article does not name the app's developer or the plans.

23.e: Requesters can "Raise tickets using the bot … Get ticket notifications Get approval notifications View ticket lists" and "Reply to tickets from the notification card." **Missing:** none of the pages read describes requester intake from a help channel or /support command that creates a private requester–agent conversation. Agent side: "Notes & replies from Freshservice to Slack is restricted to 250 characters currently" (2022 article).

24.p: Starter (API "100 API calls/minute"; Growth 200, Pro 400, Enterprise 500)
24.e: "This document provides comprehensive information about the REST APIs available for: Freshservice". Webhooks: "The Workflow Automator can be used to create workflows to trigger a Webhook when a specific Event occurs." Grid, all plans: "Extend functionalities in your service management platform with integrations in the Marketplace".

25.p: Starter (grid: Single Sign-On on all plans; no separate SSO subscription in the grid)
25.e: Grid: "Allow users to access Freshservice via any internal directory like Facebook, X, Google". "All password policies and SSO configurations like Google / OAuth2 / SAML / JWT based Custom SSO can be configured by Organization Admins". "Let users configure TOTP-based two-factor authentication". The same 2021 article lists "Ability to enforce 2FA as a mandatory policy for all admins/agents" under "What’s Coming up Soon?".

26.e: "Explore our ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 27701:2019 certificates, SOC 3 report, subprocessor list, Data Processing Agreement (DPA)". On request: "SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports … Business Continuity Plan, Disaster Recovery Test Summary, and completed SIG and VSA questionnaires." NIS2 is not mentioned on the Trust Center overview.

27.p: All (grid: "Data Center Location" on all plans)
27.e: AWS regions "US, EU, AUS, IND, ME". "The productive product instances and back-up instances are deployed within the same region." "By default, all data for Freddy AI Copilot features is processed and stored within your local data centers" (exceptions are listed for IND, AUS and MEC only). **Missing:** "Personal data subsequently remains in the data center unless, shifted to ensure performance and availability of services". SendGrid (US) is a backup mail provider, which "can be disabled from the backend". AI training needs an email opt-out. None of the pages read names the EU country.

28.p: Not stated (Workflow Automator is on all plans)
28.e: "Using Scheduled Workflow automation can also help delete tickets automatically." … "add the task Delete the Ticket from the drop-down list." Data Archival is not deletion: "Archived tickets will remain accessible to requesters and agents in a read-only format." **Missing:** there is no retention-period setting for tickets and attachments. Whether a deleted ticket is purged permanently, or goes to trash first, is not stated.

29.e: Pricing is "/agent/month". "there is no limit on the number of requesters that can be created" (trial: 100). Approvers: "the approver might not be an agent in the system" and can "respond to the requests directly from their inboxes".

30.p: Enterprise (Freddy AI Agent; "1,200 sessions … per year" per Enterprise licence); bot ticket actions on all plans
30.e: "Freddy AI Agent is available with the Enterprise plan." On Slack it lets "employees to ask questions, raise requests, and receive contextual responses". With the catalog connected, "the agent understands what services are available, guides users to the right ones, and helps them raise requests accurately". ServiceBot on all plans: "View list of tickets and approvals from the Slack home tab."

31.p: Growth (Service Catalog; Starter has no catalog)
31.e: Grid, Service Catalog from Growth: "Make requesting for services easier by setting up a shopping like catalog experience". One catalog spans workspaces: "every service item across every category and workspace in the catalog". **Missing:** a catalog entry that links out to a request handled in another system (for example Aboard) was not verified.

32.p: Growth (MSP mode, Portal Customization); Pro for up to 50 portals
32.e: Grid, MSP mode from Growth: "Create multiple support portals for different clients and manage all client tickets from a single solution using the MSP mode". Support Portal: Starter and Growth "Includes 1 portal", Pro "Includes up to 50 portals". MSP help center: "Each portal can be uniquely customized with separate branding, URL, and knowledge base access restrictions". **Missing:** quick setup from existing data is not described (the HubSpot connector syncs contacts only, #52). MSP mode excludes ESM workspace behaviour (note 4).

33.e: "In Freshservice, notifications can be sent over: Microsoft Teams WhatsApp Push notifications on the Freshservice mobile app Slack Phone SMS Email". "You won't be charged additionally for the notifications … they are a part of your existing plan already i.e. Growth, Pro, & Enterprise."

34.e: "Add agents under the +Add watchers button or select from the options displayed in the dropdown". Watchers "receive email notification every time something happens on the ticket". Activities capture "Add/Remove watchers". Watchers are agents only.

35.e: GitHub app "Published by DevOps integration" (not Freshworks): "support agents can Create, Link, and Notify GitHub issues". The Notion app lets agents "fetch knowledge base content and links from Notion, and attach them as replies". **Missing:** there is no native structured link field for Notion, GitHub or other systems. Route: third-party marketplace app, or a custom app on the API.

36.p: Growth (Business Rules); plan for dependent fields and dynamic sections not stated
36.e: "Dependent fields allow you to nest each item into various levels of categories." Dynamic sections: "This enables the selection of different sets of fields that appear based on user input." Grid, Business Rules from Growth: "Create no-code dynamic ticket forms to perform specific actions based on conditions".

37.e: Fields are added by choosing "the required field type from the Drag & Drop Field options". "only the Ticket form fields can be configured at the workspace level." **Missing:** none of the pages read says that a business team's workspace admin can edit its own forms without account-admin rights.

38.e: "select the required Agent groups and Requester groups who can access the service item." "Other users will not be able to see or access the item."

39.e: "Based on the Journey request configuration, specific activities are automatically assigned to the relevant stakeholders for completion." The panel shows "the agent assigned to the ticket, the due date (automatically syncs with the associated task), ticket status". Grid, Journeys (Pro): "Streamline critical employee transitions such as onboarding, offboarding, relocations, transfers".

40.e: "Tickets associated with a restricted group are not visible to admins and agents outside that group, even when users have the 'Across all groups in the service desk' access level" (K.O. screen). Grid Access Controls: "restrict agent action is specific groups" (sic). **Missing:** restriction is per group. Limiting one ticket to its assignee and a manager, hidden from the rest of the group, is not documented.

41.e: "The bulk upload feature allows you to submit multiple journey requests at once". "All requests in a single upload must belong to the same journey." A CSV template is downloaded and mapped. **Missing:** no CSV import for ordinary tickets was found. Route: journey bulk upload, or a script on the public Tickets API.

42.e: "Freshservice allows you to automatically create recurring tickets at set intervals, providing a way to schedule routine IT tasks like system backups, password resets, or contract renewals". "Create once: Enter the required date and time you want to schedule the ticket." There are Daily, Monthly and Yearly repeat options.

43.p: Starter (1,000 orchestration transactions/account/month included; Growth 2,000, Pro 5,000, Enterprise 20,000)
43.e: Google Sheets orchestration app: "The list of actions supported for this app include: Sheet Management Create Sheet Insert New Row Append New Row". FAQ: "Any action taken via the App node in the Workflow Automator is classified as a transaction". The close event is set as a workflow event (the webhook article gives "Status is Updated" as an example condition).

44.p: Pro (Alert Management); solution hints need the Copilot add-on
44.e: Grid, Alert Management from Pro: "Pipe in alerts from monitoring tools on a single pane of glass, minimize noise, and automate conditional actions". "you can create a condition to trigger an incident when an alert has a P1 tag" (note: "Alert Rules have now been replaced by workflows"). Copilot: "Similar Incident Suggester Surface historical tickets with similar context".

45.e: Views: "filter tickets based on properties such as source, type, status, assigned agent, tags, and custom fields" and "Find tickets from a particular requester." Analytics: "(Optional) Add a Created date filter to limit the results". **Missing:** one view or report that combines requester, date range and a numeric range on a custom field is not shown.

46.e: Grid, Time Tracking from Growth: "Track the amount of time spent by an agent on service desk tasks".

47.p: Not stated (Workflow Automator and Supervisor Rules)
47.e: "For custom pre-breach timings or group alerts, create a Time-based rule in Admin > Workflow Automator" (K.O. screen). "Supervisor runs every hour on tickets updated in the past 30 days." Journeys have "Send Reminder", but only for journey activities. **Missing:** a reminder that an agent sets on a ticket, and a display of how long a ticket has waited, were not found.

48.e: "You can combine multiple filters to further narrow your results. For example, you can: View tickets assigned to a specific agent. Find tickets from a particular requester." An agent sees only the workspaces their role allows (K.O. #13).

49.e: Reporting manager is used in approvals: "Send Approval Mail to Reporting Manager" (K.O. screen). The GSuite orchestration app acts on Google: "User Management Get User Create User Update User Delete User". **Missing:** automatic sync of manager and department from Google Workspace or Aboard into Freshservice is not documented.

50.p: Not stated (API access on all plans)
50.e: Official Zapier app. Triggers include "New Ticket Triggers when there is a new ticket is created in Freshservice" and "Triggers when a Ticket is updated".

51.e: No Outline integration was found on Freshservice pages. The Zapier pair page for Freshservice and Outline returned 404 on 2026-11-18. That Zapier lists an Outline app was seen only in search results, not on a fetched page.

52.e: "The Hubspot CRM Connector app for Freshservice enables you to automatically sync contacts from Hubspot CRM and create requesters in Freshservice." "available for customers with active subscriptions to the Pro and Enterprise plans." **Missing:** syncing company/organization data and setting up a client's support space from HubSpot are not described.

53.e: No native or Freshworks-built integration was found. Zapier: "Connect Freshservice and Productive.io" (pair page "Freshservice Productive.io Integration - Quick Connect - Zapier"). Route: Zapier.

54.p: Pro (Connector Apps; grid "Connector App Tasks" Pro and Enterprise)
54.e: Official ServiceNow Connector: agents can "Create and update tickets between Freshservice and ServiceNow. Map custom fields across both systems." … "Sync conversation notes." **Missing:** connecting several external client ServiceNow instances, one per client, is not described. Other client tools were not checked.

55.e: "From the Google app, users can sync Tasks, Projects tasks, Changes, Releases, Problems & Tickets." "Workload Management has to be enabled in order for Tasks, Problems and Tickets to have planned dates". "all other modules can be synced on the basis of planned dates only". **Missing:** ticket deadlines (due dates) sync only as planned dates. Tasks sync by due date.

56.e: No Aboard integration (native, marketplace or Zapier) was found on any official page read. A custom route would need Aboard's API or webhooks, which were not checked on an Aboard page.

57.e: "Freshservice has built a 'Forget User' option. This would permanently delete user information in the system, as well as tickets/notes/calls that belong to the user." Requesters involved in "Approvals, Change requests" are kept. **Missing:** an export of one person's data (copy for the data subject) is not described. The article dates from 2020.

58.p: Starter (grid: Data Center Location on all plans)
58.e: Grid: "Choose the location of the data centre where you would prefer your data to be hosted". **Missing:** a region choice per client or per workspace inside one account is not described. Per-client regions would therefore need separate accounts (not verified with the vendor).

59.e: "You can display filtered tickets in either List or Board view." Default view "New & My Open Tickets Open tickets assigned to you and all unassigned tickets". Views can be shared with agents and used in dashboard widgets. Grid "Team Dashboard" from Pro.

questions: Single-tool question (Freshservice). Question: "May external B2B clients be requesters in a Freshservice account in Employee Support (ESM) mode, with a Platform workspace beside IT, People, Finance and Operations workspaces? Is that allowed under the licence terms, with no requester fees?"
Freshservice #13 detail. Question: "Which plans include Restricted Groups? Can one restricted group per client limit Platform agents to their assigned clients' tickets?"

Freshservice licences. Question: "Can People, Finance and Operations agents work in business workspaces on Starter or Growth with standard agent seats, or is Pro + Business Agent licence (or FSBT) required?"
#17, both products. Question: "Can Audit Log or ticket Activity entries be edited or deleted by anyone, including admins? Can the 6-month Audit Log retention in Freshservice be extended?"
Freshservice #23. Question: "Do agent public replies reach the requester in Slack in full? Can requesters raise a private ticket from a shared help channel or a slash command?"
#26. Question: "Do you provide NIS2-specific supply-chain documentation or contract clauses (incident notification times, Art. 21 measures)?"

#27. Question: "In which EU country are EU-region accounts hosted? Can all US-only sub-processors (e.g. SendGrid backup mail) be disabled for an EU account? Under what conditions is data 'shifted' out of the region?"
#8: "Can each workspace (IT, People, Finance, Operations, Platform) have its own set of ticket statuses, or is the Status list shared by the whole account?"
#20: "Can Copilot's Help Article Generator and Knowledge Content Recommendations, or Enterprise Search, use Notion and Outline as sources? On which plan?"
#22: "Can content from the Notion for Freshservice app be shown to requesters in the support portal (per client)? Who develops the app, and on which plans is it available?"
#25: "Can 2FA be enforced as mandatory for all agents today? (The 2021 Freshworks Organization article lists it as 'coming up soon'.)"

#28: "Is there a retention setting that permanently deletes tickets and attachments after N days? Does 'Delete the Ticket' in a Scheduled Workflow purge the ticket permanently, or move it to trash, and when is trash emptied?"
#31: "Can a service catalog item link out to a request handled in another system (for example Aboard) instead of creating a ticket?"
#32: "In ESM mode, can we run a separately branded portal per client (Pro: up to 50 portals) next to the internal workspaces? Can client portals be pre-filled from HubSpot company data?"
#37: "Can a workspace admin of a business workspace (for example People) create and edit that workspace's ticket forms and catalog items without account-admin rights?"
#40: "Can a single ticket be restricted to its assignee and a named manager, hidden from other agents in the same group or workspace?"
#41: "Is there a self-service CSV import that creates ordinary tickets, not only journey requests?"
#45: "Can one ticket view or report filter by requester, a created-date range and a numeric custom-field range at the same time?"
#47: "Can an agent set a personal reminder on a ticket? Is the waiting time of a ticket shown in the ticket list?"
#49: "Is there a Google Workspace (or SCIM) user sync that fills Reporting Manager and Department automatically?"
#51: "Is there any Outline integration (marketplace app or Zapier)?"
#52: "Can the HubSpot CRM Connector sync companies, not only contacts, and map them to client portals or departments?"
#54: "Can the ServiceNow Connector connect several external client ServiceNow instances at the same time, one per client?"
#55: "Can a ticket's due date (not only its planned dates) appear in Google Calendar?"
#56: "Is there any Aboard integration? Which inbound route (API or email) is recommended for Aboard hire and leaver events?"
#57: "Can an admin export all data about one requester (tickets, notes, assets) as a copy for a data subject request?"
#58: "Can different clients' data be stored in different regions inside one account, or does each region need a separate account?"
#30: "What does an extra pack of Freddy AI Agent (Classic) sessions cost on Enterprise?"
AI licensing: "Must Freddy AI Copilot be bought for every agent on the plan, or only for selected agents?"
Pricing: "What is the Enterprise price per agent in EUR for about 11 agents (an assumption), billed annually?"
checks: Re-checked: the only Freshdesk “Approval workflow” is for knowledge-base content (pricing page data).
Re-checked: Freshservice “Send Approval Mail to Reporting Manager” (hierarchical approvals article).
Re-checked: Freshservice accounts in “Managed Services (MSP)” mode have different rules (multiple requester portals article).

Corrected Freshdesk #29 from “Meets” to “Unknown” under the uniform #29 rule in analysis/01_ko_criteria.md: the pricing page (including collapsed FAQ text) has no explicit statement that contacts are free or unlimited.

Re-checked: "The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshservice" and the example "Update status of the ticket ID 1001 to Resolved" (MCP article). #21 Meets stands.
#25 kept as Meets: the requirement asks for SSO and 2FA, not for enforced 2FA; same treatment as Freshdesk #25.

1.e: “Your customers can send requests by email if your service space is set up for it. They can also track requests through email notifications.” Customers can “Create and comment on requests via email”.

2.n: Each client can get its own service space and address (up to 10 addresses per space, each mapped to a request type); agents pick up work from queues.
2.e: "A service project can have up to 10 email addresses connected to it." / "set up different service spaces for each one of them" / "Queues allow requests to be easily managed by your team."

3.p: Free. Templates can't be edited on Free.
3.e: “Request created: When customers create requests in the portal or send an email to your email channel, your service space sends a confirmation that their request was received.”

4.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; notice at each approval step is inferred, not documented
4.e: “Customer-visible status changed: When a request transitions to a status that is visible to the customer, your service space notifies the customers involved.” Approvals: “the person who submitted the request is notified of any comments that the approver added.” Note: a notice at each approval step follows from these two documented behaviours (approval steps sit on workflow statuses). No single page states it.

5.e: “You can also add internal notes (the customer cannot see these)”

6.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets (2 items not verified)"; @mentions and threads not verified
6.e: “add internal notes … to get help from other members of your team”. “A work item can have subtasks that can be assigned and tracked individually.” History: “when someone edits a field, moves the work item through its workflow”. @mentions and threaded comments not verified on an official page.

7.n: Assignee changes are field edits and appear in work item history. Audit-log limits (no tamper-proof evidence, user-activity log Enterprise only) are covered in K.O. #17.
7.e: "Work item assigned ... The flow will run when the Assignee of a work item is changed." / "History: Updates on a work item, like when someone edits a field, moves the work item through its workflow"

8.n: Each request type has its own workflow; admins can create their own statuses and rename them for customers.
8.e: "The flow of a request is determined by the workflow associated with a request type." / "you can edit or remove them from a workflow to suit your team's need. You can also create your own."

9.e: “Create forms that use conditional logic to dynamically show or hide fields … Use forms on request types”. Supported field types include “Date Picker” and “Select list (single or multiple choices)”. Required fields exist: “If you have a required field in a request type…”. CSM: per customer group “Forms – the request forms customers use”.

10.p: **Unclear: Free or Premium.** The pricing table ticks “Approvals” (Change Management section) only for Premium and Enterprise. The help doc for approval steps states no plan.
10.e: “You can add an approval step to any status in any request type’s workflow.” “Leave requests may need to be approved by an employee’s direct manager.” The approver source is a “user picker (multiple users) or group picker” field. The manager must be put into that field. Automatic manager lookup was not verified.

11.n: Agents create linked work items in another space; links work across spaces and show each linked item's status; automation can create and link items in any space.
11.e: "Select + Create linked work item. Select the space you want to link to" / "You can link work items across different spaces in Jira" / "You'll see the link type, work item key, summary, and status for each linked work item."

12.e: Customer role: “Raise requests, comment on their own requests”. Sharing setting: “Customers can share requests with their organization, or raise a private request.”

13.p: Free for separate spaces. Plan for security levels not stated.
13.e: “You can also control work item level security to restrict a work item to select members of your team.” CSM role: “View and work on all work items in their space”. Atlassian KB on using security levels plus automation calls this a way to “get around this limitation”.

14.n: Native rule engine with triggers, conditions and actions. Official Zapier app exists (#50).
14.p: Free (1,250 steps per subscription/month); Standard 3,000 steps per user/month
14.e: "1,250 automation steps per subscription per month" (Free) / "Apply conditions directly to the trigger to add criteria to the entire flow."

15.p: Free (“queues and SLAs”; 1,250 automation steps per month)
15.e: “High priority: 2 hour target / Medium priority: 4 hour target …” Trigger “SLA threshold breached”: “The flow will run when a Jira Service Management SLA has breached or is about to breach. … You can select the SLA to monitor, and the time before or after it has breached to trigger.”

16.e: “default reports … measure common service space functions such as workload, satisfaction, and requests deflected or resolved”. Agents can “View the portal, queues, reports, and SLA metrics”.

17.e: Work item history: “Updates on a work item, like when someone edits a field, moves the work item through its workflow”. Audit log: “isn't available if all of your Jira Cloud apps are on the Free plan”. Also: “The audit log isn't intended to record all activity in Jira.” **Missing:** no evidence that entries are tamper-proof (“cannot be edited retroactively”). The comprehensive “Audit logs - user activity” is Enterprise only.

18.n: Rovo agent Service Request Helper finds similar past requests and suggests resolution steps, using Atlassian and connected third-party knowledge. Included in the plan (consumes Rovo credits: Standard 250 per user/month); no separate price.
18.e: "Service Request Helper gathers context from past and ongoing similar requests in your space and suggests steps" / "Designed to use both Atlassian apps and connected third-party apps as knowledge sources" / tool "Find similar work items"

19.n: Rovo agent Request Router suggests request type and priority and can run inside automation rules. Included in the plan (Rovo credits).
19.e: "The Request Router agent reads request details and sentiment to recommend the right request type, urgency, and priority, then routes each request to the correct queue or assignee." / "this agent can be used within automation rules, so you can automate triage and field updates"

20.n: Rovo drafts KB articles from resolved tickets and finds KB gaps. Missing: drafts are published to Confluence; connecting them with the existing Notion or Outline knowledge is not documented (named third-party KB sources: Google Drive, SharePoint). Included in the plan (Rovo credits).
20.e: "Agents can convert the resolution steps provided by agents on tickets to Knowledge Base articles." / "analyzes the primary issue and up to 10 similar closed issues from the last 180 days" / "Select Yes when asked if you want to create a Confluence document."

21.n: Vendor-provided MCP server (v2) lists Claude as a client and covers JSM; it can create and update work items. OAuth 2.1 or API token.
21.p: Not stated (some search/context tool calls consume Rovo credits)
21.e: "Atlassian MCP supports any app with MCP support, including: OpenAI ChatGPT Claude" / "Summarize and search Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence" / "Create and update work items or pages using natural language commands."

22.n: Official Atlassian Rovo connector indexes Notion pages for Rovo search, chat and agents (internal use). Missing: Notion is not documented as a JSM knowledge-base source shown in the help center or used by the virtual service agent (named sources: Confluence, Google Drive, SharePoint).
22.e: "Make Notion pages searchable alongside your company knowledge." / "Indexed objects Pages" / KB sources: "A third-party folder, such as a Google Drive or SharePoint folder"

23.p: Free (“submit requests via email, Microsoft Teams and Slack”)
23.e: “When someone sends a message in a request channel, agents can create a work item by: Reacting with a ticket emoji (:ticket:)”. “comments and actions in Slack or Teams immediately sync with the work item, and vice versa.” **Missing:** intake is a shared request channel. No evidence of a private requester–agent ticket or a /support command. Approvers do get a DM.

24.n: REST APIs, webhooks per event type with JQL filters, Marketplace.
24.e: "Rich APIs and 1,000+ Marketplace apps enable you to customize your service experience." / "Issue webhooks created (jira:issue_created) updated (jira:issue_updated) deleted (jira:issue_deleted) JQL filtering supported."

25.n: with Atlassian Guard Standard. SAML SSO with Google Workspace and enforced two-step verification need a separate Guard Standard subscription on Free, Standard and Premium ($4.35 per user/month as displayed); included in Enterprise.
25.p: Any plan + Guard Standard; Enterprise includes it
25.e: "To enforce single sign-on with Google Workspace: Go to Atlassian Administration." / "You can enable SAML single sign-on and other enhanced security features (like enforced 2-step verification, password policies, and user provisioning) with a subscription to Atlassian Guard" / Standard: "Requires Atlassian Guard Standard subscription"

26.n: reviewer correction: was "Partial"; uniform #26 rule; CSM not in ISO scope remains a note
26.e: The Compliance Resource Center lists “ISO/IEC27001:2022”, “SOC 2”, “GDPR”, “DORA”, “C5” and “ENISA”. The ISO page lists “Jira Service Management” under Relevant products. The site offers “pre-filled vendor security assessment questionnaires”. **Missing:** no NIS2 entry in the Compliance Resource Center list. CSM is not listed under ISO 27001 Relevant products.

27.p: Standard (data residency ticked for Standard, Premium and Enterprise)
27.e: “EU Consists of Europe (Frankfurt) and Europe (Dublin) regions”. Backups follow the pinned region for backups created after 28.04.2026. **Missing:** JSM “Customer accounts” are in the “Can’t be pinned” column. Also not pinnable: “App, audit, and operational logs”, “Data in transit (up to 30 days)” and “Cached content, such as emails and notifications”. CSM has no row in the table. For AI, only storage is covered: “all of your in-scope app data will remain stored in the region you've selected”. Rovo uses third-party LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), and no EU processing location is stated.

28.n: Deletion can be scheduled with automation (scheduled trigger + JQL + "Delete attachments" or "Delete work item"). Missing: no built-in retention-period setting for work items and attachments was found; a fixed automatic deletion is documented only for alert data.
28.e: "As the Trigger, choose the Scheduled option." / "Choose the ACTION in this case, Delete Attachments." / "Delete work item ... Deletes the current work item that is in context."

29.e: “Customers are free and don’t require a Service Collection license.” “Approvers don't need a Jira Service Management license to approve requests – they just have to be customers of the service space.”

30.n: Virtual service agent answers from the KB, links the right request form and creates a request; channels include Slack, Teams and the help center. Missing: checking the status of an existing request is not documented. Premium includes 1,000 assisted conversations/month; above that from $0.30 (USD) each.
30.e: "search your linked knowledge base" / "a link to a related request form (if one is found)" / "offers to create an issue for a human agent to resolve" / "Deliver contextual support directly in Slack, Microsoft Teams, and the help center"

31.n: One help center shows the request forms of linked spaces; up to 10 external links per space point to forms in other systems.
31.e: "Linked spaces show their request forms, knowledge base articles and other resources in the help center." / "if your HR team uses a different tool to receive requests, you could add a link to request forms that live in this request management system."

32.n: A branded portal per client space is documented; separate help centers (up to 300) need Premium. Missing: quick set-up that reuses existing data (for example from HubSpot) is not native; only via API/CSV import (see #52).
32.p: Free/Standard (portal per space; custom URL on Standard); Premium (multiple help centers)
32.e: "Brand your portal to suit your organization's and client's needs." / "This feature is only available for users on Jira Service Management Premium and Enterprise plans." / "you can create up to 300 help centers per site"

33.n: On-call schedules, escalations, SMS, voice and mobile push are built in.
33.p: Free (200 SMS/month); Standard (unlimited SMS and voice)
33.e: Free: "Unlimited alerts, unlimited alert email notifications, and 200 SMS per month"; Standard: "Unlimited alerts, unlimited alert email notifications, SMS, and voice" / "notifies via email, text messages (SMS), phone calls, and iOS & Android push notifications"

34.n: Watchers (licensed users) and request participants (customers) can be added and removed; automation can add or remove watchers. Note: participants see public comments only.
34.e: Participants: "How they are removed Only by a user with edit work item permissions"; watchers added "By any user with the Manage Watchers permission" / "Add or remove watchers on a work item."

35.n: Links to other work items, web pages, Confluence pages and "app content" are documented. Missing: structured Notion and GitHub links were not verified on an official page.
35.e: "Add context to work items by linking them to each other, or by adding links to web pages, Confluence pages, or app content."

36.n: (visibility). Form sections show or hide based on an earlier answer. Note: conditions apply to sections, and the controlling field must be radio, checkbox or dropdown; options that change with a previous field were not verified.
36.e: "You can use conditional logic to show or hide a section based on what someone selects earlier in the form." / "The field types must be radio, checkbox, or dropdown."

37.n: Drag-and-drop form builder. Note: the business-team member needs the space-admin role in their own space.
37.e: "Drag and drop extra fields from the right panel." / "To create or edit forms, you'll need admin or space admin permissions."

38.n: Request types can be restricted to users, groups, customer accounts or organizations (max 50 per type). Caveat: restricted types do not work in email, chat, widget or the virtual agent.
38.e: "These could be requests reserved for managers" / "You can restrict request types by users, groups, customer accounts and customer organizations." / "except in email, chat, widget, and the virtual agent"

39.n: Automation can create sub-tasks or work items with set fields (owner, due date) for onboarding/offboarding. Missing: no native checklist on a work item was found; checklists appear only via Marketplace apps (not verified).
39.e: "Create sub-tasks ... Creates sub-tasks on a work item." / "Creates a work item of any type in a space. You can select fields to configure and set their values."

40.n: Work item security levels restrict who can view a work item.
40.e: "To set the security level of individual work items in Jira Service Management, upgrade to the Standard, Premium or Enterprise plan." / "To add permissions around who can view work items, you'll need to set up work item security levels."

41.n: CSV importer; non-admins up to 250 items per file.
41.e: "It also allows you to create your own CSV file to perform bulk work item creation and updates." / "Users without administrator permissions will be able to import 250 work items per CSV file."

42.n: Scheduled automation trigger (fixed rate, cron, optional JQL) plus "Create work item".
42.e: "This flow runs on a specified schedule. You can run the flow at a fixed rate (for example, every 7 days), or use a Cron expression" / "Creates a work item of any type in a space."

43.n: Route: automation "Work item transitioned" + "Send web request" to a custom endpoint, or Zapier. Missing: no native spreadsheet (Google Sheets) action in the automation action list.
43.e: "The flow will run when a work item transitions from one status to another." / "Sends an outgoing web request to notify another system when a flow is run."

44.n: Native monitoring integrations create alerts; an Operations automation template turns alerts into linked incidents; AIOps adds related resources and incident suggestions. Plan for the alert-to-incident rule not stated.
44.e: "Connect ChatOps tools and hundreds of third-party monitoring integrations." / "Select the template named "When an alert is created → Create an incident"." / AIOps Standard: "Related resources, similar alerts, incident suggestions panel"

45.n: JQL filters on reporter, created date and custom fields (for example an amount field).
45.e: "Reporter Search for work items that were reported by a particular user." / "Created Search for work items that were created on, before, or after a particular date (or date range)." / "Search for work items where a particular custom field has a particular value."

46.n: Native time logging, separate from SLAs; admins enable it site-wide.
46.e: "You can use the time tracking feature in addition to SLAs" / "The Logged field displays the amount of time logged working on the work item so far"

47.n: SLA timers and the "SLA threshold breached" trigger alert before or after a breach; scheduled JQL rules can flag stale tickets. Missing: a reminder set on an individual ticket was not found on an official page.
47.e: "The flow will run when a Jira Service Management SLA has breached or is about to breach." / "You can select the SLA to monitor, and the time before or after it has breached to trigger."

48.n: JQL search by reporter across spaces. CSM adds a customer context view.
48.e: "Reporter Search for work items that were reported by a particular user." / CSM: "Customer context One place to access all relevant information about organizations and customers."

49.n: Route: Assets employee objects with a Manager attribute plus an automation rule that sets the reporter's manager as approver (Atlassian blog, 2020, uses the old name "Insight"). Missing: the data must be imported (CSV, JSON) or entered manually; no native sync from Google Workspace or Aboard documented.
49.e: "we want the approver for the laptop requests to be automatically set as the reporter's manager" / "This can be done by importing data with LDAP (Data Center only), CSV, or JSON files, or by entering it manually."

50.n: Official Zapier app for Jira Service Management.
50.e: "Jira Service Management Integrations" / "Create Jira Service Management requests for new Jotform submissions"

51.n: Route: Zapier or Make (Outline lists both, plus webhooks) combined with the JSM Zapier app. Outline's integrations page lists no Jira integration.
51.e: Outline integrations: "Developers GitHub GitLab Linear Webhooks Zapier Make"

52.n: (CSM). Route: custom build on CSM bulk APIs following Atlassian's HubSpot import guide (contacts to customers, companies to organizations). No native HubSpot connector found.
52.e: "This guide helps you import, update and keep in sync your customer and organization data from HubSpot to Atlassian Customer Service Management (CSM). Using our bulk APIs"

53.n: Official free app built by Productive for Jira Cloud time tracking. Missing: JSM service spaces are not named on the listing.
53.e: "Built by Productive" / "works with Jira Cloud" / "A simple and efficient way to integrate time tracking on projects in Jira"

54.n: Official ServiceNow app syncs ServiceNow incidents to JSM alerts (not service requests); bidirectional needs Premium. Other client tools: email channel only (K.O. #1); ticket-to-ticket sync via Marketplace apps not verified.
54.e: "When an incident is created in ServiceNow, an alert is created in Jira Service Management." / "The following capabilities are available in Jira Service Management Premium and Enterprise: Bidirectional integrations"

55.n: Route: Zapier (Google Calendar is listed among popular JSM integrations on Zapier). No official Atlassian calendar sync for ticket due dates found.
55.e: Zapier page lists "Google Calendar" under "Popular Jira Service Management Integrations"

56.n: Route: custom build: an Aboard event would call the JSM automation "Incoming webhook" trigger (or the REST API). No Aboard integration found; whether Aboard can send such events was not checked.
56.e: "The flow will run when a HTTP POST is sent to a specified webhook URL. A webhook is a way for a third-party to trigger an automation flow."

57.n: Admins can permanently delete a portal-only customer (all plans). Missing: exporting a copy of a person's data and erasing their data inside work items (comments, fields) are not documented on the pages checked; deletion is manual per customer.
57.e: "When you delete a customer, they won't be able to log in to your Jira Service Management help centers" / "Atlassian Cloud: Jira Service Management (all plans)"

58.n: Regions include USA and India. Residency is set per app; no per-space or per-client region is documented, so a different region per client would need separate sites (multiple sites only on Enterprise, up to 150).
58.e: "India Consists of Asia Pacific (Mumbai) regions" / "USA Consists of US East (North Virginia) and US West (Oregon) regions." / Sites: "Enterprise Multiple, up to 150"

59.n: Team queues (default or custom); personal views via JQL with currentUser().
59.e: "Your teams will spend the majority of their time working out of queues. Use the default service project queues or set up your own." / assignee field "supports: currentUser()"

questions: #6: Are @mentions and threaded replies available in internal notes on JSM work items? (No official page confirming either was opened.)

#10: Are workflow approval steps (outside Change Management) available on Standard, or only on Premium? Can the requester's manager be filled in as approver automatically (for example from a directory or HR source)? Where is each approval decision (who, when, comment) logged?
#13: Which plans include work item security levels in JSM and CSM spaces?

#17: Can work item history or audit log entries be edited or deleted by any role (including admins)? What is the retention period? What does the Standard audit log record compared with Enterprise “user activity”?

#23: Can an employee raise a private ticket from Slack (DM to Assist or a slash command) visible only to them and the agents? The docs conflict on Slack workspaces: “Each Jira site can connect to multiple Slack workspaces” (What is chat?) vs “A Jira site can only connect to one Slack workspace” (Receive requests in Slack). Which is current?
#26: Does Atlassian provide NIS2-specific supply-chain documentation? Is CSM within the ISO 27001 / SOC 2 certification scope?

#27: Where are JSM “Customer accounts” (customer emails and names) stored when pinned to the EU? Where are Rovo, virtual service agent and CSM AI agent prompts processed? Can AI processing be limited to the EU? Does CSM data follow the JSM EU pin?
#29: Do internal collaborators (Service Desk Team role) need any paid Jira licence?
Pricing: what are the prices in EUR for an EU billing address?

#20: Can Rovo-generated KB articles be linked to or published in a non-Confluence knowledge base (Notion, Outline)? Does the JSM knowledge base in Service Collection need a separate Confluence licence?
#21: Which Service Collection plans (incl. Free) can use the Atlassian MCP server, and which JSM tools (requests, queues, comments, transitions) does v2 expose?

#22: Can Notion (via the Rovo Notion connector) be linked as a JSM knowledge source shown in the help center and used by the virtual service agent? Does the Notion connector require a Confluence licence?
#25: Is Guard Standard billed only for agents, or for every managed account (incl. employees who are portal customers)? What is the EUR price?
#28: Is there a native retention policy for JSM work items and attachments (delete after N days), or is automation the only route? After automated deletion, when is the data purged from backups?
#30: Can the virtual service agent or a Rovo help-center agent report the status of an existing request (help center, Slack)? Can a Rovo agent in the help center be used on Standard?
#32: Can per-client branded help centers be created on Standard? Is there a way to create a client space from existing CRM data without a custom API job?
#35: Are Smart Links / structured links to Notion pages and GitHub pull requests supported in JSM service spaces? Does "GitHub for Jira" work in JSM spaces?
#39: Is there a native checklist field or checklist template for JSM work items in Cloud?
#43: Is there a native automation action that writes a row to Google Sheets (or another register)?
#44: Which plan includes the Operations automation rule "When an alert is created → Create an incident"?
#47: Is there a native per-ticket reminder ("remind me on date X") in JSM Cloud?
#49: Can the requester's manager be synced automatically from Google Workspace or an HRIS into user profiles or Assets (no CSV/JSON import), e.g. via Assets Data Manager?
#52: Is there (or is planned) an official HubSpot connector for CSM customer and organization profiles?
#53: Does Productive's Jira Cloud app work in JSM service spaces?
#54: Can ServiceNow incidents create JSM service requests (not alerts), and on which plan?
#55: Is there an official calendar feed or Google Calendar sync for ticket due dates?
#57: Is there a tool to export all personal data of one person (access request) and to erase it from work item content (comments, fields, attachments), not only delete the account?
#58: Can service spaces on one site use different data residency regions, or does each region need a separate site (Enterprise multiple sites)?
checks: Re-checked: “Customers are free and don’t require a Service Collection license” and “Each Service Collection user license covers both JSM and CSM” (pricing page FAQ).
Re-checked: “Approvers don't need a Jira Service Management license to approve requests” (approvals doc).
Corrected #4 and #6 from “Meets” to “Partial”, for consistency with the other screens: a part of the requirement that is not documented or not verified gives “Partial”, not “Meets”.

Corrected #26 from “Partial” to “Meets” under the uniform #26 rule in analysis/01_ko_criteria.md (ISO 27001 and SOC 2 confirmed; NIS2 is an open question for all vendors). If client support moves to CSM, the CSM ISO scope still has to be confirmed.

Re-checked: "Summarize and search Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence" and "Create and update work items or pages using natural language commands" (Atlassian remote MCP server). #21 Meets stands.
#25 kept as Meets: SSO with Google Workspace and 2FA exist; the separate Guard Standard cost is recorded in the row and in the add-on list.

1.e: "If you are just starting out with email-based customer support, the Support plan is a great place to begin." Plan lists "Email and ticketing system".

2.p: Support Team (addresses, "Ticket routing"); Suite Team ("Omnichannel routing")
2.e: "You can manage up to 3,000 support addresses, use them with multibrand setups, and apply business rules, views, and SLA policies based on the address received." The pricing page lists Support Team "Ticket routing" and Suite Team "Omnichannel routing".

3.e: Standard trigger "Notify requester and CCs of received request: Notifies the requester … that their request has been received and has become a ticket."

4.e: "When an agent or end user adds a comment to the ticket, the requester and CCs are notified via email." **Missing:** none of the standard triggers notifies the requester of a status change. For approvals, only "The ticket assignee receives email notifications for all responses to approval requests." Whether custom triggers can notify the requester of each approval step was not verified.

5.e: Agents can "Add public or private comments or both to tickets". End users' "ticket comments can never be private".

6.e: "Side conversations are spaces in a ticket where agents can have a side conversation with a specific group of people". Plan line: "Customer Service Suite Professional, Enterprise". Light agents "can read tickets and provide input by adding private comments". **Missing or unverified:** @mentions were not verified. "Tasks" is listed as an Employee Service Suite addition, and was not verified for CS.

7.p: Support Team (assignment); ticket audit plan not stated
7.e: "Tickets assigned to me ...a ticket is assigned to you." A recipe runs "when a ticket is reassigned and invites the previous asignee and new assignee". History: "Audits are a read-only history of all updates to a ticket."
