8.p: Support Team (custom statuses); Suite Growth (HC) for statuses per form, i.e. Suite Professional on the pricing page
8.e: "Create custom ticket statuses to give agents and end users clearer, business-specific descriptions of ticket progress." "Form ticket statuses let you choose which standard and custom statuses appear on each ticket form".

9.p: Suite Growth per help center; Suite Professional is the lowest plan on the pricing page
9.e: Multiple forms: plan "All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise". "Custom ticket fields can be required or optional." Drop-down "Field values … for each option". **Limits:** "You cannot make the same field required on one form but optional on another form" (conditional fields are the workaround). Forms can be limited per brand, but per-client (organization) forms are not documented. A date field type was not verified.

10.p: Conflicting: help center header says CS Suite Growth; help center body says "Customer Service Suite Professional plans and above"; pricing page lists "Approval workflows" under Suite Enterprise
10.e: "If … multiple approvals … must be done sequentially, you must create a separate approval request for each approver, one after the other." Decisions "are tracked in the approval request on the ticket and in the ticket events". **Missing:** no native sequential chain (manual, or "action flows"). No evidence that the requester's manager is resolved automatically. "End user-approvers must respond to requests from the help center" (not Slack).

11.e: Side conversation child tickets: "the status and assignee of the child ticket is displayed on the side conversation in the parent ticket". Fields can be copied at creation. **Limited:** "Generally, there isn't a reverse connection between parent and child tickets". A private comment on the child "won't appear in the side conversation interface of the parent ticket", and parent status changes do not carry over. Automatic creation of a child ticket by a rule (e.g. onboarding creates an IT ticket) was not verified.

12.e: End users "can only submit and track tickets". Seeing others' tickets is opt-in: "Allow users within an organization to see all the tickets in their organization, referred to as a shared organization". Visibility of tickets where the user is only CC'd was not verified.

13.e: "When a group is private, only agents from that group can view tickets assigned to it." Plan line: "All Suites Enterprise or Enterprise Plus". On lower plans, "Access to Tickets in agent's groups" exists, but it "is not completely secure … Each admin has access to data from all groups."

14.e: The Support Team plan lists "Automations and triggers". "All Suite plans include powerful automations". Zapier is the complement (#50).

15.p: Suite Growth per help center; Suite Professional is the lowest plan on the pricing page
15.e: "Enter a time target for each ticket priority." "You can also create business rules that take action based on SLAs (for example, to get attention on a ticket before the SLA is breached)." Plan line: "All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise". Group (internal team) SLAs are Enterprise only.

16.e: The plan lists "Prebuilt analytics dashboards" and "out-of-the-box analytics to help you analyze trends in ticket volume and agent performance". **Note:** "Only agents with access to all tickets in your Zendesk account will be able to view reports" (relevant together with #13).

17.p: Ticket audits: plan not stated. Account audit log: Suite Enterprise
17.e: "Audits are a read-only history of all updates to a ticket." Approval decisions are logged "in the ticket events". The account-level audit log is only for "customers on Enterprise plans", and "End user activities are not captured."

18.p: Suite Professional + Copilot add-on (USD 50/agent/month, paid yearly); included in Suite Enterprise + Copilot
18.e: "Auto assist uses a large language model (LLM) to understand the contents of submitted tickets and make suggestions to your agents on how to solve them." "Similar tickets helps agents find recently solved or closed tickets about the same issue". Suggested first replies are "based on existing macros and help center articles". Copilot: "available as an add-on for Suite and Support Professional and above plans".

19.p: Suite Professional + Copilot add-on (USD 50); included in Suite Enterprise + Copilot
19.e: "Intelligent triage uses AI to classify incoming tickets by topic, sentiment, language, and custom entities, so you can route requests to the right team". It "Powers automated routing workflows that send incoming requests to the appropriate agent the first time." The pricing page lists "Intelligent Triage" under Suite Enterprise + Copilot.

20.p: Knowledge builder: rolled out "to all our customers" (no plan line on the page)
20.e: It "analyzes your ticket data from the last 90 days to pinpoint the most common customer issues" and creates "up to 40 proposed articles" as drafts. **Missing:** it is aimed at accounts with no help center or "an outdated help center that you want to refresh" and generates a new one. Writing articles from individual resolved tickets into the existing KB, and linking them with Notion or Confluence content, was not verified. Knowledge copilot is EAP and was not read.

21.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets (early access only)"; the feature exists but only in an early access program, not generally available, and pricing may change
21.p: All Suites from Team (HC plan line); "available without charge" during the EAP
21.e: "Zendesk Bridge provides a way to establish governed connections between Zendesk and external AI agents your organization uses, including Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, or AI agents you build yourself." The agent "can perform Zendesk actions, such as creating and updating tickets". "During the early access program, destructive actions, bulk exports, and changes to admin settings aren't available." Separately, the "Zendesk MCP Server" was announced on 2026-05-19 for "Early access this summer".

22.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; showing Notion content in a client's own support space was not verified; same rule as Freshservice #22
22.p: Suite Team ("any Zendesk Suite or Knowledge plan")
22.e: "You can now connect Notion to your Zendesk account to make the content available for help center search, generative search, AI agents Essentials, and Agent Workspace." "You can create a Notion connection on any Zendesk Suite or Knowledge plan." **Limits:** "you can set up only a single Notion connection". Restricting Notion content to one client's (brand's) help center was not verified.

23.p: Support Team / Suite Team (integration); Suite Team (Slack DM channel)
23.e: "Create new tickets directly from Slack … designed to cater to an internal use case". Slack notifications only "If your Zendesk administrator has configured triggers for Slack". For requester-side two-way chat, the Slack DM channel: "intended to support 1:1 requests", and "replying within a thread in the direct message will not come over to Zendesk." **Missing:** no documented flow where a help channel or /support command opens a private ticket conversation with replies and statuses synced both ways. The shortcut is "/zendesk".

24.e: Webhooks "send HTTP requests to third-party systems based on ticket, user, or other Zendesk events … Connect webhooks to triggers, automations, or subscribe to events". Event domains: "Article … Organization … User … Agent availability … Ticket … Messaging … Access log events". For ticket activity, "connect the webhook to a trigger or automation instead". "Prebuilt integrations: Available through the Zendesk Marketplace". The API reference covers "ticketing, help center, live chat, voice, sales CRM". The Marketplace site itself was blocked.

25.p: Support Team / Suite Team. No separate SSO subscription found
25.e: The SAML plan line is "All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus". "Enable SAML single sign-on … set up access for team members, end users, or both." 2FA: "Require two-factor authentication for team members, end users, or both" (all Suites). Zendesk 2FA "isn't available for users who sign in through third-party authentication such as Google, JWT, or SAML". Those users can use "Google 2-Step Verification, if you're using Google authentication".

26.e: "Zendesk is ISO 27001:2022 certified." SOC 2 Type II reports are "available upon request and under NDA". Also ISO 27017, 27018, 27701 and 42001. The DPA "incorporates the new EU Standard Contractual Clauses". The Trust Portal has "certifications, audit reports, policy documents, and standardized security questionnaires". No NIS2-specific statement was found.

27.e: "The Data Center Location add-on is available and free of charge for Zendesk Suite Professional or higher plans, but it is not automatically activated." Hosting includes "archival, backup, and logging purposes". **Missing:** below Professional, Zendesk "may move the account data … between regions without notice". The add-on "does not apply to or cover any other Zendesk Services or functionality, or to any beta or Early Access Program offerings". The processing location of generative AI / Copilot was not found.

28.e: "Create ticket deletion schedules to automatically remove archived tickets after a set period, helping you comply with data retention laws". Attachments: "Create recurring attachment deletion schedules". **Limits:** schedules apply to archived tickets ("Zendesk automatically archives tickets 120 days after they are closed"). Without the Advanced Data Privacy and Protection add-on, "only one ticket deletion schedule can be active at a time".

29.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; uniform #29 rule, no explicit "end users are free" statement
29.e: "Zendesk pricing is primarily seat-based (per agent, per month)". End users "can only submit and track tickets". Approvers can be end users ("employees without an agent seat").

30.p: Suite Team (AI agents included; usage is counted in automated resolutions)
30.e: "AI agents automate customer support across messaging, email, web forms, and voice by answering questions from trusted knowledge sources". They can be extended with "authorized actions, and API integrations". "Each account includes an allowance of automated resolutions based on their plan, and you can buy more". **Missing:** an AI agent in Slack is not documented. Pointing the user to the right form, checking request status (possible only through a custom API integration) and opening a ticket on the user's behalf were not verified.

31.p: Suite Growth (HC); Suite Professional on the pricing page
31.e: "Support admins can create a list of services and assets that users can then request through the help center." "The service catalog can only be turned on in one help center." **Missing:** linking catalog items to requests handled in other systems (e.g. Aboard) is not documented.

32.p: Suite Growth (HC) / Professional for 5 brands; Suite Enterprise for 300
32.e: "Set up multiple brands to give each customer-facing identity its own help center, contact points, and ticket brand." "Suite Growth and Professional includes up to five brands. Suite Enterprise and Enterprise Plus includes up to 300 brands." **Missing:** quick setup that reuses existing data (e.g. from HubSpot) is not documented. More than 5 clients requires Enterprise.

33.e: "When a Zendesk event occurs, a mobile push notification is sent based on the event type, user settings, and registered devices." Options include "All new tickets" and "Tickets assigned to me". On-call tool integrations (e.g. PagerDuty) were not checked.

34.e: Followers "are internal users who stay informed without being visible to end users. They can make private comments and access tickets they follow." "Internal users who can view the ticket can add and remove followers from the ticket, including themselves."

35.e: Jira: the developer docs list a "JIRA Integration API" (the Jira help article was not read). GitHub is available only through a third-party Marketplace app: "TicketSync Pro connects GitHub issues and pull requests to Zendesk tickets". Notion is available only as a knowledge source (#22). **Missing:** structured links from a ticket to Notion pages are not documented.

36.p: Suite Growth (HC); Suite Professional on the pricing page
36.e: "You can use conditional ticket fields to show agents and end users only the fields relevant to their answers … Set if-then rules by user type, make fields required". The feature controls visibility. Filtering the options of a single field is not described.

37.p: Suite Enterprise (custom roles). Below Enterprise, only admins can build forms
37.e: Custom role permissions: "Manage ticket forms: Create, modify, and delete ticket forms." "Manage ticket fields: Create, modify, and delete ticket fields using the Ticket fields page in Admin Center." Plan line: "Customer Service Suite Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus". Note: the permission covers all forms, not only the team's own.

38.p: Suite Growth (multiple forms, K.O. #9) plus help center theme code
38.e: The only route is a theme-code workflow that hides forms by organization: "This workflow doesn't work for unauthenticated users or users who don't have an organization". "Zendesk doesn't support or guarantee" it. Natively, forms can be limited only per brand (K.O. #9). For agents: "You can't restrict a ticket form to a group or set of groups."

39.p: Suite Growth (HC); Suite Professional on the pricing page
39.e: "Task lists help you track actions needed to resolve tickets by adding a checklist directly within the ticket workspace. You can add one task list per ticket, mark tasks complete or incomplete". **Missing:** owners and due dates per task are not documented.

40.e: "When a group is private, only agents from that group can view tickets assigned to it." In custom roles, an agent may access tickets "Assigned to them". Below Enterprise, the group restriction "is not completely secure" (K.O. #13).

41.e: Route: the API only. "Create Many Tickets POST /api/v2/tickets/create_many Accepts an array of up to 100 ticket objects." No native CSV import of tickets was found. The help article on bulk ticket creation requires sign-in and was not read.

42.e: Route: a third-party Marketplace app. "Recurring Tickets by Veryation (Support) (paid) … choose a schedule, and it creates that ticket automatically every time it falls due." The native recipe only reopens an existing ticket: "Automation runs on the selected date and changes the ticket status back to Open".

43.e: Route: a trigger plus a webhook to a custom endpoint, or Zapier. "Connect webhooks to triggers, automations, or subscribe to events to automate notifications and data sharing with services like Slack or Asana." No native or official spreadsheet integration was verified.

44.p: Ticket creation: plan not stated (Datadog). Solution suggestions: Suite Professional + Copilot
44.e: Official Datadog integration (built by Datadog): "Create and update tickets using @zendesk mentions in monitor notifications." Pointing to a solution: auto assist makes "suggestions to your agents on how to solve them". Only Datadog was checked.

45.e: View conditions include "Requester" and "Hours since created". However, "Custom fields of type Multi-line, Numeric, Decimal, Credit Card, and Regex are not available as view conditions." **Missing:** filtering by amount in Explore reports was not verified.

46.p: Suite Growth (HC); Suite Professional on the pricing page
46.e: "Set up the Time Tracking app to track how much time agents spend on tickets, review timelogs, and control timer behavior". "Installation creates custom ticket fields for time spent".

47.p: Support Team (views, automations); Suite Growth (HC) for SLA alerts
47.e: Views can use "Hours since status category pending". SLAs: "create business rules that take action based on SLAs (for example, to get attention on a ticket before the SLA is breached)". A ticket reminder is a workaround recipe (plan not stated): "Automation runs on the selected date and changes the ticket status back to Open".

48.e: "You can see tickets activity for yourself or another user in the user profile." "For end-users, you can view requested tickets and CCs."

49.e: No official source was found that syncs company structure or fills in the requester's manager in Customer Service Suite. K.O. #10 found no evidence that approvals resolve the requester's manager automatically. The "Workday integration" is listed only for the internal-only Employee Service Suite.

50.e: Zapier "Zendesk Integrations" page: "Connect Zendesk to Zapier to streamline and organize your customer interactions".

51.p: All plans (external content; storage limits vary by plan)
51.e: There is no dedicated Outline connector. Route: the native universal connector. "The universal connector retrieves content through the source's REST API and makes that content available in Zendesk as external knowledge." Compatibility with Outline was not verified. The Zapier Zendesk + Outline page returned 404.

52.e: Route: Zapier. The Zapier HubSpot + Zendesk page lists the HubSpot triggers "New Contact" and "New Company". No official HubSpot–Zendesk integration was verified (Marketplace blocked). Setting up a client's support space (brand, help center) from HubSpot data is not documented.

53.e: Route: a custom build on the Zendesk API ("Work with tickets, users and organizations and manage ticket workflows"). Time is logged natively by the Time Tracking app (#46). No official or Zapier integration was found: the Zapier Zendesk + Productive page returned 404, and the Marketplace was blocked.

54.e: Route: a custom build on the Tickets API ("Create Many Tickets POST /api/v2/tickets/create_many"). The ServiceNow connector is for knowledge only ("Client ID and Client secret of an OAuth API endpoint for external clients in your ServiceNow instance"). Ticket exchange with ServiceNow was not found (Marketplace blocked; search budget used up).

55.e: "The following example action flow automatically creates a meeting in Microsoft Calendar when a ticket is reassigned". **Missing:** Google Calendar (the company uses Google Workspace) and showing ticket deadlines or tasks in calendars are not documented.

56.e: Route: a custom build that calls the Zendesk Tickets API ("Create Many Tickets POST /api/v2/tickets/create_many") on Aboard events. No Aboard integration was found. Whether Aboard offers an API, webhooks or a Zapier app was not verified.

57.e: Deletion is a manual workflow: "Delete personal data in ticket conversations … Permanently delete the end user or agent from Zendesk Support." Export: "If a data subject requests a copy of their personal data, you can export the data". However, "The exported data doesn't include all the users' possible personal data", the export requires "a Zendesk Suite Growth plan or above", and "You must contact Zendesk Customer Support to activate it." Nothing is automatic.

58.p: Suite Professional (Data Center Location add-on, free)
58.e: "a Subscriber can choose to host their data within the following regions: United States European Economic Area (EEA) United Kingdom (UK) Japan (JP) Australia (AU)". "Service Data for Covered Functionality can only be hosted in a single location." Per-client regions therefore require separate accounts, and India is not offered.

59.e: "Shared views: Admins can create views that are available to all agents or to all agents in a specific group." "Personal views: Agents can create views that are available to themselves only." Kanban-style boards are not documented.

questions: #4: Can a trigger notify the ticket requester about status changes and about each approval decision (e.g. a condition on the "Approval status" field)? On which plan?
#6: Are @mentions in internal notes, and tasks within a ticket, available on Customer Service Suite? From which plan?
#9: Is a date custom field type available, and can a ticket form be limited per client (organization), not only per brand?

#10: Which Customer Service plan includes approvals: Growth, Professional or Enterprise? The help center and pricing page disagree. Can a two-step chain (manager, then Head of Finance) run automatically via action flows, and can the requester's manager be resolved automatically?

#13: Is per-client separation for Platform with private groups (one group per client project) supported on Enterprise without exposing tickets to other agents? Is "Suite Growth" still sold for Customer Service, and at what price?
#17: Is the ticket audit / events history available on all plans, and can any entry (including comment visibility) be changed retroactively?
#23: Is there a supported flow where a Slack help channel or slash command creates a private ticket and syncs agent replies and status changes back to the requester in Slack?
#26: Can Zendesk provide NIS2 supply-chain documentation (e.g. incident notification commitments in the contract)?
#27: Where are generative AI features (Copilot, Zendesk AI) processed for an account hosted in the EEA? Which sub-processors are involved?
#29: Which plans include light agents, and how many? Confirm that end users (internal and external) are unlimited and free.
Pricing: EUR prices and monthly-billing prices, and the Enterprise price for Customer Service Suite.
#49: Can Customer Service Suite sync the company structure (from Google Workspace or an HR system) and fill in the requester's manager automatically for approvals? On which plan?

#11: Can a trigger or action flow create a side conversation child ticket automatically (e.g. an onboarding ticket creates an IT equipment ticket)? Can the parent show the child's full history, including internal notes?

#20: Can Zendesk AI draft an article from a single resolved ticket into an existing help center and link it with connected Notion or Confluence content? Is Knowledge copilot (EAP) available on Customer Service Suite, and from which plan and at what price?
#21: When will Zendesk Bridge and the Zendesk MCP Server be generally available, on which plans, and at what price after the EAP?
#22: Can Notion content be restricted to one brand's (client's) help center, given that only one Notion connection per account is allowed?

#30: Can AI agents work in Slack for employees, check the status of an existing request, point the user to the right form and open a ticket on the user's behalf? What is the automated-resolution allowance per plan, and what does an extra resolution cost?
#31: Can a service catalog item link to a request handled in another system (e.g. an external URL to Aboard)?
#32: Can a client's brand and help center be created through the API or from a template, reusing existing data (e.g. from HubSpot)?
#38: Is there a native way, without theme code, to show a ticket form only to selected requesters (e.g. a user segment or an organization such as managers)?
#39: Can task-list items have an owner and a due date?
#41: Is there a native CSV import for tickets? The article "Can I bulk create tickets to email my users?" requires sign-in.
#45: Can Explore reports filter tickets by numeric or decimal custom fields (amounts)?

#52, #53, #54, #56: Are there official integrations, built by Zendesk or the other vendor, for HubSpot, Productive, ServiceNow ticket exchange and Aboard? The Zendesk Marketplace is blocked for the headless browser.
#55: Does the action builder support Google Calendar?
#57: Can data subject deletion and export be automated through the API, and does the export include ticket content?
#58: Can one account host different clients' data in different regions? Is India available?
checks: Re-checked: Suite Professional “$115 agent/month paid yearly”; Enterprise lists “Approval workflows” (https://www.zendesk.com/pricing/).
Re-checked: ES Suite is “for organizations that want to use Zendesk products exclusively for internal services” (ES overview).
Not re-checked: the supplemental-terms quote. The sections on that page are collapsed and plain page text does not show them.

Corrected #29 from “Meets” to “Unknown” under the uniform #29 rule in analysis/01_ko_criteria.md: the pricing page (including collapsed FAQ text) has no explicit statement that end users are free or unlimited.

Corrected #21 from "Meets (early access only)" to "Partial": Zendesk Bridge can create and update tickets for external agents such as Claude, but only in an early access program (EAP); general availability and pricing are not stated. Other vendors got Meets only for generally available features.

Corrected #22 from "Meets" to "Partial": the Notion connection feeds help center search and AI agents, but restricting Notion content to one client's help center was not verified (only one Notion connection is allowed). Same rule as Freshservice #22.
Note: zendesk.com/marketplace returned a Cloudflare challenge (403); marketplace-based verdicts rest on help-center and partner pages.

1.e: "E-mail tickets – Convert emails into tickets automatically when you add email as a channel." "Ticket history – See the activity on a ticket in chronological order." Both available on all plans.

2.e: "Email channel" ("This refers to your support email address."): 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 100. "When customers send emails to specific support email addresses for different departments, support administrators can set rules to automatically generate tickets and route them to the right department." Standard view: "Unassigned Open Tickets". Limit: the number of client addresses is capped by the plan.

3.e: Contact notification "Receiving a new ticket – Notifies the requester that their ticket has been received".

4.e: Contact notifications: "Receiving a reply – Notifies the requester of a new reply", "Closing a ticket", "Adding a public comment". **Missing:** the only status-change rule for requesters is for closing. No requester notification for approval steps exists (the only approval-related rule notifies "the reviewer (approver)").

5.e: "When an agent marks a comment as private, the comment is visible only to internal users who have access to the ticket". "By default, comments are added as private."

6.p: Standard (Tasks, Followers); side chats from Professional
6.e: "You can mention other agents in a comment; they will be notified via email." Comparison: "Tasks – Create follow-up tasks for your team based on ticket conversations" (Standard+). "Side chats" (Professional+).

7.n: change recorded in Ticket history; the Enterprise Audit log does not list tickets, see K.O. #17
7.p: Free (history); Express ("Direct assignment to agents and teams")
7.e: Update Ticket API field: "assigneeId … ID of the agent assigned to resolve the ticket". "Get Ticket History Retrieves details of all actions(called events) performed on a ticket". The example event shows the actor and "Case Owner". Schedules can "Periodically reassign tickets from offline agents to agents who are currently available".

8.p: Express (custom statuses); Professional (per department layout); Enterprise (per process: "Multi layout" 20 / department)
8.e: "Custom ticket status & status grouping – Create customized statuses for your tickets." "Ticket properties like status values, picklist values, multi-select picklist values, and mandatory fields are set at the layout level". "Multi layout – Show a separate set of fields for each process or service".

9.p: Enterprise ("Multi layout" 20 / department). Professional: one "Department specific layout"
9.e: "Multi layout – Show a separate set of fields for each process or service" (Enterprise). Field types include "Date", "Date/Time", "Picklist". Fields can be marked "mandatory". Field dependencies from Standard. Per-client forms: not checked.

10.e: "Approvals – Ask for internal approvals in the context of a specific ticket" (Professional+). API: "agent can submit the ticket for approval", with "approverIds", "description", "status" and "processedTime" recorded. **Missing:** no documented sequential chain (manager, then department head). Approvers must be agents. Zoho staff answer: "the native approval functionality does not allow us to achieve this directly" for non-agents or a lite agent, and suggests "Blueprint rule or custom functions" (forum, ~2 years old).

11.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; Early Access only, "We are opening this feature on request basis"; same rule as Zendesk #21
11.e: "Parent-child ticketing is available in the Enterprise and Professional editions." "Tickets from within a department and cross-department can be associated with each other." The onboarding example has HR, Asset Management and Admin, and each department "Has complete visibility on the progress". "Within the parent-child subtab of a ticket, users can update the ticket status and owner of a child and parent ticket."

12.p: Free (own tickets); Professional for CC'd contacts ("Secondary contact (Cc's)")
12.e: The admin can enable "Customers can view tickets of other users in their account" so "users can see all tickets of their company rather than just the ones created from their own email address". Public comments are visible to "other secondary contacts who have access to the ticket in the help center".

13.e: "Once you assign a department, the agent can access and view only those tickets that belong to that department." "Data sharing – Assign different levels of access to support data to different roles" (Enterprise only). **Missing:** no documented per-client (account) visibility rule inside one department. Per-client separation works only by modelling each client as its own department (Professional: 10 departments total; Enterprise: 50 plus add-on).

14.p: Standard (5 workflow rules / module + Zapier). Express: 1 rule, ticket module only
14.e: "Workflow rules – A set of actions that are executed when certain specified conditions are met." (Express 1, Standard 5, Professional 15 / department / module). "Zapier – Use the Zapier integration to connect Desk with other vital apps." (Standard+). "Supervise - Time-based rules" (Standard+).

15.e: Targets: "select fields and a corresponding value to set a criteria". The response target can be applied "only to the first response". Escalation: "You can choose to be notified before, on, or after the resolution time."

16.e: "Response, resolution & FCR dashboards" (Standard+). "Agent queue" (Express+). "Custom dashboards": "10" on Standard, "Unlimited" from Professional. "SLA dashboards" (Professional+).

17.e: "Audit logs are retained for a minimum of two years." Tracked entities include "Agents", "Department", "Workflow", "Blueprint", "Contacts" and "Accounts". **Missing:** Tickets are not in the audit-log entity list. Ticket changes appear only in "Ticket history". Owner-change entries and the claim that entries cannot be edited are not stated.

18.p: Express (Reply Assistance with own key, BYOK); Professional (native Zia, included, "No charges")
18.e: "Reply Assistance – Get relevant solutions from your knowledge base". "Suggested articles – Pulls relevant answers from your FAQs and Knowledge Base". **Missing:** suggestions from past tickets and the "similar problem before" flag. Zia (native) "Trains exclusively on Knowledge Base articles and does not use ticket-related data". "Resolution Expert" (past resolutions) is a Zia agent, and "AI agents for Desk is available for selected users only in USDC and INDC" (not EU).

19.n: included; Zia Actions "supported only in English"
19.p: Enterprise (Zia Actions, EU DC listed). Professional: native "Field predictions" only
19.e: "Zia can auto-populate these fields, which can then trigger assignment rules or other workflow rules to route the ticket to the appropriate team or agent". "Field predictions – Zia can analyze ticket patterns and automatically update field values such as priority, type of issue" (Professional+). "Zia Actions … categorizing tickets … Available DCs: US, AU, EU, CA, and IN" (Enterprise).

20.e: "Article generation – Convert resolved tickets into knowledge base articles". "Add resolution as KB – Directly add the ticket resolution as an article in your Knowledge Base." **Missing:** linking the result to the existing scattered KB (Notion, Outline) is not documented. The only route found is a one-off import ("You can import … knowledge base articles").

21.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; Zoho MCP supports Desk, but which Desk tools it exposes, for example creating or updating tickets, was not verified
21.p: All plans (uses the plan's API credits)
21.e: Zoho MCP "connects LLMs like GPT or Claude to Zoho's APIs, data models, and actions". "Compatible with Claude, GPT, and other AI agents right out of the box." Desk is in the supported services list. "Zoho MCP is included at no additional cost for all Zoho users." Native Zia BYOK lists ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Azure OpenAI only (no Claude).

22.n: custom build on the public API
22.e: No Notion integration on the Desk integrations page or in Desk help. The Zapier Zoho Desk app has no article action (actions include "Create Ticket", "Create Contact", "Add Comment"). Route: custom sync to the Desk KB through the API ("Desk.articles.CREATE Grants access to create articles"), or a one-off CSV import of KB articles. Answer bot / Zia answer only from the Desk KB.

23.e: "Create tickets, comment on tickets, and respond to tickets from Slack". Notifications are delivered "to your agents via Slack". "Other users, however, must authenticate themselves by logging in to Zoho Desk". **Missing:** the integration is agent-facing. There is no documented intake by non-agent employees from a help channel, no private requester–agent sync, and no requester notifications in Slack.

24.p: Professional (webhooks: 5 active; Enterprise 10). API on all plans (Free 5,000 credits)
24.e: "Zoho Desk supports webhooks that asynchronously deliver information on events that occur in the help desk." Events include Ticket_Add, Ticket_Update, Ticket_Comment_Add, Ticket_Approval_Update and Ticket_Attachment_Add, filtered by "departmentIds". "Public extensions – Build, host, and sell custom extensions on the Zoho Desk marketplace."

25.p: Desk plan not stated for SAML (configured in Zoho Accounts). G Suite login: all plans in the comparison, but the help article says "(Professional or Enterprise Edition), you will be able to access all the features"
25.e: SAML with Google: "Configure SAML in your Zoho account using the SSO URL and the Certificate downloaded from Google." G Suite: "Log in to Zoho Desk from Google's Universal Navigation bar with your G Suite credentials." MFA: "If you are an organization admin, you can enforce MFA for all the users in your organization." No separate subscription is named for SAML in Zoho Accounts. Zoho Directory (optional) is priced separately.

26.e: "ISO/IEC 27001 … Valid Upto : 21-Aug-2028 … Applicable to - All cloud services of Zoho". "Zoho is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant." Also ISO/IEC 27701, 27017 and 27018. DPA: "drop an email to legal@zohocorp.com to request a copy". **Missing:** no NIS2 supply-chain documentation on the compliance or GDPR pages.

27.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; backup location not stated, pre-built AI agents only in US/IN DC
27.e: Europe: "Amsterdam, Netherland – Primary Datacenter", "Dublin, Ireland – Secondary Datacenter" (map tooltip in page source). Zia GenAI "is hosted on Zoho's servers within the data center corresponding to the customer's region". Caveats: ChatGPT/Azure BYOK sends data outside Zoho. "Pre-built Zoho Desk AI Agents … *Available in US & IN DC". Backup location is not stated explicitly.

28.e: No admin-set retention period for tickets or attachments was found. The retention page covers only Zoho's own handling: "We hold the data in your account as long as you choose to use Zoho Services." Deleted records: "60 days in RCB". Closed tickets are auto-archived, not deleted. A custom deletion job (Schedules + Deluge, Enterprise) is not documented.

29.e: Pricing is "/ agent / month". No price is listed for contacts or help-center users. **Missing:** approvers must be agents (see #10), so the manager and Head of Finance need a paid agent seat. Internal people who only comment need paid "light agents" (US$6 / month) below Enterprise.

30.p: Standard (Answer bot); Enterprise (Answer bot in ASAP, GC flows)
30.e: "Answer bot – An AI-powered reply assistant that provides relevant responses to agents and customers based on its intelligence from the existing KB articles." "Answer bot in ASAP – AI-powered answer bot within ASAP, for customers to interact with." Help center users can "Check the status of their tickets". **Missing:** a bot that opens tickets on the user's behalf, points to the right form or checks status is not documented. No employee assistant in Slack (the Slack app is agent-facing, see K.O. #23).

31.p: Free (help center); Enterprise ("Employee Self service", "HTML customization")
31.e: "you can display your department catalog when users submit a ticket from the help center. Users can click on a department to create their ticket in it." "Agents and customers can select an appropriate layout of the Tickets module while adding a ticket." **Missing:** a service catalog with links to requests handled in other systems (e.g., Aboard) is not documented.

32.e: "Create self-service portals for multiple brands within the same Zoho Desk account." "You can customize the logo, colors, layout and permissions of the multi-brand Help Centers". Each brand Help Center is tied to a department. **Missing:** one brand per client means one department per client (Enterprise 50, then a paid add-on). Quick setup from existing data (e.g., HubSpot) is not documented.

33.n: push/SMS; no on-call tool integration found
33.p: Free (mobile app); Standard (SMS add-on, price not found)
33.e: Mobile app: "Get push notifications for new ticket assignments, updates, and other alerts." "SMS add-on – Send acknowledgment messages to your customers and notify agents on new ticket assignment via SMS." "Zoho Desk app" is available on all plans.

34.e: API: "adds one or more users to the followers list of a ticket" and "removes one or more users from the followers list". Sharing gives "full access, restricted or read-only access", and agents can "un-share a ticket". **Limited:** sharing works per department, not per person. "Email alerts cannot be set for tickets that you follow". Adding another person as a follower in the UI is not verified.

35.e: GitHub extension: "You can even link multiple issues to a single ticket." Jira: "Break silos and collaborate with your engineering team effectively using Jira." **Missing:** no Notion link integration found. Other systems only via the API or Zapier.

36.e: "Field dependencies – Manage dependencies between two fields." (Standard). Layout rules: "Show Fields: Choose this action when you want specific fields to be shown". "Check Apply to Help Center to manage dependencies between fields when tickets are submitted through your help center."

37.p: Standard (custom profiles: 5); Enterprise (several forms per department)
37.e: "Users with Manage Layouts and Fields permission in their profile can access this feature." "You can add fields and sections, reorder, mark as required". **Missing:** limiting a business team (e.g., People) to editing only its own forms is not documented. The permission is per profile.

38.e: Layout options found: "In the Layout Permissions field, select the user profiles that will have access to the layout" (agent profiles) and "Select the checkbox for Display in Help Center" (on/off). No way to show a form only to a group of requesters was found.

39.e: "Ticket templates are available only on Professional and Enterprise." Templates let you "Specify the ticket's Status and Owner." Blueprint: "Create flowcharts with automated steps, notifications, and requirements to follow and keep processes on track." "Tasks – Create follow-up tasks for your team". **Missing:** checklist items that each owner ticks off are not documented.

40.e: "users higher in the hierarchy always have access to all the records belonging to the users below in the hierarchy". "By default, users of the same role cannot access each other's data." "Data sharing – Assign different levels of access to support data to different roles." **Missing:** restriction is by role and department. Hiding one specific ticket from other agents is not documented.

41.e: "You can import your support tickets, contacts, customer accounts, knowledge base articles…" "The supported formats are Excel (XLS) and Comma Separated Value (CSV)." (article titled "Old UI"). "Import data" is on the comparison from Express.

42.e: "Schedules are automated, user-defined actions that run custom actions either at a specific time or on a recurring basis." "a schedule can create a follow-up ticket every Monday morning". Repeat options include "Every Month" and "Every Year".

43.n: Zapier, or a workflow webhook / custom function
43.e: Zapier trigger: "New Status Change – Triggers when a status of ticket is changed." Zapier template: "Add new Zoho Desk tickets to Google Sheets as rows". "Webhook – Send automated messages or information to third-party apps every time an event occurs". No native spreadsheet register was found.

44.e: "E-mail tickets – Convert emails into tickets automatically when you add email as a channel." Zapier action "Create Ticket – Creates a new ticket for customer requests." **Missing:** no monitoring-tool integration was verified (Site24x7 not checked: search limit reached). Pointing to a solution is not documented.

45.e: "Custom views – Use filters to list just the tickets you need to focus on." "Custom reports – Create your own custom reports to keep track of metrics that matter to you." "Custom fields – Store additional information relevant to a ticket using custom fields."

46.e: "Time entry – Keep track of time spent on every ticket and manage billable hours." "Auto ticket time tracking – Automatically track the time spent on a ticket without any manual intervention."

47.e: "Supervise - Time-based rules – Create rules for time-based events such as ticket resolution reminders." Standard views: "My Overdue Tickets", "Customer Responded Tickets". **Missing:** a reminder an agent sets on a single ticket, and a visible "waiting for X time" counter, are not verified.

48.e: "Ticket timeline – See a timeline of all the past tickets from a particular customer."

49.n: agents only; custom build for requesters
49.e: "Roles – Create roles to replicate your organization chart and assign a profile to each role accordingly." G Suite: "Add users from G Suite to Zoho Desk as agents." **Missing:** requester (contact) manager fields, directory sync and auto-fill of the requester's manager for approvals are not documented. Approvers must be agents (K.O. #10).

50.p: Standard ("Excludes zaps that use features not supported in the standard plan")
50.e: Official Zapier app "Zoho Desk Integrations". Triggers include "New Ticket", "Updated Ticket" and "New Status Change". Actions include "Create Ticket" and "Update Ticket".

51.n: custom build on the public API only
51.e: Not on the Desk integrations page. The Zapier pair page returned 404. Route: custom build on the Desk API (e.g., "Desk.articles.CREATE"). The Outline side was not verified.

52.p: Standard (extension "Compatible Editions Standard Professional Enterprise"; "Pricing Free")
52.e: Official extension "Developed by: Zoho Corporation": "Fetch information about contacts and deals from HubSpot". The widget shows "Name, Email, Mobile Number, Organization of the customer". **Missing:** importing or syncing HubSpot companies and contacts into Desk accounts/contacts (to set up a client space) is not documented. The extension works inside a ticket widget.

53.n: custom build on the public API only
53.e: Not on the Desk integrations page. The Zapier pair page returned 404. Route: custom build on the Desk API (e.g., time entries: "Time entry", "Ticket TimeEntry" API). The Productive side was not verified.

54.n: Zoho Flow, Zoho's iPaaS, separate product
54.p: Standard ("Zoho Flow": "Excludes flows that use features not supported in the standard plan")
54.e: Zoho Flow ServiceNow trigger: "Record created Triggers when an incident record is created". Actions include "Create incident" and "Update incident", plus Desk ticket triggers. Email-to-ticket also works from clients' L1 tools. No native ServiceNow connector was found.

55.e: The G Suite integration lists only "import your business contacts", "Add users from G Suite to Zoho Desk as agents" and "Log in … with your G Suite credentials". "Events – Log and schedule events and invite other agents" (Professional) is internal. No Google Calendar sync was found (search limit reached).

56.n: custom build on the public API, or Zapier "Create Ticket"
56.e: No Aboard integration found. Route: an Aboard event calls the Desk API or Zapier action "Create Ticket – Creates a new ticket for customer requests." The Aboard side (API, Zapier app) was not verified.

57.n: admin-run DSR request, not fully automatic
57.e: "In Zoho Desk, you can register this request and send them a copy of the data from one or many modules." "you can take up this request and permanently delete the data from one or many modules." "All Records - Choose to view all the records associated with the contact's email address".

58.e: "Data center location – Choose the nearest data center country location while signing up." DCs named on the page: "US, EU, IN, AU, JP, CA, CN, UAE". The region is chosen per account at sign-up, so per-client regions need separate Desk accounts.

59.n: queue views; no kanban board found
59.e: "Agent queue – Quick way to access open tickets under each agent." "Teams queue – Quick way to access open tickets under each team." Standard views: "My Open Tickets", "My Teams Open Tickets", "Unassigned Open Tickets".

questions: #10: Can one ticket run a **sequential** approval (requester's manager, then Head of Finance), natively or via Blueprint, with each decision and comment recorded? Can an approver be a light agent or a non-agent (e.g., by email)? Is that Zoho staff forum answer still valid?
#4: Can requesters be notified automatically of every status change and of each approval step (workflow email alerts), and from which plan?
#13: Can visibility be limited per client account inside one department (e.g., Data Sharing / Teams on Enterprise), without one department per client?
#17: Are ticket owner changes and approval decisions logged with user and time? Can any audit log or ticket history entry be edited or deleted by an admin?
#23: Can non-agent employees raise a ticket from a Slack help channel or slash command, and get replies and status updates back in Slack (private thread or DM)?
#26: Does Zoho provide NIS2 supply-chain documentation (security questionnaire, incident-notification terms, sub-processor list) for Zoho Desk?
#27: Are backups of EU-DC accounts kept only in the EU (Amsterdam/Dublin)? Is any support or remote access to EU data performed from outside the EU?
#29: Confirm in writing that contacts/help-center users (internal and external) are unlimited and free on each plan.
Pricing: confirm EUR prices and the Standard user limit ("Unlimited" in the comparison vs "5 users" in the FAQ).
#28: Can an admin set a retention period for tickets and attachments (e.g., delete closed tickets after N months) natively or with a supported Schedule/Deluge function, and from which plan?
#38: Can a ticket form (layout) or department in the help center be shown only to a selected group of requesters (e.g., managers), and from which plan?
#55: Is there an official Google Calendar (or Zoho Calendar) sync for ticket due dates, tasks and events? Does the G Suite integration cover Calendar?

#18: In the EU DC, can Zia suggest solutions from past resolved tickets, or flag similar earlier tickets? When will the "Resolution Expert" Zia agent be available in the EU DC, and at what credit cost?
#20 / #22: Can Zia or the Answer bot use an external knowledge source (Notion, Outline), or only Desk KB articles? Is any Notion connector planned?
#11: Is parent-child ticketing generally available on Professional/Enterprise, or still Early Access "on request"? Can every requester see sub-ticket status?
#21: Which Zoho Desk tools (read and update tickets, comments, assignment) does the Zoho MCP server expose? Is Zoho MCP available for EU-DC accounts?
#25: Is SAML SSO with Google Workspace for Desk agents free on every Desk plan, or is a paid Zoho Directory edition required? Can MFA be enforced for agents without Directory?
#30: Can the Answer bot / ASAP widget create a ticket for the user, check ticket status or route the user to the right form? Is there an employee-facing assistant in Slack?
#34: Can an agent add another agent or light agent as a follower from the ticket UI? Can a single person (not a department) get temporary access to one ticket?
#40: Can one ticket (e.g., an HR case) be restricted to its owner and the manager while other agents in the same department cannot see it?
#44: Is there an official Site24x7 (Zoho) or other monitoring integration that creates Desk tickets automatically?
#52: Can HubSpot companies and contacts be imported or synced into Desk accounts and contacts (not only shown in the ticket widget)?
#58: Can one organization run Desk accounts in several DCs (e.g., EU and US) under one contract, with shared agents and licences?
#42 / #47: Is there a no-code recurring-ticket feature (without Deluge)? Can agents set a reminder on a single ticket?
checks: Corrected #27 from “Meets” to “Partial”: the requirement covers backups and AI processing, and the screen itself says the backup location is not stated and pre-built AI agents run only in US/IN data centres. Same rule as TOPdesk #27.
Corrected #26 from “Partial” to “Meets” under the uniform #26 rule in analysis/01_ko_criteria.md (ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 confirmed; NIS2 is an open question for all vendors).
Corrected #11 from "Meets" to "Partial": parent-child ticketing across departments is Early Access, opened on request. Only generally available features get Meets (same rule as Zendesk #21).
Corrected #21 from "Meets" to "Partial": rule 7 needs evidence that an external agent can act on tickets; the Desk tool list of Zoho MCP was not verified.

1.e: "The mail import can automatically create new calls … or update existing ones"; "When an imported email's subject includes a number of an existing call card … TOPdesk updates the relevant card"; Progress Trail shows "Emails sent from the card. Imported emails are also displayed". Note: replies are matched by the ticket number in the subject line.

2.n: One mail import per address, with default values such as the operator group. Automatic assignment spreads new calls across logged-in members of the group. Caveat: there is no B2B "client organization" object; clients are modelled as branches (K.O. screen).
2.p: Essential ("Unlimited mail imports", "Round Robin assigning (Auto assigner)")
2.e: "If your organization receives multiple emails at different addresses, set up different mail imports"; "Automatic assignment distributes new calls over the members of an operator group, to ensure these calls are picked up more quickly."

3.e: "an event-and-action combination that automatically sends an email to the caller when the newly created call card is saved". This has to be configured.

4.e: "This event will be triggered when the value of a field is changed". Missing: nothing works out of the box, and each notification has to be built as an event plus an email action. Notifying the *requester* at each approval step is not documented; only notifications to the approvers are ("These e-mail actions will be sent to all members of the group"). The events page sits under "The old Action Management".

5.e: "Share internal notes (invisible for end user)"; "Make invisible to caller option, which makes your actions and possible attachments invisible in the Self-Service Portal"

6.e: Tasks: "With partial calls … the processing of the call is subdivided" (but "Partial calls are only available in Second Line Calls"). Pricing lists "Active view on who has the ticket open" and "Share with others". Missing: I found no @mentions and no threaded agent-to-agent comments in the docs I reviewed.

7.n: Assigning and reassigning: yes. The audit-log comment is not verified: the audit trail says "nearly all" fields are tracked and does not name the operator field.
7.e: "you can transfer the call to another operator"; "Via the audit trail in TOPdesk, you can follow the changes that are made to a card … Nearly all fields are tracked."

8.n: Custom status names exist in the Call Management status drop-down list. Separate status sets per process (per team, category or request type) are not documented.
8.e: "In this drop-down list you can provide a name for the status, and you can define what the processing status and On Hold status values must be."

9.e: Forms for "new first line calls; new second line calls; new (preliminary) requests for change"; "Mandatory fields"; optional fields of types "Drop-down list … Number field … Date field". Limits: forms live in the Self-Service Portal (not used for email tickets); optional fields are capped at "two tabs … with a maximum of five of each field type"; forms per client are not documented.

10.p: Engaged ("Approval (multiple levels)" is listed as "Excluded in Essential plan")
10.e: "All persons who are tagged as managers on their Person cards can be assigned as authorizers"; approvers can "add a reply to it, or immediately click Approve or Reject" in the portal. Missing: approvals are documented only in Change Management (requests for change, authorization activities), not on regular calls. Automatic routing to the requester's *own* line manager is not documented.

11.n: Partial calls stay linked to the main call, and change activities can span departments. Missing: partial calls work only on second-line calls, and the docs do not say that a sub-ticket's status and full history are visible from the parent.
11.p: Essential (partial tickets); Engaged ("Collaborate with multiple departments on a change", "Link changes, problems and tickets")
11.e: "The partial calls can be handled separately, but will remain linked with the original call"; "Partial calls are only available in Second Line Calls."

12.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets" based on inference
12.e: "When a call has been shared with them, sharees can track the progress and update the call via the My Requests overview"; sharing can be restricted to "other persons from their own branch". Note: I found no explicit statement about default visibility. The verdict rests on the explicit-sharing model, which implies that other people's calls are not visible unless shared (my inference).

13.p: Essential ("Unlimited teams"; filters are not plan-gated in the comparison)
13.e: Operator filter: "only view cards linked to their own or to specified operator groups"; "Branch filter: filters the visible cards by branch". Caveats: "An operator can always view cards when … they are the last changer of the card", and "data of filtered cards may always be visible on a specific tab of another (unfiltered) card".

14.n: If/then events and actions, action sequences, scheduled actions and webhooks are built in. An official Zapier app exists (#50).
14.e: "Customizable actions and triggers" and "Plug and play action sequence library" (Included in Essential plan); "This event will be triggered when the value of a field is changed"

15.p: Engaged ("Service level agreements" is listed as "Excluded in Essential plan")
15.e: "Define the response time, first line duration, second line duration … for each priority"; warnings can be configured: "create an event based on card dates, such as the target date" that fire "when a card date will be reached within a particular period of time".

16.e: "Adjustable dashboards", "KPI report", "Standard duration report"; standard reports "Responded in period and Response target date achieved or breached"

17.e: "Via the audit trail in TOPdesk, you can follow the changes that are made to a card … Nearly all fields are tracked." Missing: the docs do not say that entries are tamper-proof or cannot be edited retroactively, and the log covers "nearly all", not all, fields.

18.n: The AI answer assistant and TOPdesk Robin draft answers from the knowledge base only. Analysing past tickets, or flagging that a similar problem has come up before, is not documented. Included in the Excellent plan; no add-on price.
18.e: "analyzing the knowledge base to generate a useful answer to the caller"; "The Knowledge Base is the only source for the AI"

19.n: AI triage suggests category, subcategory, priority and operator group (queue), but an agent must apply the suggestions on the call card. Routing incoming email tickets without an agent is not documented. Included in the plan; no add-on.
19.e: "It suggests the category and subcategory together with priority and operator group."; "Accept them with one click while you stay fully in control."

20.n: AI creates a knowledge item from a solved call. Connecting it to the existing, scattered knowledge base (Notion, Outline) is not documented. Included in the plan; no add-on.
20.e: "The AI knowledge item generation feature automatically creates a knowledge item based on a solved call."

21.n: (reviewer correction: was "Meets"; the MCP server is read-only, so an external agent cannot act on tickets as rule 7 requires). Vendor MCP server on Excellent. Caveats: the first release is read-only and cannot create or change tickets. The docs use Microsoft Copilot Studio as the example; Claude is not named. On Essential and Engaged only the REST API is available, which would be Partial.
21.e: "The TOPdesk MCP server connects AI assistants, such as Microsoft Copilot Studio agents, to TOPdesk."; "If you subscribe to the Excellent package, this feature is available to you."; "We release the first version of the TOPdesk MCP server as read-only."

22.n: Only through a custom build on the TOPdesk Knowledge Base API. A marketplace search for "notion" returned nothing, and TOPdesk's AI uses only the TOPdesk knowledge base.
22.e: Marketplace search "notion": "No results were found matching your selection."; developer portal lists "Knowledge Base API"

23.p: Unknown (an integration, not a plan feature)
23.e: The pricing page lists "Slack" among "100+ standard integrations". A marketplace search for "slack" shows only "ITSAPI", "TicketBuddy" and "Zapier Integration Platform". Missing: there is no native TOPdesk Slack app (the docs cover a native Microsoft Teams app, not Slack). Two-way sync and private tickets created from Slack are not documented.

24.n: Documented REST APIs, inbound webhooks, outbound HTTP actions on field-level events, and a marketplace.
24.e: "We have different APIs for several aspects of TOPdesk" (Incident API, Knowledge Base API and others); "The API is free to use"; pricing: "Webhooks", "Customizable web hooks", "Marketplace with 90+ integrations"

25.n: SAML 2.0 SSO for agents is included in every plan; no separate subscription is needed. Missing: Google Workspace is not named as an IdP (the docs cover Entra ID and AD FS; other IdPs are in KI 5260 behind a login). Native 2FA is not documented: the operator login methods are TOPdesk, LDAP and SAML only.
25.e: "Single Sign On Included in Essential plan"; "Single Sign-on via SAML 2.0"; login methods: "TOPdesk Authentication … LDAP Authentication … SAML Single Sign On"

26.e: "TOPdesk SaaS has an SOC 2 certification, which is audited annually"; "TOPdesk is now ISO 27001 certified" (TOPdesk employee post, about Aug 2026); pricing lists "ISAE 3000", "GDPR compliant". Template DPA, sub-processor list, RTO/RPO and exit strategy are published. Caveats: I did not see the ISO certificate or its scope, and found no NIS2-specific page.

27.e: "Customers can choose where their environment is hosted"; EU locations EU1–EU6 (Netherlands, Ireland, Germany, Sweden) on Azure; "Off-site back-ups are stored on a different location within the same region"; "All TOPdesk SaaS environments are managed from the European Union". Missing: the AI processing location is not public; it is covered in the "TOPdesk AI Policy, which is available to customers through MyTOPdesk".

28.n: Attachments and emails are deleted automatically after a retention period per card type. For tickets, only the content (request, action, brief description, emails) is deleted; the call card itself stays. On SaaS, deletion schedules are set "with the help of TOPdesk Support".
28.e: "set how many days after closing or archiving a card its uploaded files and linked emails should be removed"; "TOPdesk can delete irrelevant card content after a chosen period of time. It removes … request, action, brief description and attached emails."

29.e: "Unlimited assets, tickets, and end users"; "An agent is someone who handles tickets … Users who simply view dashboards are free"; "Organizations … are not charged for operators with only this type of [free] permissions"

30.n: TOPdesk Robin in the portal answers from the knowledge base, links forms and submits a request for the user. Checking a request's status is not documented, and there is no Slack channel. Robin is included in Excellent. Live chat is an add-on for Engaged; Ebbot is an add-on (no prices).
30.e: "TOPdesk Robin for end users answers your employees' questions directly in the new Self-Service Portal"; "If one of those KIs has a linked form, they are also linked"; "click Submit a request from your conversation"

31.e: Pricing (Self-service): "Service catalogue", "Unlimited services", "Links to external sources" (Included in Essential plan)

32.n: A portal design can be applied per branch (a client is modelled as a branch), with its own logo and title. Layout is fixed. Quick setup from existing data is not documented.
32.e: "Select the branch(es) that will use the design"; "The layout (except tile size) is the same for all SSP designs."

33.n: A mobile app exists, but push or SMS alerting is not documented. An on-call tool can be reached only through a custom action sequence to its REST API. Notifications are built with events and action sequences.
33.e: "You can set up custom notifications via events and action sequences."; action sequences talk to "any other program that has a REST API"

34.n: Calls can be shared with other persons (requesters). Watchers among agents, and removing a participant afterwards, are not documented. Agents only see who has the card open.
34.e: "sharees can track the progress and update the call via the My Requests overview"; "See a message when another operator has a card open"

35.n: Only through a custom build (action sequences or REST API). No Notion or GitHub link integration was found; Azure DevOps is listed as a standard integration.
35.e: "use action sequences to let your TOPdesk communicate with a second TOPdesk or any other program that has a REST API"

36.n: The forms pages describe drag-and-drop components and "Customize question", with no mention of conditional or dependent fields.

37.e: "You drag and drop these components into the design area"; "You need permissions for setting up forms."

38.n: Publishing covers tiles and services only. Restricting a form to person groups is not documented.
38.e: No statement found ("link forms to services, or publish the form by adding it as a tile")

39.n: Through Change Management: a template creates activities, and each operator ticks them off with a planned final date. These are change activities, not calls.
39.e: "The form is linked to a template, making sure that the correct activities are created."; "Start, Resolve or Skip the activities by ticking the corresponding boxes"; list shows "the planned final date"

40.n: Visibility can be restricted by operator group, branch or category filter, but not per ticket. Exceptions apply, such as the last changer of a card.
40.e: "only view cards linked to their own or to specified operator groups"; "An operator can always view cards when … they are the last changer of the card"

41.n: Standard imports do not include calls. Routes: custom imports built by TOPdesk Consultancy or Support (price not listed), a Zapier template from Google Sheets rows, or the API.
41.e: "standard imports … such as information about branches, persons, hardware and software"; "TOPdesk Consultancy or Support can create customized import scripts"; Zapier: "Create TOPdesk incidents from new Google Sheets rows"

42.n: Recurring operational activities (Operations Management) and scheduled automated actions. These are activities, not calls.
42.e: "you can create recurrence patterns for activities … the activity occurs every month or every two weeks"; trigger type "On a schedule"

43.n: Through a custom action sequence (event on close, then an HTTP call to the register's API) or Zapier (Updated Incident trigger).
43.e: Zapier trigger "Updated Incident: Triggers when an Incident is updated."; action sequences reach "any other program that has a REST API"

44.n: The pricing page lists a monitor tool integration and Microsoft SCOM, without details. Other monitoring tools need inbound webhooks with an action sequence (custom) or Zapier (PagerDuty template). Pointing to a solution is not documented.
44.e: "With webhooks, you have an option to trigger an action straight from another system."; Zapier: "Create TOPdesk incidents for new or updated PagerDuty incidents"

45.n: Selections, overview filtering and custom reports exist. Filtering by requester, by period and by a custom amount field is not shown on a docs page I reviewed.
45.e: Pricing: "Selections", "Create your own reports", "Extensive overview filtering"

46.n: A separate Time Spent field and tab, not SLA time.
46.e: "On a number of card types you can register the time spent."

47.n: On Hold time is tracked, and date-based events can alert before a deadline. Personal reminders on a ticket are not documented.
47.e: "TOPdesk keeps track of how long calls have been On Hold"; events fire "when a card date will be reached within a particular period of time"

48.n: Not found for agents. Requesters see their own and shared calls in "My Requests" (K.O. #12 is also Unknown).

49.n: Persons can be imported from a file, a database or Entra ID (SCIM is also listed). Managers are flagged on person cards. Google Workspace sync and auto-filling the requester's manager are not documented.
49.e: "Import assets, persons, operators, branches, and locations from a file, a database, or Microsoft Entra ID."; "All persons who are tagged as managers on their Person cards can be assigned as authorizers"

50.e: Triggers "New Incident", "Updated Incident"; actions "Create an Incident", "Update Incident"

51.n: Only through a custom build on the TOPdesk Knowledge Base API or action sequences. No Outline integration was found (the marketplace was not searched for Outline). Outline's side was not verified.
51.e: Developer portal lists "Knowledge Base API{REST}" and "Knowledge Base APIGraphQL"

52.n: Only through a custom build on the TOPdesk REST API. The marketplace has no HubSpot app, and the Zapier app cannot create persons or branches (actions are incidents only).
52.e: Marketplace search "hubspot": "No results were found matching your selection."; Zapier write actions: "Create an Incident", "Update Incident"

53.n: Only through a custom build (time registration plus API or action sequences). No Productive integration was found (the marketplace was not searched). Productive's side was not verified.
53.e: "action sequences … communicate with … any other program that has a REST API"; time registration "grants insight into the duration of the work"

54.n: The marketplace app "Link TOPdesk => ServiceNow" only sends tickets out to ServiceNow, not in. The Collaboration Platform works only with partners who also use TOPdesk. Inbound from a client's tool needs webhooks or the API (custom).
54.e: "Will escalate calls from TOPdesk to ServiceNOW … Messages from ServiceNOW to TOPdesk are not included."; "operators can share call to partner organisations"

55.n: Native export of Plan Board appointments to Microsoft Exchange only. Ticket deadlines in Google Calendar are not documented.
55.e: "Any changes will be updated in the Operator's calendar automatically"; "Appointments exported to Microsoft Exchange"

56.n: Only through a custom build: an inbound webhook from Aboard triggering an action sequence. No Aboard integration was found (the marketplace was not searched). Aboard's side was not verified.
56.e: "With webhooks, you have an option to trigger an action straight from another system."

57.n: Deletion: manual or automatic anonymization of a person and linked cards. Export of a copy of a person's data is not documented.
57.e: "You can anonymize individual users and multiple users in bulk. These anonymizations can be triggered manually or they can be automatically executed by TOPdesk."

58.n: The region is chosen per environment, so per-client regions would need separate environments (instances). India is not offered.
58.e: "Customers can choose where their environment is hosted"; "Australia (AU), Brazil (BR), Canada (CA), the European Union (EU), Norway (NO), the United Kingdom (UK), and the United States of America (US)"

59.e: "Visualize the entire workload for your team"; "Show and reassign all tasks of one operator, e.g. yourself"

questions: #4: Can the requester get an automatic email at each approval step (approved or rejected by the manager, then by the department head) on a request for change? Is there a ready-made template for this, or must each event or action sequence be built?
#6: Do agents have @mentions or threaded internal comments on a call, beyond partial calls and invisible actions?

#10: Can an approval step be routed automatically to the requester's own line manager (from the person card), followed by a fixed department head? Can approvals run on calls (service requests), or only on requests for change?
#12: In the Self-Service Portal, does a requester see only their own and shared calls by default? Is there any setting that shows a whole branch's calls?
#17: Can audit trail entries be edited or deleted by anyone, including application managers or TOPdesk staff? Which fields are not tracked ("nearly all fields")? How long are entries kept?

#23: Is there an official two-way Slack integration (create a private ticket from a channel or slash command, sync replies and status both ways)? If it only works through Zapier or a partner, which partner and at what price?
#26: What is the scope of the ISO 27001 certificate (whole company or SaaS)? Can you send the certificate, the SOC 2 report and NIS2 supply-chain documentation?
#27: Where are the AI features processed (model provider and region)? Can AI processing be guaranteed to stay in the EU? Please send the TOPdesk AI Policy.
Pricing: Are the prices shown billed monthly or annually, and what is the minimum contract term? Which plan is the 30-day trial on?
#7: Does the audit trail record every change of operator and operator group on a call, with old value, new value, who changed it and when?
#8: Can each process (for example People, Finance, IT, or a client) have its own set of call statuses, or is there one status list for all calls?
#11: Does the main call show each partial call's status and progress trail? Can a partial call go to another team's operator group? Can first-line calls have partial calls?
#18: Can any AI feature use past calls (not only knowledge items) to suggest a solution or flag a similar earlier call?
#19: Can AI triage apply category, priority and operator group automatically to calls created by mail import, without an agent?
#21: When will the MCP server get write scopes (create or update calls)? Is any MCP client, such as Claude, supported with the user-delegated OAuth integration?
#22 / #51: Is there an official or partner way to sync or import a Notion or Outline knowledge base into the TOPdesk knowledge base, so that Robin and the answer assistant can use it?
#25: Is Google Workspace supported as a SAML IdP for operators? Is there a native 2FA option (for example TOTP) for TOPdesk authentication without an external IdP?
#28: Can whole closed call cards (not only their content and files) be deleted automatically after a retention period? Can the customer change the SaaS deletion schedule without Support?
#30: Can TOPdesk Robin for end users check the status of a user's existing request? Is Robin available in Slack?
#33: Does the TOPdesk Mobile app send push notifications for new or urgent calls? Is there an on-call tool integration (PagerDuty, Opsgenie)?
#36: Do Self-Service Portal forms support conditional or dependent questions (show, hide or filter options based on an earlier answer)?
#38: Can a form or service in the Self-Service Portal be limited to selected person groups (for example managers)?
#41: Can operators import calls from a CSV file themselves? If not, what does a customized import cost?
#48: Can an agent see all calls, changes and assets of one person in one place (person card)?
#49: Can persons and managers be synced from Google Workspace (SCIM or another route)? Is the requester's manager filled in automatically on a call?
#54: Is there any way to receive calls from a client's ServiceNow (or other tool) into TOPdesk, beyond a custom webhook build? What does the "Link TOPdesk => ServiceNow" app cost?
#57: Can TOPdesk export all data about one person for a GDPR access request?
#58: Can one environment keep different clients' data in different regions, or does each region need its own environment and licence? Is an India region planned?
Prices: What do Live chat, Ebbot and the WhatsApp channel cost? Is Live chat included in Excellent or an add-on (the pricing table says both)?
checks: Re-checked: Engaged €101 / Essential €71 / Excellent €143 per agent/month at 11 agents, EUR (https://www.topdesk.com/en/pricing/?pa=11&pv=eur).
Re-checked: ISO 27001 post is in TOPdesk's official community, “News and Announcements”, author marked “Employee”. Certificate and scope not seen.
Corrected #12 from “Meets” to “Unknown”: no explicit statement found; the original verdict was an inference.

Re-checked: "We release the first version of the TOPdesk MCP server as read-only. The AI agent can look up information in TOPdesk, but it can't create or change …" and "If you subscribe to the Excellent package, this feature is available to you." (https://docs.topdesk.com/en/topdesk-mcp-server.html).
Corrected #21 from "Meets" to "Partial": rule 7 needs an external agent that can read and act on tickets; the MCP server is read-only.

1.p: Growth (multiple support emails; Free allows one)
1.e: "Any email sent to your configured email ID will be automatically converted to Freshdesk tickets." "This behavior helps maintain the complete conversation history in a single ticket." "You can add multiple support emails from the Growth plan."

2.e: "You can add multiple support emails from the Growth plan." Per address: "Assign to group: Select the group (department/team) to which you want to assign the incoming tickets when addressed to this support email." Grid: "a shared inbox for your support team to collaborate and respond to incoming emails" (all plans).

3.e: "New Ticket Created Sends a notification to the requester when they submit a ticket."

4.e: "Requester notifications: Notifies customers about status changes and agent responses." The listed events are a public comment, solved and closed. **Missing:** there is no ticket approval flow (#10), so there are no approval-step notifications.

5.e: "Private note: Visible only to agents within your organization, as long as they have access."

6.p: Growth ("Threads and tasks"); Collaborators from Pro
6.e: Plan tooltip: "enabling internal conversation threads … Create tasks that are linked to a ticket". "tag agents on the Private Thread by ‘@’ mentioning the agents’ email IDs". Collaborators "(Available on Pro & Enterprise plans)".

7.e: "When a ticket is assigned, reassigned, or updated…" The Activities log captures "Changes to default fields (Type, Status, Priority, Group, Agent, Product, Source)". Note: this is the ticket Activities log. The Enterprise Audit Log does not cover tickets (K.O. #17).

8.e: "if you're on the Growth plan or higher, you can add custom choices that represent your support process." **Missing:** Status is a single account-wide field. Even with Workspaces (Enterprise), "Account-wide settings … including roles, ticket fields" apply to all workspaces. None of the pages read documents status sets per process or form.

9.e: "Multiple forms are available from the Pro plan onwards" (e.g. for "Different types of customer issues"). Custom fields are Growth+ and include "Date … deadlines" and dropdowns. A field can be "Required when submitting the ticket".

10.e: The only "Approval workflow" in the plan grid (Enterprise) is: "Create an approval workflow to review content before it gets published to your knowledge base." Collaborators can "assist … with … approvals", but none of the pages read documents an approval step, sequence or recorded decision on tickets.

11.e: "break down tickets into smaller sub-tickets … addressed simultaneously by different agents." The parent lists "Child ticket Status, Priority, Agent". A child in a group the agent cannot access is shown as "non-editable ticket (View-only)". A child can be added "Using a Template".

12.e: Indirect evidence only. Company-wide visibility is opt-in per contact: "click the Ticket icon to allow that contact to view all tickets from the company." There is also a "public ticket URL" that "does not require the customer to sign in". None of the pages read states the default visibility.

13.e: "Tickets in a group Agents and collaborators can view tickets assigned to their groups, as well as tickets directly assigned to them." The options also include "Groups where agents and collaborators can only view tickets".

14.e: Grid "Automations" (all plans): "Use specific time and event-based triggers to perform any action of your choice." Rules can call external systems: "Trigger Webhook … Update an external CRM". An official Zapier app exists (#50).

15.p: Growth (1 default policy); Pro (multiple policies, reminders)
15.e: "Establish specific first-response, every-response, and resolution-time targets for each priority level." Reminders are "available from Pro plan onwards". **Missing:** "You can set the reminder from 5 minutes to 4 hours", so a warning one day before a breach is not possible.

16.e: The plan grid lists "Standard reports and real-time dashboards" on all plans and custom dashboards from Pro. Metrics include "Unresolved tickets", first-response violation and resolution time "calculated from the time the ticket was created until the time the ticket was resolved".

17.e: "This feature focuses on What the change was Who made this change and When it was made." The modules covered are "Account Subscription Agent Authentication Automations Knowledge base". **Missing:** tickets and owner changes are not in the Audit Log. None of the pages read states that entries cannot be edited. There are no approvals to log.
