18.e: Grid (Copilot, Pro+): "Resolution assistant: Drive faster resolutions with similar ticket suggestor and solution article suggester." Similar Tickets: "automatically suggesting past, resolved tickets that are contextually similar". Paid add-on, not available on Growth.

19.p: Pro (listed as a Copilot feature, add-on USD 29/agent/month)
19.e: "Auto Triage can predict values for three default ticket fields(Priority, Group, and Type), custom dropdowns, and dependent (nested) fields." "Automatic … Freddy applies the value … immediately upon ticket creation." Prerequisite: "Freshdesk Pro/Enterprise". The Freddy feature list puts "Auto triage" under Freddy AI Copilot.

20.e: The Copilot add-on lets agents "Generate ticket summaries and solution articles." Writing Assistant: "Generate solution article" is available in the solution-article editor only, not in ticket replies. Without AI, Email-to-KBase can "convert your agents' ticket replies into solution articles" (drafts). **Missing:** AI drafting directly from a resolved ticket is not documented. Linking to the existing scattered KB (Notion, Outline) is not documented. AI Agents learn from "solution articles, web links, files, custom Q&As, or Workflows".

21.e: "The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk." The article gives setup steps for "Claude Code" and "Claude Desktop". Tools include "createTicket", "updateTicket" and "fetchSearchTickets". Authentication is "by using an API key only". Generally available since "September 10, 2026".

22.e: Route: **Zapier only**, e.g. the template "Create Notion database items for new Freshdesk tickets". The Freshworks "Notion MCP" app is "Supported for Freshdesk Omni Freshservice for Business Teams Freshservice", not Freshdesk. **Missing:** none of the pages read shows Notion content used as the knowledge base or in a client portal.

23.p: Not stated ("all plans providing API access")
23.e: "Both a Freshdesk agent and a Slack member who is not an agent on Freshdesk, can create tickets directly from the Slack interface." Replies in the channel thread are "added as a private note". "Ticket notes and replies from Freshdesk to Slack are restricted to 250 characters". **Missing:** notifications go to group-mapped team channels, not to a private requester–agent conversation. A requester's Slack reply becomes a private note. A non-agent "will not be able to update the ticket".

24.e: API v2 limits "Growth 100" calls/min ("Ticket Create - 50"). Webhooks: "Trigger Webhook … Update external systems when a ticket is created … or when a ticket is updated" (Growth, Pro, Enterprise). "Trigger API is applicable from Pro plan onwards." Marketplace: Freshworks Marketplace, e.g. "Connector Apps (13)".

25.p: Growth (SAML SSO on all plans; no separate subscription)
25.e: Grid: "Configure and provide SAML Single Sign On for your agents" (Growth, Pro, Enterprise). Org policy: "Freshworks login managed by a password policy or/and Google Login or/and SSO login … applicable to all admins/agents". "Users can also opt to configure two-factor authentication." Not verified: whether an admin can enforce 2FA (article from 2023).

26.e: Same Freshworks Trust Center as Freshservice: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, SOC 3 and DPA are public. SOC 1, SOC 2 Type 2, BCP, DR test summary and SIG/VSA are available on request. NIS2 is not mentioned.

27.e: "Our Data Centres are located in: US EEA UAE IND AU You can choose your preferred data location when you sign up". Backups are in the same region, and Copilot AI runs locally by default (see Freshservice #27). **Missing:** the same caveats as Freshservice #27 (data may be "shifted"; US backup mail provider; AI training opt-out by email). None of the pages read names the EU country.

28.e: "if you wish to automate the deletion of tickets … please use our 'Delete ticket' API. This API moves tickets to Trash, and Freshdesk will permanently delete the tickets after 30 days." The other option is a manual "bulk-delete action". **Missing:** none of the pages read documents a retention-period setting, so automatic deletion needs a custom script. Retention for attachments alone is not documented.

29.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; uniform #29 rule, no explicit "contacts are free" statement
29.e: Pricing is "/agent/month". Collaborators: "5,000 collaborators included" (Pro, Enterprise). Occasional agents need paid day passes. The pages read do not state explicitly that contacts are free or unlimited.

30.p: Growth (500 one-time AI Agent sessions; then USD 49/100)
30.e: "The Email AI Agent is available in both Freshdesk and Freshdesk Omni, while the Chat AI Agent is available only in Freshdesk Omni." Workflows: "Raise a complaint → collect issue details and create a ticket". **Missing:** in Freshdesk standalone there is no portal chat assistant and no Slack assistant documented. Checking a request's status is not documented.

31.e: "Publish multiple forms to your support portal." Grid "Customer portal": "Create a place for customers to submit tickets and self-serve information". **Missing:** the Freshdesk plan grid lists no service catalog. Linking from the portal to requests handled in other systems is not documented.

32.e: "A separate branded customer support portal for each product". "You can create up to 5 products on the Freshdesk Pro plan. On the Freshdesk Enterprise plan, you can create unlimited products." **Missing:** setting up a portal from data we already hold (e.g. HubSpot) is not documented. Also, "Unless segregated by automation rules, agents can see tickets from all products".

33.e: Mobile app: "You can receive notifications for … When tickets are assigned to your group or to you When new tickets are created". On-call tool integrations (e.g. PagerDuty) were not checked.

34.e: "Use the search bar to add other agents to the watch list. To remove yourself from a watch list, click the Minus symbol … You cannot remove other agents from the list." Collaborators (Pro+): "Invite external agents and third parties to help".

35.e: GitHub: **third-party marketplace app** "GitHub - Freshdesk Integration … Published by DevOps integration … FREE", which can "link existing Freshdesk tickets to existing GitHub issues". Notion: Zapier only (#22). None of the pages read shows a native structured-link field.

36.p: Pro (dynamic sections); dependent fields from Growth
36.e: "Dependent field … Category > Subcategory > Item. When a customer picks a category, the relevant subcategory dropdown appears." "Dynamic sections are available from the Pro plan onwards … groups of custom ticket fields that appear when a particular dropdown option is selected."

37.e: "Your form is created and you're taken to the form builder page." Fields are added by dragging: "Drag the Dependent field type into the main body." **Missing:** the steps start "As an admin, go to Admin > Workflows > Ticket Forms". Giving form editing to a non-admin business-team role is not documented.

38.e: Forms are published per portal or widget: "Select portals and widgets to associate the form with". None of the pages read restricts a form to a group of requesters.

39.e: Grid (Pro+): "Ticket templates: Create templates with pre-filled information like subject, description and ticket properties". A child ticket can be added "Using a Template". To-do widget: "Type a task … To mark an item as done, click the checkbox", with "Set Reminder". **Missing:** template checklist items with an owner and a due date for each step are not documented.

40.e: "Agents and collaborators can view tickets assigned to their groups, as well as tickets directly assigned to them." **Missing:** visibility is set per group or scope, not per ticket. None of the pages read hides a ticket from agents with global access.

41.e: None of the pages read documents a CSV import of tickets. Route: a script on the public API (Growth limit "Ticket Create - 50" calls/min) or the MCP tool "createTicket".

42.e: "As of now, we do not have the ability to schedule recurring tickets. However, as a workaround, you could make use of any third party event scheduler like Google Calendar to trigger an email to the support email address". Note: the article was last modified on 5 Jul 2017 and still lists the current plans.

43.e: Route 1: the native "Trigger Webhook" in ticket-update rules, which needs a receiving endpoint. Route 2: **Zapier**, e.g. the template "Add rows to Google Sheets from new Freshdesk tickets". A Zapier trigger on ticket close was not verified.

44.e: Route: the monitoring system sends email ("Any email sent to your configured email ID will be automatically converted to Freshdesk tickets") or calls the API ("Ticket Create"). Solution hints are possible via Copilot (#18). No monitoring-tool integration was checked.

45.e: Filters: "Customer details: Filter by Contacts and Companies", "Created: View tickets based on their creation date/time", "Custom fields: any dropdown and dependent fields", "custom date fields". **Missing:** number fields (amounts) are not listed as ticket-list filters. Reporting by a custom number field was not verified.

46.e: "Track the time spent on each ticket using the start/stop timer." Time Logs widget: "View the time logs tracked on the ticket." These are separate from the "SLA timers".

47.e: Hourly rules use "hours since an agent responded on a ticket or hours since the first response is due". A default view shows "My Overdue Tickets". To-do: "click the Set Reminder option, choose a date and time".

48.e: Contact page: "Tickets: This tab shows the tickets of the customer." Ticket sidebar: "Recent timeline Shows recent tickets by the requester".

49.e: None of the pages read documents Google Workspace directory sync or a manager field. The only directory connector seen is "Azure Active Directory Connector App Sync users from Azure Active Directory to Freshdesk" (paid connector tasks). Freshdesk has no ticket approvals (K.O. #10).

50.e: Official Zapier app "Freshdesk Integrations". Triggers include "New Ticket" and "New Ticket Note"; actions include "Create Company".

51.e: **Zapier only**: "Zapier seamlessly connects Freshdesk and Outline" (a "New Ticket" trigger can start a "Create Document" action in Outline).

52.p: Growth + connector app tasks (USD 80 per 5,000 tasks)
52.e: The Freshworks-published "Hubspot Connector App": "The app allows syncing of contacts and accounts." Also free: the Freshworks "Freshdesk-Hubspot" app, "Sync marketing contacts from Hubspot with your Freshdesk contacts", which runs "every 12 hours". Setting up a client portal from HubSpot data is not documented.

53.e: No Freshworks Marketplace app was found, and the Zapier pairing page https://zapier.com/apps/freshdesk/integrations/productive returned 404. Route: a custom build on the Freshdesk REST API. The Productive side was not verified.

54.e: The Freshworks "ServiceNow Connector App" is "Supported for Freshservice for Business Teams Freshservice", not Freshdesk. Route for Freshdesk: email-to-ticket from the client's tool, or a custom build on the REST API.

55.e: **Zapier only**: "Freshdesk + Google Calendar". The most popular template is "Create Freshdesk tickets for new Google Calendar events", which runs in the opposite direction. Ticket deadlines appearing in calendars was not verified.

56.e: No Aboard integration was seen. The Freshworks Marketplace and Zapier were not searched for Aboard. Route: Aboard events call the Freshdesk ticket-create API or email a support address. The Aboard side was not verified.

57.e: Delete: "'Delete forever' … will permanently delete customer information in the system and tickets/chats/calls they were part of." Export: contact export, plus a "Customer ticket export" via the "Contacts dropdown" filter and "Export". Or "use the Freshdesk API call to export all the tickets of a customer". These are manual admin steps; automation would go through the API.

58.e: "Our Data Centres are located in: US EEA UAE IND AU You can choose your preferred data location when you sign up". The region is set per account, so a different region for a client needs a **separate Freshdesk account**.

59.e: Default views: "My Open and Pending Tickets", "Open Tickets in My Groups". Saved views can be "Personal" or "Shared". Layouts: "Card, Inbox, and Table View". No Kanban board was seen.

questions: Freshdesk #12 (Unknown). Question: "With no company-wide 'Ticket' toggle and no public ticket URL placeholder, can a contact see any ticket in the portal other than those they requested or are CC'd on? Can the public ticket URL be disabled for the whole account?"
Freshdesk #23. Question: "Which Freshdesk plans include the API access the Slack app requires?"
#26. Question: "Do you provide NIS2-specific supply-chain documentation or contract clauses (incident notification times, Art. 21 measures)?"

#27. Question: "In which EU country are EU-region accounts hosted? Can all US-only sub-processors (e.g. SendGrid backup mail) be disabled for an EU account? Under what conditions is data 'shifted' out of the region?"
Freshdesk #10. Question: "Is there any native or Marketplace multi-step ticket approval (manager, then department head) with recorded decisions?"
#8: "Can different ticket forms, products or workspaces have their own set of statuses, or is the Status field always shared across the account?"

#19: "Does Auto Triage need Freddy AI Copilot licences? If so, for which agents?"

#25: "Can an admin enforce 2FA for all agents, and does Google Login count as satisfying 2FA?"
#31: "Does Freshdesk have a service catalog, or can the portal list links to requests handled in other systems?"

Plans: "Is the Freshdesk Free plan still offered? The pricing page on 2026-11-18 shows only Growth, Pro and Enterprise."
checks: Re-checked: the only Freshdesk “Approval workflow” is for knowledge-base content (pricing page data).
Re-checked: Freshservice “Send Approval Mail to Reporting Manager” (hierarchical approvals article).
Re-checked: Freshservice accounts in “Managed Services (MSP)” mode have different rules (multiple requester portals article).

Corrected Freshdesk #29 from “Meets” to “Unknown” under the uniform #29 rule in analysis/01_ko_criteria.md: the pricing page (including collapsed FAQ text) has no explicit statement that contacts are free or unlimited.

Re-checked: "The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk", with tools "createTicket" and "updateTicket" (MCP article). #21 Meets stands: an external agent can read and act on tickets.
#42 "Does not meet" rests on an official article last modified in 2017 that is still published; the date is noted in the row. Confirm with the vendor.

1.p: Professional (Help Desk is listed under Professional; I did not check whether Starter's conversations inbox meets this)
1.e: "Team email: Connect a shared email address to automatically create tickets from incoming emails. Your team can view, manage, and reply to emails in help desk." History tab "displays all related activity, including when the ticket was created, status changes…"

2.n: Each team email channel sets its own pipeline and assignment. The pages I checked state no limit on the number of team addresses.
2.e: "When you connect a team email address, such as support@mycompany.com, HubSpot automatically creates a ticket for each incoming email." Admins "can also set default email addresses for teams". "Tickets are automatically assigned to available users who have the fewest open tickets of the same ticket type".

3.e: "Service Hub Professional and Enterprise users can use this action to send automated emails when a ticket is received or closed." It is built as a workflow and is not on by default.

4.e: The automated requester email is documented only "when a ticket is received or closed". The Send Email action otherwise sends "marketing emails that have been saved for automation". Agent replies go to the requester by email, and the agent can "reply and update the ticket status in a single action". Missing: no documented Service Hub-only email to the requester on other status changes, and no approval steps to notify (see #10).

5.e: "Use Notes to notify another team member of the conversation. This note will not be visible to the contact."

6.e: "Type @ and your team member's name… A notification will be sent to the team member with a link to the conversation." The default views include "My Mentions" and "Following". Pipeline automation can "Create and assign a task: creates a task associated with the record". Caveat: threaded replies to notes are documented only through the Slack sync.

7.n: Owner history is visible on the ticket. Audit-log limits are covered in K.O. #17 (Partial).
7.e: "click the Ticket owner, Assigned Teams, Priority, Category, or Status fields at the top of the ticket"; "To view a history of the record's owners, click the History tab".

8.n: Each pipeline (process) has its own statuses. Limits: Starter 15, Professional 100, Enterprise 350 custom pipelines.
8.p: Starter (custom pipeline); the Help Desk workspace needs Professional
8.e: "Tickets: a default Support Pipeline with four ticket statuses: New, Waiting on contact, Waiting on us, Closed". "To add a new stage: Under the existing stages, click + Add stage. Enter a stage name." "A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create a custom pipeline."

9.e: "form submissions automatically create tickets"; each form sets "Ticket pipeline, Ticket status, and Ticket priority"; "To add a ticket property… click Add another property". Field types include "Dropdown select" and "Date picker: stores a date value". "Make this field required: …the field must be completed" (this quote is from the legacy forms editor article).

10.e: "Approvals are supported in the following areas of HubSpot": quotes, content, exports and "Require approvals for deals (Sales Hub Enterprise)". Tickets are not listed. The deal approval page is limited to "Sales Hub Enterprise".

11.n: Tickets can be linked to tickets, and workflows can spawn tickets. Missing: no documented parent/child view showing sub-ticket status and history on the parent ticket. The ticket-to-ticket link is shown here only in the API docs.
11.e: "452 Ticket to ticket" (default association type). Workflow actions: "Copy ticket Copy details of an existing ticket record to a new ticket"; "Create record … Tickets (Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)".

12.e: "Only tickets they're associated with: when a contact logs into the support portal, only the tickets that are associated with their contact record will appear."

13.e: "A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to assign team only permission… users can only view, edit, or delete records where they or another user on their team are the owner. If a user is on multiple teams, they can access records assigned to any of their teams." Missing: there is no documented restriction by client (company). Access follows the owner's team, so it does not follow the client project. Help Desk spaces (Enterprise) "display tickets assigned to main team members within selected HubSpot teams", which is a view, not a permission.

14.n: If/then workflows are built in, and an official Zapier app exists (#50).
14.e: "Branches Use branches to direct your enrolled record down specific workflow paths based on set criteria". The page is available with "Service Hub Professional, Enterprise".

15.p: Professional (Enterprise is needed for combinations of properties)
15.e: Goals for "Time to first reply, Time to next reply, Time to close"; "Set SLA goals based on priority, team, source, or pipeline"; "Mark as due soon". A workflow can alert on "due soon, or overdue" by "internal email notification, an in-app notification, or a Slack notification".

16.e: "Today's team summary: view key metrics, including the number of open and closed tickets, Time to first reply, Time to close, and CSAT". Reports include "First reply average over time" and "Time to close average over time". Queue views include "Unassigned" and "My Team's Open".

17.e: In the audit-log table, "CRM objects" (including Tickets), "Property value updates", "Pipeline changes" and "Approvals" are ticked for Professional and Enterprise but not Starter. "The log only records HubSpot-user based actions" and "All Logs: all log categories within the last 30 days." Missing: no statement that entries cannot be edited; retention beyond the 30-day view is not stated; automated changes (e.g. form submissions) are not logged. The article's own text contradicts its table ("Starter or Professional account will be able to filter by Login or Security Activity").

18.n: Included in the plan with no credits, but it needs a Service Seat. Missing: no documented analysis of past tickets and no "similar problem before" flag. Suggestions use only synced content and the current conversation.
18.e: "Reply recommendations are based on the content sources you sync with the customer agent. The agent analyzes both the context from the conversation and your synced content". "Using reply recommendations does not consume HubSpot credits."

19.n: AI sets the Category (and Language) property. Routing is rule-based: workflows act on those AI-set properties, and no autonomous AI router is documented. The catalog rate sheet lists no credit rate for this feature.
19.e: "This property is automatically set using AI by analyzing the first message of the ticket". "A Service Hub Enterprise subscription is required to use the Category and Language properties". "Use these insights across the platform in workflows and reporting".

20.n: Paid add-on: 200 HubSpot Credits per generated article; the feature is in BETA. Missing: no link to the existing scattered knowledge (Notion, Outline). It works only inside one HubSpot knowledge base at a time.
20.e: "The knowledge base agent uses your closed support tickets to identify gaps and generate article drafts, then analyzes your existing articles to surface suggested edits". "Knowledge Base Agent (Beta) Generate one new knowledge base article 200".

21.n: HubSpot provides an MCP server and a Claude connector. The connector needs a paid Anthropic plan.
21.p: All tiers (connector). Help Desk read needs Service Hub Starter or higher
21.e: MCP server: "enables an agent to read, write, and update HubSpot records (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and more)". Connector: "Works on all HubSpot tiers"; "Write: create/update contacts, companies, deals, tickets"; "Help Desk (read) Service Hub Starter, Pro, & Enterprise".

22.n: The only route is HubSpot's own Notion Data Sync app, which needs Data Hub Starter and a Notion subscription. It syncs Notion database records with CRM objects, including Tickets. Missing: no documented use of Notion pages as knowledge-base content in the support portal, the customer agent or reply recommendations.
22.e: "Notion Data Sync - Sync Notion data with HubSpot Built by HubSpot". "This app requires a paid subscription to Data Hub Starter." Data sources: "Custom Objects Contacts Companies Deals Tickets".

23.p: All plans for creating a ticket from Slack; Professional for Help Desk ticket sync
23.e: "You can create a HubSpot task, ticket, or note from a Slack message". With the sync, "Ticket details updated in Slack will automatically be updated in HubSpot, and vice versa", but "only comments in the automatically created Ticket synced to external tools note… will be synced to Slack". Missing: no documented private conversation between requester and agent in Slack, no /support command, and Slack is not among the Help Desk channel types. It is not documented whether people without a HubSpot user can create tickets.

24.n: (reviewer correction: was "Meets"; the fine-grained webhook evidence is from a BETA API; only generally available features get Meets). Webhooks can be filtered by object, action and property, but that example is in the BETA "Webhooks journal" API. The pages do not state the lowest plan for API access.
24.p: Not stated on the pages checked

25.n: SSO is included in any Professional or Enterprise hub; I found no separate SSO subscription. Google appears among the identity providers. The page does not state the plan for 2FA.
25.e: "Available with … Service Hub Professional, Enterprise". Identity providers: "Okta OneLogin Microsoft Entra ID … Google". "Can I turn on two-factor authentication, required two-factor authentication, SSO, and required SSO at the same time? Yes".

26.e: Trust Center badges: "SOC 1 Type II SOC 2 Type II SOC 3 HIPAA GDPR CCPA EU Cloud Code of Conduct TRUSTe Certified Privacy TX-RAMP". HubSpot's own knowledge base says: "While HubSpot itself is not currently ISO 27001 certified, our infrastructure provider—AWS—maintains ISO 27001 certification". Missing: HubSpot has no ISO 27001 certificate of its own, and I found no NIS2-specific documentation on the public Trust Center page (most documents are gated).

27.p: Any paid plan (data centre is changeable on paid plans)
27.e: "hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in… European Union (Germany)". Backups: "replicated for disaster recovery and back-up purposes within your regional Hosting Location". Missing: "Analytics and Usage Data… will be transferred from the hosting location to the United States"; "Sub-Processors might process your data… outside the hosting location"; AI processing is shown per provider on the sub-processor page, which I did not check. Terms: "WE MAKE NO WARRANTY THAT A SPECIFIC HOSTING LOCATION WILL MEET YOUR DATA RESIDENCY REQUIREMENTS". The data centre is assigned "based on the geolocation of your IP address at sign-up", so the existing account's location is unknown.

28.n: Automatic deletion exists only for inactive contacts. Missing: I found no retention period or automatic deletion for tickets or attachments. The workflow delete action covers contacts only.
28.e: "turn on the setting to automatically delete data for inactive contacts"; the page title is "Manage data retention policy settings for inactive contacts". Workflow action: "Delete contact Automatically delete enrolled contacts".

29.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets (inferred from the seat model)"
29.e: Seats apply to users: "Every user on a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is assigned a seat". Requesters are contacts: "when a contact logs into the support portal…"; "grant specific contacts access using access groups". View-Only seats are "free and unlimited". No page says outright that contacts never cost anything.

30.n: The customer agent answers on chat, email and forms, at 50 credits per resolved conversation. Missing: Slack is not a customer-agent channel. Breeze Assistant in Slack is for HubSpot users, not requesters. Pointing people to the right form, checking request status and opening tickets on someone's behalf are not documented.
30.e: "you can assign it to Facebook, WhatsApp, SMS, calling (BETA), live chat, form, or email channels". "ask questions about your HubSpot records directly in Slack using Breeze Assistant".

31.n: A login-protected support portal with a support form exists. Missing: no catalog of request types and no links out to other systems (for example Aboard).
31.e: "A support portal is a login-protected space where customers can access and manage their support tickets"; "add a support form".

32.n: Company-level ticket visibility exists. Enterprise allows 25 knowledge bases with private access groups. Missing: a separate branded portal per client is not documented, and the portal page describes one support portal.
32.e: "any tickets that are associated with their primary company record … will appear". Enterprise: "25 knowledge bases per account"; "Up to 100 access groups for private knowledge base (limit shared with customer portal)". "Multiple language support portals are not supported at this time".

33.n: The mobile app sends push notifications, and SLA alerts can go by email, in-app or Slack (K.O. #15). Missing: ticket- or SLA-specific mobile push is not stated explicitly. I found no SMS to agents and no on-call tool integration (marketplace search was not usable).
33.e: "You can turn on and troubleshoot push notifications on your iOS or Android device, so you never miss important updates from the HubSpot mobile app."

34.n: Users can follow tickets themselves. Others are added or removed through a user-type property, such as a "Collaborator" property.
34.p: Professional (Help Desk follow); user properties on all plans
34.e: "you can follow tickets and receive notifications when there's new activity on a ticket". "you may want to create a "Point of contact" or "Collaborator" property … Users selected for this property will be treated as record owners".

35.n: HubSpot's own Notion Data Sync (needs Data Hub Starter) syncs Notion records with Tickets. Missing: no GitHub integration found (marketplace search was not usable). Links to other systems were not verified.
35.e: "Notion Data Sync - Sync Notion data with HubSpot Built by HubSpot"; "Two-way sync: Data is shared between Notion and HubSpot in real time".

36.n: Missing: the only evidence is the legacy forms editor article, which is "a reference for existing forms built with the legacy editor only". The updated editor was not verified, and changing a field's options based on another field is not documented.
36.e: "Dependent fields: display additional fields based on visitors' responses to a previous field".

37.n: Forms are built in the UI, and access is controlled by a permission.
37.e: "Select an existing form or set up a new form"; "To add a ticket property that isn't listed, click Add another property". "Edit forms permissions are required to create or edit a form".

38.n: Access groups apply to the whole portal (and to private knowledge-base content). Per-form visibility is not documented.
38.e: Portal only: "Access group membership required: grant specific contacts access using access groups".

39.n: Tasks with an owner and due date can be created automatically per stage, and playbooks exist on Professional. Missing: no ticket template with a checklist that each person ticks off.
39.e: "Create and assign a task: creates a task associated with the record when it enters the pipeline stage. Configure the details of the action (e.g., name, assignee, due date)". Pricing: "Create up to 5,000 playbooks".

40.n: Access is set per user (owned only, team only) and per pipeline. Missing: no per-ticket access list.
40.e: "Their [object name]: only manage their owned records for the object". "A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to restrict a pipeline by team"; "Manage access: manage which users can view and edit the pipeline".

41.e: "Import records for multiple objects to add or update data across different objects"; "Select the unique value property (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, custom objects only)".

42.n: A scheduled workflow plus the "Create record" (Tickets) action.
42.e: "You can set a workflow to recur just once, or on an annual, monthly, weekly, or daily schedule"; "This enrollment trigger type can be used across all workflow object types". "Create record … Tickets (Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)".

43.e: "Use the Create Google Sheet row action or Update data in a Google Sheet action to send data from HubSpot properties to your spreadsheet." Page availability: "Service Hub Professional, Enterprise".

44.n: Possible routes: monitoring alerts sent by email to a team email channel, the custom channels API, or a custom build on the public API. Missing: no native monitoring integration, and no documented step that points to a solution.
44.e: "Team email: Connect a shared email address to automatically create tickets from incoming emails". "Custom channels: Connect external messaging apps using integrations from the HubSpot Marketplace or the custom channels API".

45.n: Custom views need a Service Seat.
45.e: "Click the Filtering on dropdown menu and select an object (Ticket, Associated Company or Contact)"; "Select and configure any ticket properties you'd like to filter on". Reports: "add, edit and remove filter criteria and data sources".

46.n: No official page I checked documents native time tracking on tickets. SECONDARY (search-result summaries only, not opened): community threads and third-party apps (for example PSOhub) suggest it is not native.

47.n: Waiting time and SLA alerts are documented. Missing: a reminder set by hand on a ticket is not documented; I found only tasks with due dates.
47.e: "Cumulative time in [status ID]: the cumulative time spent by the ticket in the status". SLA statuses: "Due soon, Overdue". Tasks: "(e.g., name, assignee, due date)".

48.n: A view filtered by the associated contact shows all of that person's requests.
48.e: "Click the Filtering on dropdown menu and select an object (Ticket, Associated Company or Contact)".

49.n: Contact-to-contact association labels can model the company structure. Missing: no sync from an HR system and no automatic fill of the requester's manager.
49.e: "A pair of labels … (e.g., Manager and Employee, Parent and Child…)"; "up to 50 labels per object pair (e.g., Contact to Deal, Contact to Contact)".

50.e: Zapier: "Connect HubSpot to 9,000+ apps Supported triggers and actions". HubSpot Marketplace: "Zapier By HubSpot 167K installs".

51.n: The only route is Zapier: Outline has a Zapier app. No native integration was found.
51.e: Outline on Zapier: "New Document Triggers when a new document is published."

52.n: Same CRM: tickets use HubSpot contacts and companies natively, and the portal can show a client company's tickets.
52.e: "To associate a company or contacts with the ticket, click the Company and Contact dropdown menus". Portal: "any tickets that are associated with their primary company record … will appear".

53.n: Productive's official integration syncs deals, companies and contacts and needs Productive's Ultimate plan. Missing: tickets and time logging are not part of that sync. A Zapier route was seen in search results but not opened (zapier.com/apps/hubspot/integrations/productiveio).
53.e: "integrate it with Productive to have your deals, companies, and contacts synced with Productive". "HubSpot integration is available on the Ultimate subscription plan."

54.n: Routes: Zapier, or a client's tool sending email to a team email channel. No native integration was found.
54.e: Zapier: "When an existing record in ServiceNow is updated, Zapier automatically syncs the changes to a corresponding custom object or record in HubSpot".

55.n: Tasks sync one way to Google or Outlook Calendar. Missing: ticket deadlines (for example SLA due dates) are not synced. Note: the page lists Service Hub Starter but also requires "an assigned Sales or Service seat".
55.p: Starter listed (needs a Sales or Service Seat)
55.e: "any new task you create in HubSpot will appear as a 15-minute event at the task's due date and time."

56.n: No official integration found. The Zapier URL for Aboard returned 404. A custom build on HubSpot's ticket API would depend on Aboard's own API, which I did not check.

57.n: Permanent deletion is manual, one contact at a time. Missing: no automation, export of a person's data was not verified, and the effect on ticket content is not stated.
57.e: "Permanent deletions can only be performed on individual contact records. You cannot perform permanent deletions in bulk using segments of contacts or workflows".

58.n: There is one hosting location per account, so per-client regions would need separate HubSpot accounts. India is not among the listed regions.
58.e: "hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in the United States (East and West regions), Canada, Australia, and European Union (Germany)"; "view where your HubSpot data is hosted".

59.e: "You can choose from Table, Split or Board layouts". "My Team's Open: all Open tickets assigned to you or another member of your team".

questions: #10: "Is native multi-step approval for tickets (manager, then department head, with decisions recorded) on the roadmap or in beta? Is a workflow-based workaround supported?"
#4: "With Service Hub Professional alone (no Marketing Hub), can a ticket workflow send a custom email to the requester on any status change, not only 'received' or 'closed'?"

#23: "Is there a native Slack intake channel for Help Desk (help channel or slash command) that creates a private requester↔agent ticket and syncs public replies to Slack? Can Slack users without a HubSpot user create tickets with 'Create a ticket'?"
#13: "Can ticket visibility be restricted per client (company or project) independent of the owner's team? Are unassigned tickets in Help Desk visible to all teams?"

#17: "Are audit-log entries immutable? What is the retention for CRM object and property-value entries (the UI shows 30 days)? For Professional, does the table (CRM objects ticked) or the prose (Login/Security only) apply?"
#26: "Do you have, or plan, ISO 27001 certification for HubSpot itself? Which Trust Center documents support a NIS2 supply-chain assessment (incident notification timelines, security overview)?"
#27: "Where is our existing HubSpot account hosted, and can it be migrated to the EU data centre? Which sub-processors, including AI providers, process EU-hosted data outside the EU/EEA?"
#15: "Can 'Mark as due soon' be set to one day before the SLA deadline?"
#29: "Are contacts (requesters) ever billed in Service Hub, for example through contact tiers?"

Pricing: "What are the EUR prices? Which shown price ($90 or $100, $7 or $20) applies to which billing option? With our existing hubs, what would Core and Service Seats cost? Is a Service Hub Professional trial or sandbox available?"
#38 (Unknown): "Can a form in the support portal or knowledge base be shown only to a specific access group (for example managers), while other forms stay visible to everyone?"
#46 (Unknown): "Does Service Hub have native time tracking on tickets (time logged per agent, separate from SLA time)? If not, which marketplace app do you recommend?"
#56 (Unknown): "Is there any integration (native, marketplace or Zapier) with the HR system Aboard, so that a new hire or leaver creates a ticket?"
#11: "Can agents link a ticket to another ticket in the Help Desk UI, as parent and child, and see the child tickets' statuses and history on the parent ticket?"
#18: "Can reply recommendations or the customer agent use past resolved tickets as a source, and flag that a similar ticket was solved before?"
#20: "Can the knowledge base agent use external sources (Notion, Outline) or only HubSpot tickets and articles? When will it leave beta?"
#22: "Can Notion pages be used as content sources for the knowledge base, the support portal or the customer agent, not only Notion database rows through Data Sync?"
#28: "Can a retention period with automatic deletion be set for tickets, conversations and attachments, not only for inactive contacts?"
#30: "Can the customer agent run in Slack for employees, check a ticket's status and create a ticket on the requester's behalf?"
#32: "Can one account run several branded support portals, one per client company?"
#33: "Does the mobile app send push notifications for new, assigned or SLA-breaching Help Desk tickets? Is there a native on-call or SMS alert for agents?"
#36: "Does the updated forms editor support conditional (dependent) fields and option filtering, as the legacy editor did?"
#40: "Can a single ticket be restricted to its owner and a named manager, without restricting the whole pipeline?"
#47: "Can an agent set a reminder on a ticket, other than by creating a task?"
#55: "Can ticket SLA due dates appear in agents' Google Calendar? Does the task calendar sync work on Service Hub Starter without a Service Seat?"
#57: "Can a data subject export (a copy of all data about a contact, including tickets and conversations) be produced automatically? Does a permanent contact delete also remove the ticket content?"
#58: "Can different clients' data be hosted in different regions inside one account? Is an India data centre planned?"
#24: "Which plans include API access and webhooks? When will the webhooks journal API leave beta?"
#2: "Is there a limit on the number of team email addresses connected to Help Desk on Professional?"
checks: Re-checked: “While HubSpot itself is not currently ISO 27001 certified, our infrastructure provider—AWS—maintains ISO 27001 certification” (hosting FAQ).
Corrected #29 from “Meets (inferred)” to “Unknown”: no page states that contacts are never billed.
Re-checked: the remote MCP server "enables an agent to read, write, and update HubSpot records (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and more)" (developer docs). #21 Meets stands.
Corrected #24 from "Meets" to "Partial": the fine-grained webhook evidence is from the BETA "Webhooks journal" API; same generally-available rule as Zendesk #21 and Zoho #11.

1.p: Not stated (email is not listed on the pricing page; Pro is the lowest plan)
1.e: "you can respond to customers directly from Slack. This means you never need to open Outlook or Gmail again"; "the message will be sent to the customer in the same email thread". Web inbox: "By default the audit trail is enabled" … "status changes, assignments, and other ticket changes inline with the thread". Note: emails are posted to an internal Slack channel; a Slack reply needs "/unthread send" when that setting is on.

2.p: Not stated (the pricing page does not list email)
2.e: Inboxes are added with "New Email Inbox", and each has its own setup: "Inbound emails can have their own assignment rules". Emails are matched to clients: "Email conversations will automatically be linked to customers based on domain." Pickup by whoever is available: round robin and "Away Tracking", where away users "will be skipped over in a round-robin rotation". Note: email is posted only to an internal Slack channel ("not a Slack Connect or shared channel").

3.p: Not stated (Pro is the lowest plan)
3.e: "a way to automatically respond to new customer messages in a Slack channel, email, or in-app chat request". "For Email Head to “Channels” > “Email” … You’ll see the option to enable the autoresponder from there."

4.p: Not stated (Pro is the lowest plan)
4.e: Replies reach the requester: "the message will be sent to the customer in the same email thread". Slack Private Mode: "all ticket activity will be routed to requestors Messages tab of the Unthread App". Approvals: "The sender will be notified of your response." **Missing:** no explicit statement that the requester is notified of each status change (the email channel especially) or of each approval step. Possible only as a custom build in Automations (trigger "Conversation updated").

5.p: Not stated (Pro is the lowest plan)
5.e: "By default, all comments in this thread are private and not shared with the customer." Web: "If you’ve enabled triaging, you can also add private notes about a conversation into the respective triage channel."

6.p: Not stated (Pro is the lowest plan)
6.e: Triage = "a private thread about a customer issue"; "any user tagged will be notified"; Standard role: "can see tickets and leave responses". Triage message shows "Any linked tasks". **Missing:** no native tasks inside a ticket are documented. Only linked external tasks (for example Jira, via the external-tasks API) or a checklist built from checkbox custom fields ("visible to agent only").

7.e: "Change assignee: Shift + 🅰". On the conversation page: "By default the audit trail is enabled … to see status changes, assignments, and other ticket changes inline with the thread." Note: the separate Audit Logs page is "only available on the Enterprise plan" and lists account and configuration events, not ticket changes.

8.e: "Within each Status custom sub-statuses can be added for more granular status tracking. … Within a Project go to the Setup page and select Statuses". Requester-facing statuses can also be added. Note: custom statuses are sub-statuses under the fixed Open / In Progress / On Hold / Closed. Projects are per team ("one project for 'IT' and another for 'HR'").

9.p: Not stated (Pro is the lowest plan)
9.e: "Ticket types can each have their own unique properties"; types include "Single-select", "Date"; "Required (indicating whether the field must be filled for a ticket to be created)"; "ticket types are configured on a per-project basis". Portal: "ticket type–level conditional visibility rules" (for example "customers on certain plans").

10.e: "Approval Requests will automatically DM that person with an easy way to give approval, leave comments, or make a note about why the request was rejected." "Add an approval step to your assignment rules". Automation trigger: "Approval request response received". **Missing:** no documented built-in chain (requester's manager, then department head) and no automatic lookup of the requester's manager. Chaining only by building Automations (custom build). Audit logs do not list approval decisions.

11.e: "Escalations allow you to control how tickets move up or across teams". An escalation has its own assignee and Acknowledge/Resolve steps, and "Escalations are considered a separate thread from the conversation". API: "Create a related to, blocking, or tracking link to a conversation" and "Transfer Conversation … to another project". **Missing:** none of the pages read shows a linked ticket created in another team's project queue (for example HR onboarding → IT equipment) with sub-ticket status visible on the parent. Escalation paths are set up inside one project.

12.e: Slack bot: "All conversations are by default private between the user and ticket assignees". Portal: "Users can view their submitted tickets". Seeing all of an account's tickets is an opt-in role: "Account Admins have permission to view all tickets submitted by users within their account". Not verified: tickets the user was only added to. In Slack help channels, privacy needs the bot DM or "Private Mode to limit ticket visibility".

13.p: Not stated for Projects; Custom RBAC = Business
13.e: "“Restricted” means only users within the project are able to see tickets. This is a commonly used setting for teams like HR." Admin "cannot view tickets in private Projects that they are not a member of". **Missing:** per-client separation inside the Platform desk is not documented. "Custom RBAC permissions" is listed only from Business. An org Owner "can see all ticket data".

14.e: "The Automations feature empowers you to build custom workflows through built-in Unthread actions, 3rd party integrations, and custom code." Triggers include "Conversation created", "Conversation updated" and "Scheduled", with filters on "ticket type, status, customer, assignee". Note: "Automations need to be enabled for trial accounts."

15.e: "apply different targets by priority"; metrics "First Response" and "Resolution"; "Warning: The number of minutes after the timer starts when the SLA should be considered at risk."; "Yellow: Due soon or past the configured warning time."

16.e: "Track response times, resolution times, and overall team efficiency"; "Use the board builder to create custom dashboards". Queue: "You can choose between a Kanban or a List view for your conversations".

17.e: "Note: this feature is only available on the Enterprise plan." It "captures key account and configuration events" (login, users, projects, automations, settings). Ticket view: "By default the audit trail is enabled" … "status changes, assignments, and other ticket changes inline with the thread". **Missing:** approvals are not in the audit log event list; the ticket audit trail does not say who made each change; nothing says entries cannot be edited.

18.p: Not stated (AI is included; no add-on price found)
18.e: "Unthread AI can recommend a response to a question based on your existing documentation … Suggest the response privately to the support rep". "Surface Similar Conversations … You will be able to see the previous conversation's question & resolution".

19.e: "When Auto Set Ticket Type is enabled … the ticket type will be set automatically." "Unthread AI [can] automatically apply tags". "Agentic AI automatically tags, categorizes, and routes tickets to the right person or team". Routing by type: "if they select a 'Laptop Replacement', you can configure the request to be sent directly to the IT team".

20.p: Business ("Self-learning documentation"); KB sync is in Pro
20.e: "As you close out a conversation … the system automatically detect if the answer is not yet captured in your knowledge base. If not, we'll generate a draft article using AI". Existing scattered knowledge: "Supported native integrations: Google Drive Notion Confluence … SharePoint … GitHub".

21.e: Vendor MCP server: "Unthread supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP)". Write tools: "update_conversation … create_conversation_comment … create_approval_request". "As of 4/16/26 Unthread is an official Anthropic Partner". A separate Portal MCP can "Create a ticket". Claude can also be the built-in model: "Supported models: … Anthropic Claude". No beta label was seen.

22.e: Notion is a native KB source ("Supported native integrations: Google Drive Notion …"). Portal: "Republish your docs in a branded support portal … powered by the same knowledge base your AI uses." Per audience: "Who can read: When user groups are selected here the article visibility will be limited to these user groups."

23.e: Native Slack app. "All conversations are by default private between the user and ticket assignees". "Messages sent from the web inbox will be posted into Slack with your name and photo." "Customers can also close out their own issues … which will close it out on your end as well." Users "get notifications about conversations".

24.e: "Everything in Unthread is driven by our powerful API." There is a REST API with service-account keys, plus "100+ native integrations". **Missing:** webhooks are not fine-grained. "The following event types are supported: 'conversation_created' 'conversation_updated' 'conversation_deleted' 'message_created'". The integrations page is a vendor-built list, not an open third-party app marketplace.

25.e: "Unthread supports Single Sign-On (SSO) to allow your team to log in using your existing identity provider (Google, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, etc.)". Google Workspace works via OIDC or SAML. The audit log lists "Auth method changes (password/Google sign-in toggled)". **Missing:** no official page found on 2FA/MFA for Unthread logins. SSO is not in Pro.

26.e: "We're SOC 2 Type II certified". "Certifications & compliance" lists SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA; no ISO 27001 found. DPA "covers GDPR, UK GDPR". Trust Center is gated (request-access form). NIS2-specific documentation: not found.

27.e: "Unthread offers isolated, dedicated database instances in specific countries", list includes "EU European Union". Privacy policy (default): "we transfer the data, including Personal Data, to United States and process it there". AI: "Unthread integrates with OpenAI’s API" (region not stated). Bring-your-own Bedrock: "Enter the AWS region where requests should be sent" (only "customers on higher plans"). **Missing:** EU backups and EU AI processing not documented.

28.e: No retention setting found. The closest feature, "automatic closing of tickets due to inactivity", closes tickets and does not delete them. The privacy policy only says "We will retain your Personal Data only for as long as is necessary".

29.e: Pricing is "per agent / month". No page says that requesters or end users are free. Standard role "can see tickets and leave responses but cannot update details or be assigned"; whether it needs a seat is not stated. Enterprise "Lite" role exists "as specified in your software license agreement".

30.e: Slack bot: "Unthread AI can generate a helpdesk answer and deflect tickets", "the bot can auto-detect the ticket type", and it fills form fields. Users can check status: "From the Unthread app homepage in Slack, users can view their history of requests". Portal: "submit tickets through a conversational experience using the Unthread AI Assistant".

31.e: "Create a Service Catalog Use your Ticket Types to build out your Service Catalog in your Internal Customer Portal … create groups of request types". Links to other systems: "Custom links: appears in the top right of the nav bar."

32.e: The portal can be branded with "Brand logo Brand colors Custom domain". Clients can be separated: "Restrict Login to Account Domains", and "Account Admins have permission to view all tickets submitted by users within their account". **Missing:** the portal is set up once under "Workspace Settings → Customer Portal". A separately branded space per client was not documented.

33.e: Native PagerDuty integration: "create PagerDuty incidents directly from Unthread conversations" and "Sync PagerDuty escalation policies into Unthread user groups for on-call routing". There is also a "Create PagerDuty Page" automation action, and a mobile app: "The Unthread web app is a Progressive Web App (PWA)".

34.e: API: "Add Follower to Conversation" and "Remove Follower from Conversation". Changelog (2026-09-25): "Smarter automation followers: Add a requester's manager automatically as a …" (truncated on the index page). Temporary participants: "you can create a temporary new channel linked to the conversation … automatically be archived when the conversation is closed". Note: the UI for adding followers was not seen.

35.e: "Tasks can be helpful for tracking engineering work linked to a customer issue … (Jira, Linear, Asana, etc.)". GitHub: "Turn bug reports into GitHub issues directly from Slack threads." **Missing:** linking Notion pages or documents to a ticket is not documented. Notion appears only as a KB sync source.

36.e: "Filtering (conditionally showing or hiding the property based on the value of another input)". Options can also change through custom-code "External Select Functions" ("Dynamically showing input field options based on the ticket type selected").

37.e: Project Owner: "can see and manage all tickets as well as edit settings in the Project". "Note that ticket types are configured on a per-project basis". Field types are picked in the UI: "Short answer … Single-select … Checkbox Date User selector … File upload".

38.e: "You can define which ticket types and custom fields are visible to end users in the Customer Portal … expose specific ticket types only to C-level stakeholders or customers on certain plans by using ticket type–level conditional visibility rules." Note: shown for the portal. Group-limited forms in Slack were not verified.

39.e: "Some ticket types, like new hire onboarding … require a checklist … You can use the custom field properties to create a checklist that will be visible to agent only". The changelog (2026-10-30) adds "project templates". **Missing:** an owner and a due date per checklist step are not documented. The checklist is a workaround built from checkbox fields.

40.e: Per project: "'Restricted' means only users within the project are able to see tickets. This is a commonly used setting for teams like HR." For bot DMs: "All conversations are by default private between the user and ticket assignees". **Missing:** limiting one ticket to its assignee and a manager, hidden from other agents in the same project, is not documented.

41.e: No CSV import of tickets found. "Outbound Email Campaigns" send mass emails to channels or segments, not tickets. The API has single "Create Conversation" only.

42.e: Trigger: "Scheduled Run automations on an interval (daily, weekly, monthly) and at a specific time." The API has "Create Conversation POST /conversations", and custom code gets unthreadClient. **Missing:** a built-in "create ticket" action was not seen. Route: a custom-code step that calls the API. One-off date triggers (for example a month before a renewal) are not documented.

43.e: Trigger "Conversation updated" with status filters. "You can write your own code … When making requests to 3rd party services, any API keys … stored secrets". **Missing:** no built-in export to a sheet or register. Route: a custom-code automation step, or Zapier (beta app, see #50).

44.e: "Trigger via Webhooks We'll generate a unique URL for your automation to be kicked from a 3rd party system." The integrations page lists "Azure Manage service alerts and incidents from Azure without leaving Slack", and Datadog appears in the integration list. **Missing:** automatic ticket creation from a monitoring alert on client-hosted systems is not documented. Route: monitoring webhook → automation or Create Conversation API.

45.e: "Filter your data by assignee, customer, channel, priority, status, and custom fields". "Limit date ranges", and "Download your analytics data as CSV files". **Missing:** filtering by the individual requester (person) is not documented. "Customer" is the client account.

46.e: "To determine how much time each engineer spends on a specific ticket, you can utilize the 'waiting on agent time' metric." **Missing:** there is no manual time entry. The metric is a status-duration measure, not actual work time. Note: time is logged in Productive (sheet comment).

47.e: SLA timers show "Due soon … Breached", and the inbox shows "the most urgent actionable SLA". Alerts: "Send Slack reminder to assignee", and the trigger "Conversation left unresponded for a set period of time". Reminders on a ticket: "Snoozing a conversation will put it 'on hold' until a certain date. It will send a DM with a custom message at the specified date."

48.e: Per client account: "When you view a customer profile, you'll be able to see a history of conversations across email, Slack, and in-app chat." Requesters see their own: "users can view their history of requests". **Missing:** an agent view or filter of all requests by one person (for example during offboarding) is not documented.

49.e: "Directory sync is used to keep employee profile data, manager relationships, departments, locations, and group membership information up to date in Unthread." Changelog: "Add a requester's manager automatically as a …" (truncated). **Missing:** sending an approval automatically to the requester's manager is not documented. Approvals go via "an approval step to your assignment rules" or are sent manually.

50.e: "Join the Beta Program From the Service accounts page, be sure to click 'Join the beta', to get early access to the Unthread for Zapier app." There is no public Zapier app page: https://zapier.com/apps/unthread/integrations returned 404. Beta, so Partial. Make (Integromat) is also mentioned.

51.e: There is no Outline connector in the native KB list. Possible routes: the web crawler ("Unthread can sync documentation from any web-based documentation system automatically by crawling pages"), which works only for public sites, or a custom build on the KB API ("Create Knowledge Base Article"). Outline compatibility was not verified.

52.e: Native: "Accounts from Hubspot will begin syncing to Unthread. The Account name and support rep will be used for the Unthread customer name and primary support rep." The Accounts page lists "HubSpot Integration & Synced CRM contacts if applicable". Limitation: "Changes to Hubspot Accounts can take up to an hour".

53.e: No Productive integration was seen. Route: a custom-code automation step calling the Productive API ("When making requests to 3rd party services … stored secrets"), or Zapier (beta app, see #50). The Productive side was not verified.

54.e: "ServiceNow Sync requests tracked in Unthread over to your SNow instance." Inbound exists for Zendesk (changelog 2026-10-27: "Your Zendesk tickets automtically create Unthread tickets"). **Missing:** inbound tickets from a client's own ServiceNow (client L1) are not documented. The ServiceNow direction shown is Unthread → SNow.

55.e: Calendars are used only for availability: "users can rely on their existing Slack schedules or Google Calendars". **Missing:** ticket deadlines or tasks appearing in calendars are not documented. Route: a custom-code automation step calling the Google Calendar API, or Zapier (beta).

56.e: The HRIS integrations named are "Workday, BambooHR, Rippling, Greenhouse … and 50+ more". Aboard is not named. Route: Aboard event → automation webhook ("unique URL for your automation to be kicked from a 3rd party system") or the Create Conversation API. Aboard's webhook or API support was not verified.

57.e: "In order to request a copy or deletion of your personal data, please contact support+data@unthread.io". **Missing:** a manual request to the vendor is the only route found. No in-product function to delete or export all data about one person was documented.

58.e: "Unthread offers isolated, dedicated database instances in specific countries" (US, EU, UK, AU, CA). "We support custom deployments for enterprise customers." **Missing:** a per-client region inside one workspace is not documented. Per-client regions would need separate dedicated instances, so Partial.

59.e: "You can choose between a Kanban or a List view for your conversations". Saved views: "filter for specific messages by customer, status, assignee … save this as a custom filter". There is also a Board Builder for dashboards.

checks: Re-checked: the privacy policy says data is transferred "to United States and process it there" (https://unthread.io/privacy); EU database instance only on Enterprise. #27 Partial stands.
Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 8 / Partial 7 / Unknown 1.

Re-checked: "Unthread supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP)" with write tools such as "update_conversation" and "create_conversation_comment" (https://docs.unthread.io/docs/unthread-ai/unthread-mcp). #21 Meets stands: an external agent can read and act on tickets.
Counts recomputed by script: Meets 19 / Partial 22 / Unknown 2; Musts: Meets 9 / Partial 3 / Unknown 1.

1.e: Plan table: "Email Send email using your own custom email addresses. Either through Deskpro, SMTP or directly link your Gmail/Outlook accounts." Help Center: "allowing external users to submit tickets via email". Ticket thread: "any messages to and from the User and internal Agent notes" and "History of all the actions that have been applied to the Ticket". Users can "reopen a resolved ticket by replying to an email".

2.n: The pages read state no limit on the number of email accounts.
2.p: Team (Shared Inbox, Ticket Queues and Round Robin are on all plans)
2.e: "Go to Admin > Channels > Email > Accounts. Here, you can either: Select an existing Deskpro Cloud email account, or Click + New to create a new one." / "Toggle the 'Use a custom email address' option". Pricing: "Shared Inbox Collaborate across every contact point with connected inboxes." Per-email-account triggers handle "Assigning tickets created via email to departments".

3.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; a receipt confirmation for user-created tickets is evidenced only by the feature name "Auto Responses" in the plan table; same rule as ServiceNow name-only evidence
3.e: Plan table, "Automation & Workflows": "Auto Responses" ticked on Team, Professional and Enterprise. Default triggers also send "a notification email to the user when an agent creates a new ticket for them". Note: the evidence for a receipt confirmation on user-created tickets is the plan-table feature name only. No help article describing its content was read.

4.e: Default triggers: "Sending an email to the user when an agent replies to their ticket". Approval templates have trigger stages "Request Created", "Partial Approval Response", "Request Approved", "Request Rejected". "By default, Deskpro sends an email notification to Approvers." **Missing:** no page read documents a requester notification on every status change or at each approval step. The approval defaults notify approvers and "the agent who submitted it". The trigger-action list could not be read.

5.e: "Agent Notes are used for internal communication between Agents and will not be seen by the User."

6.p: Team (@mentions, Agent Notes, Ticket Followers). Tasks: plan not stated. Lite Agents: Professional
6.e: Plan table: "@mentions", "Agent Notes", "Ticket Followers" on all plans. Tasks "link directly to open tickets". "Use task comments to add context, discuss next steps, or flag blockers". Lite Agents "can view tickets and collaborate with your team, but can't respond to users directly" (Professional 50, Enterprise 1000).

7.n: Changes are recorded in the ticket History tab.
7.p: Team (core feature, no plan restriction shown)
7.e: "There are two types of assignment: Agent Assignment … Team Assignment". "Assigned Tickets have an Unassign link to clear the Agent or Team assignment." History tab: "History of all the actions that have been applied to the Ticket by Agents, Users, or automatic processes."

8.n: Custom sub-statuses exist. Missing: defining or limiting statuses per process or department is not documented. Sub-statuses are created once under the core statuses.
8.p: Team (core feature, no plan restriction shown)
8.e: "There is an option in Deskpro to add sub-statuses within the core statuses." "You can choose a Parent Status type (all sub-statuses must have a core status that it is associated with)". "These sub-statuses can be added automatically with Triggers".

9.p: Team ("Custom Fields", "Dynamic Forms" on all plans)
9.e: "Each Department can have its own Agent Form and User Form." Field types include "Select Field – A list of options you define", "Date" and "Date/Time". "You can make any field required before a Ticket can be submitted." Per-client forms: possible only as one department per client (not verified).

10.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; the current guide documents approvals and logging but not chaining steps such as manager then department head; chaining appears only in a 2019 release post; same rule as Zendesk #10 and NinjaOne #10
10.p: Not stated (Approvals is not in the plan comparison)
10.e: "Chain approvals together using approval triggers" and "Send a single request to one or multiple approvers" (release news, Nov 2019). Templates set "To Approve – The number of positive responses required". Approvers can be "Ticket User Organization Manager All Agents" or specific "Agents or CRM Users". The agent can add a description. The approver can "Add a message to explain their decision". "The request is logged on the Ticket, including all key details and the current status." **Caveats:** chaining appears only in the 2019 news post. The current guide shows per-stage template triggers but does not describe chaining step by step. "Requester's manager" is only the "Organization Manager" group or an agent choice. No line-manager lookup was found.

11.n: Parent and child linked tickets exist. Missing: the pages read do not show (a) that the parent shows the children's status, (b) that a linked ticket can be created in another department automatically (for example by a trigger), or (c) that the full history is visible across both. Children are fully independent.
11.p: Team (core feature, no plan restriction shown)
11.e: "The solution is to create a linked Ticket, using Linked Ticket from the Ticket Actions menu." "You can select which ticket you want to be the parent and which should be the child." "Parent and child tickets are just connected for ease of access, they will act independently of each other."

12.e: "Belonging to additional Organizations does not automatically share their tickets with those Organizations or allow them to view other members' tickets." "Once a User is set as a Manager this gives them access to all the tickets created by other members of the Organization". **Missing:** no explicit statement that a regular user sees only their own tickets. This is only implied by the manager rule. Visibility for users added or CC'd to a ticket is not documented. Caveat: an Organization Manager sees all tickets of the organization. Avoid this role for internal People/IT requests.

13.e: Desks: "Full: The Agent can view all Tickets in the Department". "Assign: The Agent can assign Tickets to the Department but cannot view Tickets within it". So tickets can move between desks without visibility. Exception: "Agents can always view Tickets that are: Assigned to them, Assigned to their Teams, Followed by them". **Missing:** no agent permission per client Organization inside one department was found. Per-client separation would need one department per client (not verified).

14.p: Team (Triggers, Escalations, Follow Ups, Round Robin, Macros and Zapier are on all plans)
14.e: "Triggers are automations that perform actions on tickets when specific events occur." "Criteria are filters based on ticket properties, such as department, team, or status." "Actions are the automations that run when a trigger is activated." Zapier is listed on all plans.

15.e: "A ticket enters Warning status when it is close to breaching its target (you define the warning criteria)." "Define the type of action required to fulfill the SLA, such as a first response or resolution time." "Multiple SLAs can apply to a single ticket." Trigger criteria can check whether "a Ticket Property has … a specific value" (for example, priority).

16.p: Team ("150+ Built In Reports", "Custom Reports", "Custom Dashboards" on all plans)
16.e: Plan table: "Ticket Queues", "150+ Built In Reports", "Custom Dashboards". "Live Dashboards Display live updates to your reports". "Maintain SLAs and departmental performance." Response and resolution times rest on a customer quote on the vendor page: "how fast we can get to resolutions or to work out our average response time". The Reports Guide was not read.

17.p: Not stated (audit log is not in the plan comparison)
17.e: Admin Audit Log: "every recorded Admin interaction … including configuration updates, permission changes". Records "type, action, performer and timestamp". Ticket History: "a record of everything that has happened related to the Ticket", with an "Assignments" tab "(when the Ticket's User, assigned Agent or Team was changed)". **Missing:** no statement that entries cannot be edited. Agents with permission can "Edit … the message content" and "Delete message … cannot be undone". It is not stated whether these actions are logged.

18.n: Included in the plan; no separate AI price is listed. Missing: suggestions from past tickets and a flag that a similar problem came up before are not documented on the pages read. A search result mentions tickets as an AI content source in release 2026.1, but that page was not opened.
18.e: "Suggested Replies – Provides AI-powered response suggestions to reduce typing time and improve consistency." Web sources "can power features such as AI Draft Reply, AI Search, and your AI Chatbot." "Deskpro AI features are available on the Professional plan and above."

19.n: Included in the plan; no separate AI price is listed. Needs an active AI connection.
19.e: "Customer Intents categorizes incoming tickets based on their content." "You can configure intent detection to run automatically on all incoming tickets or only when specific conditions are met within Triggers". "Improve ticket routing by assigning tickets to the most suitable agents." Intent sets include HR ("Benefits Payroll Time off").

20.n: Included in the plan. Missing: a link to the current, scattered knowledge base in Notion or Outline is not verified. Web Sources index only public sites that are not rendered with JavaScript.
20.e: "Draft Knowledge Base Article - Draft documentation in seconds based on a ticket interaction". "select the purple Write article with AI option … the system will automatically generate a draft Knowledgebase article." Web source: "The website must be publicly accessible and not require login credentials." "Pages rendered using javascript & SPA sites are not supported."

21.n: No Deskpro MCP server was found (2 WebSearch queries on deskpro.com and support.deskpro.com, plus release notes 2026.4). Routes: (a) the public REST API; (b) Zapier MCP, a third-party route that works with Claude; (c) "Bring your own AI" connections, which power only Deskpro's own AI features. Claude is not named among the providers on the pages read. On-premises: Private can also connect a self-hosted LLM, but the verdict does not change.
21.p: Team (REST API, Zapier); Professional (Deskpro AI connections)
21.e: Pricing: "Full REST API" on all plans. Zapier: "Call actions in natural language with Zapier MCP Act in Deskpro from your AI … Example actions on this page Add Message to Ticket Create Organization Works with Claude · ChatGPT · Cursor". AI: "Bring the model you trust". "You might configure OpenAI for Prompting and Voyage for Embeddings." Private: "Self-Hosted (Ollama) Amazon Bedrock Other supported third-party providers".

22.n: There is no Notion app in the Deskpro marketplace list (70 apps on the page). Route: AI Web Sources, which are limited to public pages that are not rendered with JavaScript. Whether Notion pages qualify was not verified. Missing: showing Notion content in a client's support space is not documented.
22.e: Web source "will use the content of an external website or knowledge base as a Data Source. The content will be indexed and can power features such as AI Draft Reply, AI Search, and your AI Chatbot." "Pages rendered using javascript & SPA sites are not supported."

23.e: Native Deskpro Slack app. "Deskpro now allows unauthenticated users to create support tickets directly from Slack channels". "/deskpro subscribe". Product page: "Track progress in Slack Receive status updates and respond to questions without opening another app." **Missing:** "Direct Messages (DMs) are not supported in this release". Intake is from public or private channels, and the ticket confirmation is posted "to the thread of the Slack message", so there is no private requester-to-agent channel. Two-way reply and status sync for non-agent requesters appears on the marketing page only. The guide documents agent actions ("Add Note", "refresh the response to view the latest ticket status").

24.n: Webhooks are fine-grained through trigger events and criteria.
24.p: Team (Full REST API, Apps Marketplace and Build Custom Apps are on all plans)
24.e: Pricing: "Apps Marketplace", "Full REST API", "Build Custom Apps". "The action Call webhook is available for Triggers, SLAs, or Escalations." "Deskpro submits a default payload containing information related to the ticket". Inbound: "Inbound Webhooks allow you to trigger actions on existing tickets". Developers guide lists "About the API", "API Reference" and "API Keys".

25.n: SSO is on all plans and needs no separate subscription. The Google app is managed by Google, not Deskpro.
25.p: Team (SSO and Agent 2FA are on all plans)
25.e: "Google provides a pre-integrated SSO application for Deskpro within Google Workspace." (Google's guide is titled "Set up your own custom SAML application".) 2FA: "There are two methods of 2FA available: Email 2FA and TOTP Service." "If you want to make 2FA mandatory for all agents, enable Require agents to set up 2FA."

26.e: "Compliance certifications and regulations ISO 27001 … SOC 2 Type II". Plan table: "ISO27001", "SOC2", "DPA" on all plans. "Recent security audits and certifications include ISO27001, PCI, Cyber Essentials Plus, CSA Star". Sub-processor list with "30 days written notice" of changes. NIS2-specific documentation: not found.

27.p: Team (EU data centre "as standard"); EU-hosted AI provider from Professional
27.e: "Deskpro offers deployment of Cloud accounts onto data centers located in either the US, EU or UK. Customers can choose which region they wish to exclusively host their data in, as standard." AI: "Berget AI offers a European-hosted, privacy-focused platform" (Professional and Enterprise). **Missing:** backup location ("Additional encrypted off-site backups are updated daily") is not stated. Region of Deskpro-managed AI is not stated. The general sub-processor list includes US-located processors ("SparkPost … Email delivery service … US", "Pusher … US"). The separate EU sub-processor list was not read. **On-premises:** Deskpro Private lets AI run "inside your Amazon VPC … or connect a self-hosted model. Your data never leaves your approved perimeter", which could close the AI gap. Not evaluated.

28.n: (reviewer correction: was "Meets"; deletion is built with automation (escalations), not a dedicated retention setting; same rule as Atlassian #28). Caveats: an escalation acts only on tickets created after it is set up, so older tickets need the API. The KB article was last updated Oct 3, 2023. The sheet says to verify this in trials.
28.e: "If you don't want to retain tickets over a certain age, create an escalation that deletes tickets after they have been in the resolved status e.g. a month." "With automation features like Escalations, you can automatically clear all ticket attachments after a set period". Deleted status: "Automatic Clean Up where the deleted Tickets are purged from the system after a certain period of time."

29.e: "End-users are free and unlimited on all licenses." (KB, last updated Aug 2023). "All plans are billed per Agent license". Approvers can be "Agents or CRM Users" and respond in the Help Center, so they need no agent seat.

30.n: Present: AI answers from the knowledge base in a Help Center chatbot and in Slack, ticket creation from Slack, and status updates in Slack. Missing: pointing people to the right form, and the assistant opening a ticket or checking status on request, are not documented.
30.p: Professional (AI Chatbot; Deskpro AI in Slack needs an AI connection). Team (Slack ticket creation)
30.e: Chatbot: "The Chatbot draws only from the knowledge you define in your AI Data Sources". Fallback goes to "the next step in your Chatflow, such as connecting the user to your support team." Slack: "/deskpro ai What is the default number of holidays we have in a year? The AI will respond in-thread". "Track progress in Slack Receive status updates and respond to questions without opening another app."

31.n: One Help Center with a separate form per department is documented. Missing: a catalog of request types that links out to other systems (for example Aboard) is not documented. Help Center cards were not opened.
31.e: Help Center: "Create a fully branded portal where users can browse help articles and submit tickets." "Each Department can have its own Agent Form and User Form." "The User Form is displayed in the Help Center for Users to submit Tickets."

32.n: A branded Help Center per brand exists (Team 3, Professional 10, Enterprise unlimited). Missing: quick setup that reuses existing data (for example from HubSpot) is not documented.
32.p: Team (3 brands); Professional (10 brands, removes "Powered by Deskpro"); Enterprise (unlimited)
32.e: "Multi-Brand Help Centers Manage separate Help Centers for multiple brands or departments from one Deskpro workspace. 3 10 Unlimited". "Theme Customization Fully customize your Help Center colors, typography, and layout". "Each brand can have unique workflows, content, automations, and visual presentation".

33.n: There is an official Deskpro-built PagerDuty app, and mobile apps are on Team. Missing: automatic paging when an urgent ticket arrives, and mobile push notifications, are not documented. The PagerDuty incident is created by an agent from the ticket.
