33.e: PagerDuty app (developer: Deskpro): "Incident Creation: Seamlessly create a PagerDuty incident upon receiving customer complaints without switching between applications". Pricing, Team: "Mobile Apps".

34.p: Team (Ticket Followers are on all plans)
34.e: "Adding an agent as a follower means they can always see the ticket, overriding Agent and Department permissions." "When adding, removing, or setting agent followers for ticket properties on Triggers, SLAs, Escalations, and Macros, Admins can now Add/Remove all members from the team."

35.n: GitHub, GitLab and Jira have official Deskpro apps. Missing: Notion. There is no Notion app in the marketplace list.
35.e: GitHub app (developer: Deskpro): "Link issues to tickets: Link tickets to issues in Github". "View linked issues". Apps list: "GitLab Link Gitlab issues to Deskpro tickets".

36.n: Field visibility depends on earlier values. Nested select fields exist, but that page was not opened.
36.p: Team (Dynamic Forms are on all plans)
36.e: "The Only show this field based on custom criteria option allows you to add conditional fields to forms." "Suppose you only want the Joiner Name field to appear if the Business Area is set to Customer Support."

37.n: The form editor is no-code. Missing: letting a business team edit only its own department's forms without full admin rights is not documented. The steps start in the Admin interface.
37.e: "To edit these forms, go to: Admin > Ticket Structure > Departments > [Department Name] > Forms". "To add a Ticket Field to a form, click the +Field button and select from the available list of fields".

38.n: Forms are per department, and departments are limited by usergroup.
38.e: "User access to Departments is controlled via Usergroups. This lets you limit access to certain Departments for specific groups of Users." "If a User belongs to multiple groups, they see only the Departments their Usergroups allow." Note: "This setting only affects ticket creation."

39.n: Tasks linked to a ticket have owners and due dates, and ticket templates exist. Missing: a template that creates the checklist or tasks with owners and due dates. Ticket templates preset only properties, and the reusable checklist uses custom fields.
39.e: Templates "define preset values such as Department, Status, Labels, and Assignments". Tasks: "You can create one or more Tasks linked to a Ticket". "Assign tasks to individual agents or teams". "Add deadlines to any task". Checklist: "Your Admins can set this up in Deskpro using custom fields."

40.p: Team (Ticket Permissions are on all plans)
40.e: "If you also disable Can view tickets for tickets assigned to others, the Agent will only be able to view Tickets assigned directly to them or one of their Teams." Agents can always view "Tickets they are following".

41.n: The importer is aimed at existing data. Whether triggers and notifications run on imported tickets was not verified.
41.e: "If you have lots of existing user, organization and ticket data in a CSV format that you would like to quickly import into your helpdesk, you can use our in-built CSV importer." "Navigate to Admin > Data > Importer Select the Import Now button next to the Users/ Organizations/Tickets label".

42.e: "Recurring Tickets automate the creation of tickets on a fixed schedule." "The Recurring Tickets feature is available on Deskpro Team, Professional, and Enterprise plans." "You can also set end conditions for each rule — for example, stopping after a fixed number of occurrences or on a specific date."

43.n: Route 1: the native "Call webhook" action in a ticket-update trigger, which needs a receiving endpoint. Route 2: Zapier, using the "Ticket Update" trigger to Google Sheets. No native spreadsheet action was found.
43.e: "Set a webhook as an action in a Trigger, SLA, or Escalation to send a payload related to the ticket". The custom payload "accepts both static data and variables using Twig". Zapier: "Ticket Update Triggers when a ticket is updated"; template "Add new Deskpro tickets to Google Sheets".

44.n: Route: a custom build in which the monitoring tool calls the REST API or sends email to a support address. Missing: inbound webhooks act only on existing tickets. No monitoring integration was found, and nothing points to a solution.
44.e: "Inbound Webhooks allow you to trigger actions on existing tickets in Deskpro by sending a request from an external script or service." Pricing: "Full REST API".

45.n: Per-requester ticket lists, custom reports and grouping by custom fields are documented. Missing: filtering by a custom-field value or range (amount) and by period in one view is not shown on the pages read. The ticket search page was blocked (403 captcha).
45.p: Team (Custom Reports and Data Export are on all plans)
45.e: Pricing: "150+ Built In Reports", "Custom Reports", "Data Export". "The Tickets section on the User Profile shows you the Tickets that the User has submitted". Release 2026.4: "Grouped ticket lists now page correctly when a custom field holds multiple values".

46.n: Billing & Time time logs are separate from SLAs.
46.e: "You can customize the fields used for each time or billing charge in your help desk. To configure these, go to Features > Billing & Time > Fields." "The same custom fields are used for both monetary billing and time log entries."

47.p: Team (Escalations and Follow Ups are on all plans)
47.e: "Escalations let you automate actions when a Ticket stays in a specific state for a defined period of time." "Follow Ups … are also Ticket specific". "Add note - Add an internal note to a Ticket as a reminder". Pending status "Total Waiting Time" settings.

48.e: "The Tickets section on the User Profile shows you the Tickets that the User has submitted to the helpdesk, these are separated into two categories: Open and Resolved". "The activity stream shows an detailed overview of the User's actions".

49.n: User provisioning from Google Workspace is documented. Missing: syncing the manager or company structure, and auto-filling the requester's manager as an approver, are not documented. Approvers are preset in the template or chosen by the agent.
49.e: "The Google Workspace SSO application also supports Auto Provisioning, which can automatically create and manage users in Deskpro." Approvals: "Approvers may be pre-set, or the Agent may select them."

50.n: There is an official Deskpro app on Zapier.
50.e: "Triggers & Actions New Organization … New Ticket Reply Triggers when a ticket is answered … Ticket Update Triggers when a ticket is updated … New Ticket Triggers when a new ticket is created". Deskpro: "Triggers and actions include creating and updating tickets, users, and organizations."

51.n: There is no Outline app in the Deskpro marketplace list. Routes: Zapier (Deskpro's Zapier app), a custom build on the REST API, or AI Web Sources if the Outline content is public and not rendered with JavaScript. The Outline side was not verified.
51.e: Apps list (70 apps) has no Outline entry. Web source: "The website must be publicly accessible and not require login credentials."

52.n: There is an official Deskpro-built HubSpot app. Missing: pulling HubSpot company or organization data to set up a client's space is not documented. The app links contacts and deals only. CRM Sync is one-way out (Salesforce or webhook).
52.p: Team (marketplace app); CRM Sync from Professional
52.e: HubSpot app (developer: Deskpro): "Automatically link your HubSpot contacts to Deskpro Users". "You can display and edit contact details for deals". "Create, view, and edit your deals." CRM Sync: "The sync direction is one-way (Deskpro → external CRM)."

53.n: There is no Productive app in the marketplace list; it lists Clockify, Harvest and Toggl apps instead. Routes: a custom build on the REST API, or Zapier. The Productive side was not verified.
53.e: Apps list includes "Clockify", "Harvest", "Toggl" and has no Productive entry. Pricing: "Full REST API", "Zapier".

54.n: There is no ServiceNow app in the marketplace list. Routes: the client's tool emails a dedicated support address (#2), or a custom build on the REST API.
54.e: Apps list (70 apps) has no ServiceNow entry. Custom addresses: "Forward all mail from help@yourcompany.com → contact@yourcompany.deskpro.com".

55.n: There is an official Deskpro-built Google Calendar app. Missing: ticket deadlines and tasks showing up in calendars automatically is not documented. Events are created by hand from Deskpro.
55.e: Google Calendar app (developer: Deskpro): "View Events/Calendar: See a list of events in your calendar within the app." "Create Events: Schedule future events directly from Deskpro."

56.n: No Aboard integration was found. Routes: a custom build in which Aboard events call the Deskpro REST API, or Zapier. A Zapier template shows a ticket-create action ("Create a Deskpro ticket from form entries"). The Aboard side (API, webhooks, Zapier app) was not verified.
56.e: Zapier: "Create a Deskpro ticket from form entries". Pricing: "Full REST API". The apps list has "People HR" but no Aboard entry.

57.n: Deletion of a person and all their tickets is documented, but it is manual. Missing: exporting a copy of one person's data and automating the request. The "Exporting Data" page was not opened.
57.e: "Deleting Users If you use the Delete button on the dropdown this will permanently delete a User's account. Warning Deleting a User will also delete all their Tickets." Security page: "Deskpro provides tools and controls to help you meet GDPR obligations".

58.n: One region applies per Cloud account, so per-client regions would need separate accounts or workspaces (rule 13). Whether linked workspaces can sit in different regions is not documented. On-premises: Deskpro Private can be hosted anywhere, but that is also one instance per region, so the verdict does not change.
58.p: Team (US / UK / EU); Enterprise (22 countries, marked "paid")
58.e: "Customers can choose which region they wish to exclusively host their data in, as standard." "Enterprise plan customers can choose to host in 1 of 22 countries around the world." Pricing: "Workspaces Link multiple Deskpro instances together". "Shared Agents/Multi-Account" Professional 3, Enterprise Unlimited.

59.e: "Kanban view organizes tickets as a visual workflow". "Group In Kanban, group dictates what property the columns in the board will be grouped by." Sort options include "Agent Agent Team Created".

questions: #10: Which plan includes Approvals? In the current version, can one ticket run a sequential chain (Organization Manager or line manager, then Head of Finance) automatically via approval-template triggers? Can the requester's line manager be resolved automatically, beyond the "Organization Manager" group?
#4: Can triggers email the requester on every status change and at each approval stage (Request Created / Partial / Approved / Rejected)? From which plan?
#3: Confirm that "Auto Responses" sends a receipt confirmation to the requester for tickets created by email, Slack and Help Center on the Team plan.
#12: Confirm that a regular user (not an Organization Manager) sees only their own tickets in the Help Center. Can users who are CC'd or added to a ticket see it?
#13: Can agent visibility be limited per client Organization inside one department? Or is one department per client required, and are there limits on the number of departments?

#17: Are message edits and deletions, ticket owner changes and approval decisions written to ticket History with user and time? Can an admin edit or delete any History or Admin Audit Log entry? Which plan includes the Admin Audit Log?

#23: Can a non-agent employee raise a ticket privately (DM or private modal) and receive agent replies and status changes back in Slack privately? When will DM support be available? Is the channel thread confirmation visible to all channel members?

#27: Where are the daily off-site backups of EU-hosted accounts kept? In which region does Deskpro-managed AI process data? Do any processors on the EU sub-processor list (e.g., SparkPost, Pusher, SendGrid, Google) process EU customer data outside the EU?
#26: Does the ISO 27001 / SOC 2 Type II scope cover Deskpro Cloud? Does Deskpro provide NIS2 supply-chain documentation (security questionnaire, incident-notification terms)?
Pricing: billing period (annual only, or also monthly?), EUR prices, Lite Agent price beyond the included number, and which plan the 14-day trial uses.
#29: Confirm that the 2023 statement "End-users are free and unlimited on all licenses" is still valid for Team, Professional and Enterprise.
#8: Can sub-statuses (or the statuses offered) be limited to one department or process, so that People sees its own set and IT another?
#11: Can a trigger or ticket template create a linked child ticket in another department automatically (onboarding to IT equipment), and does the parent show each child's status and history?

#18: Can Deskpro AI suggest solutions from past resolved tickets, and can it flag that a similar problem was reported before? Is "tickets as an AI content source" (release 2026.1) generally available in Cloud?
#20: Can AI data sources index a private Notion or Outline workspace, or only public, non-JavaScript websites?
#21: Do you offer, or plan, an official MCP server for Deskpro? Is Anthropic Claude a supported "bring your own AI" provider (directly or through Amazon Bedrock) in Deskpro Cloud?
#22: Is there a supported way to show Notion pages (for example a client's documentation) in a brand's Help Center or to the AI chatbot?
#18/#19/#30: Is Deskpro-managed AI usage metered or capped on Professional, and are there extra charges above a limit?
#24: Which webhook events exist outside triggers (for example user, organization or approval events), and are there API rate limits per plan?
#28: Can an escalation delete tickets that already existed when the escalation was created? Are deleted tickets and attachments purged from backups, and after how long?
#30: Can the AI chatbot or Slack assistant check a request's status on demand and open a ticket for the user from the conversation?
#31: Can the Help Center list request types that link out to other systems (for example Aboard), as a service catalog?
#33: Do the mobile apps send push notifications for new urgent tickets, and can a trigger page PagerDuty automatically?
#37: Can a non-admin (for example a People lead) be given permission to edit only their own department's forms?
#41: Do tickets created by the CSV importer run triggers and send notifications, like tickets created in the UI?
#45: Can agents filter ticket lists or reports by a custom-field value range (amount), requester and date range together?
#49: Can Deskpro sync each user's manager from Google Workspace (or SCIM) and use "requester's manager" as an approver automatically?
#52: Can the HubSpot app import HubSpot companies as Deskpro organizations, or pre-fill a brand or Help Center from HubSpot data?
#57: Is there a per-person data export (subject access request), and can deletion or export be automated?
#58: Can workspaces linked under Multi-Account sit in different data regions (for example EU and US), and what does the Enterprise "Global Data Center" option cost?
#18/#19/#30/#58: How is Deskpro AI processing located for an EU Cloud account when Deskpro-managed AI is used (which provider and which region)?
checks: Corrected #3 from "Meets" to "Partial": the receipt confirmation for user-created tickets rests only on the plan-table feature name "Auto Responses" (same rule as ServiceNow name-only evidence).

Corrected #10 from "Meets" to "Partial": chaining approvals (manager, then department head) is described only in a 2019 release post; the current guide does not describe it (same rule as Zendesk #10 and NinjaOne #10).
Counts after correction, checked by script: Meets 8 / Partial 8.

Corrected #28 from "Meets" to "Partial" for consistency: ticket and attachment deletion is done with escalations (automation) and applies only to tickets created after the escalation is set up; there is no dedicated retention setting. Atlassian #28 (automation rules) is Partial; only Zendesk, with dedicated deletion schedules, is Meets.
#21 Partial confirmed under rule 7: no Deskpro MCP server; "bring your own AI" powers only Deskpro's own features.

1.p: Professional ("Email to Slack Ticketing"; not in Starter)
1.e: "Email to your support address becomes a ticket in Slack, each with an owner, status, and deadline. The agent answers in the thread, and the reply reaches the customer as a normal email back." "Each email ticket holds the customer messages and the internal notes in one thread". "The communication is bi-directionally synced between Slack and the Email." "The record of each request holds the fields, the files, the approvals, and the status history".

2.p: Professional ("Email ticketing is included from the Professional plan")
2.e: "Forwarding is the connection between the mailbox and Suptask, and one address maps to one Inbox." "Several support addresses can run at once, each in its dedicated Inbox". An Inbox can also hold several email intake sources. Pick-up: "Agents will see all the unassigned tickets, or the tickets assigned to them". Auto-assignment option "Online only - Only assign the ticket to Agents who have their status set to online in Slack."

3.e: "Suptask will send an automatic reply back to the user with a confirmation that the email request has been received together with the ticket number." "By default a confirmation email is sent back to the requester. You can optionally disable this."

4.e: Email templates: "titleUpdated: Your ticket #{{ticket.ticketNumber}} has been updated", "updateMessage: Your ticket has been updated. Here are the most recent replies", "titleClosed: … has been closed". Slack: "Any reply from the Agent on a ticket will also appear directly in the ticket thread." Approvals: "A rejection asks for the reason, and the requester sees it in the thread"; "the requester sees the status change in the thread". **Missing:** no documented requester notification at each approval step (e.g. manager approved, now waiting for Head of Finance). For email requesters, only replies and closing are documented, not other status changes.

5.e: "Internal comment – The reply is internal and only visible to the team of Agents in the Inbox." Caveat: "By default, all replies from Agents are Public" (changeable in Account settings).

6.e: "They can work privately as a team to resolve tickets together, leaving both Private and Public replies on tickets." "tagging the user in the ticket message thread, which will make Slack send notifications". Tasks: "You can create effective task lists within a submitted ticket by utilizing custom fields" (Single-selection field with "Completed" and "Not completed"). **Limited:** no native task object (no per-task assignee or due date); tasks are a custom-field workaround.

7.n: Assigning and reassigning: yes. Not verified: a record of each change (the audit-log comment). Only a count of reassignments is documented. "Audit & Compliance" is ticked on the Custom plan only.
7.e: "Assignee Who is assigned and responsible for the ticket". The web overview lets you "change assignee, priority and status directly from the list". "Assignee, priority, tags and status can all be changed in bulk." Metric: "Number of reassignments: Track the number of reassignments that occurs on tickets."

8.p: Starter (custom statuses, 1 Inbox). Professional for several Inboxes (unlimited Inboxes)
8.e: "Statuses, priorities and tags are no longer shared across the whole workspace – each Inbox owns its own set, so IT and HR can run completely different workflows." "Rename, reorder or add statuses in the Inbox settings". Example custom values: "Waiting for approval", "Escalated to Engineering".

9.p: Starter (one team, "Unlimited Forms & Fields"); Professional for several team Inboxes; Growth for "Conditional & dynamic fields"
9.e: "There can be multiple Forms in each Inbox". Field settings: "Optional", "Required", "Required on close". Field types: "Single-selection list", "Date", "Date time"; system field "Due Date". Caveat: "An Email source offers one Form. Fields on the Form are not shown to the email sender; Agents can fill them in". Per-client forms: possible per Slack channel intake source; for email, one Form per address.

10.p: Growth ("Multi-person approval sequences", "Automated approval workflows"); Professional has "Ad-hoc approvals" only
10.e: "Sequential approvals – Approvers are asked one at a time, in order. A single rejection stops the sequence." Example: "send a sequential approval first to the user selected in the field Approving manager, then to the fixed user Head of Finance." "Every approval request is saved inside the ticket, including the request text and who it was sent to. Any change from an approver … is recorded in the ticket." The manager is picked by the requester in a form field (automatic lookup in HRIS/Google Workspace needs an AI Assistant; "Build your own AI Assistants" is Custom-only).

11.n: A ticket can move across team Inboxes with its history, and both tickets reference each other. Missing: sub-tickets (parent/child) running in parallel with their status visible on the parent. On a move, the original ticket is closed.
11.e: "Tickets can be moved from one Inbox or Form to another, so the right team handles the request without it being submitted again." "The original ticket is set to Closed. Both tickets reference each other". Onboarding: "One request goes through HR, IT and Facilities in turn, and each team works on the same ticket with the full history." Merging: "link the others to it and close them".

12.e: "Users will only be able to overview the tickets they have access to, such as the tickets that they have submitted." Private Form: "tickets are sent to the requester in a DM and are only accessible to the requester and the Agents in the Inbox." Caveat: a Public Form posts tickets in the channel, visible to its members.

13.p: Professional ("Unlimited Teams"; "Route tickets across channels and teams")
13.e: "Each team will only have access to the tickets submitted to their Inbox." "The HR team can not see nor access any of the submitted tickets which the IT team receives in their inbox, and vice verse." "Suptask Admin do not get automatic access to all Inboxes." **Missing:** no per-client visibility rule inside one Inbox. Per-client separation only by modelling each client as its own Inbox ("one address maps to one Inbox"); the vendor does not document this as a per-client pattern.

14.e: "The Automation feature in Suptask allows you to set up triggers, conditions and actions for your tickets." "Automations are available within the Professional & Growth & Custom Enterprise plan". "Time-based Automation rules are available within the Growth & Custom Enterprise plan". The actions include status, priority, assignee, move, automatic reply, webhook and approvals.

15.p: Growth ("SLA thresholds", "SLA breach notifications in Slack")
15.e: "Priority levels: … None, or Low, Medium, High, Critical". "Resolution time … from when the ticket is created to when it is closed." "Reply time … For the first reply, it is calculate from when the ticket was created." "Send a notification prior to a threshold breach: Define the time in minutes". "Send an escalation notification".

16.p: Starter ("Single-team analytics"); Professional ("Multi-team analytics", "Reports (CSV)"); Growth ("SLA analytics"); Custom ("Custom dashboards & metrics")
16.e: Widgets: "Active tickets", "Mean time to first reply", "Mean time to resolution", "Top 10 assignees". Queue: "Ticket overview in Web", "Ticket overview in Slack" (all plans). Custom dashboards "are set up by Suptask Support".

17.p: Custom ("Audit & Compliance", contents not documented); approval record from Professional
17.e: Pricing: "Audit & Compliance" ticked only for Custom. Approvals: "Any change from an approver, such as changing a decision from approved to rejected, is recorded in the ticket." Email page: "Full audit trail The sender, the assignee, the messages, and the resolution time are held on the email ticket". **Missing:** no documented log of who changed which field (owner, status) and when; immutability not stated. Edits are possible: "Requesters are allowed to edit their tickets after they have been submitted" (account setting); a Public reply can be withdrawn by editing the Slack message.

18.n: Knowledge-base answers and on-demand "similar tickets" exist. Missing: (a) automatic suggestions run as AI Assistants, which the help center calls "Custom plan and available in beta"; (b) similar past tickets appear only when an agent asks @Suptask, not as an automatic flag. AI is included in the plan price (see add-ons).
18.p: Pricing: Growth ("Answer from your knowledge base & documents", "Ask AI about tickets and insights"). Help center: Custom (Assistants)
18.e: "When a ticket comes in, the Assistant analyzes what's being asked, finds the most relevant answer in your connected knowledge". "Agent review - the Assistant posts a suggested answer for an agent to review, edit, and send." Ask @Suptask: "Similar tickets - What tickets are similar to this one?" "AI Assistants are a part of the Custom plan and available in beta."

19.n: Missing: (a) AI email routing is switched on by Suptask staff ("Contact your Suptask Integrations Specialist (SIS) to enable"); (b) AI tagging of Slack tickets runs as an AI Assistant (beta, Custom per the help center). Routing then uses automation rules. AI is included in the plan price.
19.p: Pricing: Growth ("Email AI categorisation & routing", "Automatic tagging and prioritization"). Help center: Custom (Assistants)
19.e: "When a new email comes in, our built in AI routing engine will evaluate the email and decide to which of the enabled AI email Forms to route the email to." Auto-tag: "an Assistant reads each incoming ticket, picks the closest Tag and Priority from your Form, and applies them". "Let the Assistant set the Tag, then let an automation rule assign or notify based on it."

20.n: Missing: (a) turning resolved tickets into knowledge is in alpha (Custom plan); (b) only closed-ticket summaries, searchable in Slack, are generally available. A connection to the scattered knowledge base (Notion) exists only through AI Assistants (beta). Outline: none.
20.p: Professional (AI problem and solution summary). Custom (AI Learnings, alpha)
20.e: "AI Learnings is a part of the Custom plan and available in alpha." "Suptask can learn from the tickets you resolve … suggest new knowledge … which agents then approve". "When a ticket is closed, Suptask AI analyzes the messages inside it and writes a summary of the problem and the solution … every summary is searchable in Slack".

21.n: The vendor MCP server is read-only, so the rule 7 Meets condition (read and act) is not met. The REST API can create and update tickets, but an API alone = Partial.
21.p: Professional (MCP article and pricing page; the AI overview says Custom/alpha, see header)
21.e: "The Suptask MCP is included in the new Professional plan and above. It is read-only. The assistant can look up and analyze your tickets, but it cannot create, update, reply to or close them - yet." "Suptask is now available as a connector in the Claude connector directory". Server: "https://ai.suptask.com/mcp-server".

22.n: A native Notion connector (OAuth) exists for AI answers. Missing: (a) it works only through AI Assistants (beta, Custom per the help center); (b) there is no client-facing support space in which to show Notion client documentation, because clients use email or Slack Connect.
22.p: Pricing: Growth ("AI Answers from Knowledge documents (Notion etc)"). Help center: Custom (Assistants)
22.e: "Once connected, the AI Assistant on an Inbox can use your Notion pages as a knowledge source and answer questions on tickets with information from your own documentation." "Each Inbox in Suptask has its own connector." "This connector can be used within the AI assistants you set up within Suptask."

23.p: Starter ("Submit tickets in Slack (Channels, DM & Groups)")
23.e: Native Slack app ("Official Certified Slack App", all plans). "Type /suptask, /request, /helpdesk, /support or /ticket to initiate the ticket creation." Private Form: "tickets are sent to the requester in a DM and are only accessible to the requester and the Agents in the Inbox." "Replying to tickets is done through Slack's own message threads … Any reply from the Agent on a ticket will also appear directly in the ticket thread."
23.s: [How to submit a ticket](https://support.suptask.com/working-with-tickets/for-users-who-submit-tickets/how-to-create-a-ticket), [Forms](https://support.suptask.com/setup-and-configure/forms-and-fields/what-are-ticket-forms-and-fields), [Ticketing as a user](https://support.suptask.com/getting-started/user-guides/ticketing-as-a-user), Pricing

24.n: A public REST API (OpenAPI v1.4.0) and webhooks exist. Missing: (a) webhooks are coarse, with 3 events only; (b) Suptask has no app marketplace of its own: "Integrations is a managed service offering", set up by Suptask staff and billed per integration.
24.p: Professional (pricing: "API & Webhooks"). The webhook guide says Custom (see header)
24.e: API operations: create, get, update, delete, reply, upload file, request approval, link external ticket, sync external message. Webhook "Events Created Ticket Updated Ticket New Reply/Comment on a Ticket". "Integrations is an add-on service managed by Suptask Integrations Specialist (SIS)."

25.n: Missing: Google Workspace SSO (SAML or Google sign-in) and 2FA for agents are not documented on any Suptask page read. The only login is with a Slack account, so SSO and 2FA would come from Slack's own settings (not verified). The Trust Center was blocked.
25.p: Growth ("Single-Sign On (SSO)" is ticked for Growth and Custom; no separate SSO subscription found)
25.e: Login page: "Sign in with the Slack account you use in your Suptask workspace. Sign in with Slack". MCP article: "Suptask uses Slack sign-in". Pricing: Growth includes "Single Sign-On".

26.p: All plans (vendor level; "SOC 2 Type II" ticked on all plans)
26.e: "SOC 2 & CSA Certified HIPAA BAA GDPR and DPA compliant". ISO 27001 is stated only for the hosting provider: "hosted within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Ireland (EU) and is covered by SOC2, ISO27001, ISO27017, ISO27018 and CSA. The complete list can be found here: https://aws.amazon.com/compliance/programs/". **Missing:** no vendor-held ISO 27001 found. Trust Center (trust.suptask.com) blocked. NIS2 documentation: not found.

27.e: Hosting: "Our technical solution is hosted within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Ireland (EU)". DPA §11.1: "The Processor may not transfer or authorize the transfer of Data to countries outside the EU and/or the European Economic Area (EEA) without the prior written consent of the Company." Subprocessors include "HelpCrunch Corporation (USA)" and "Userpilot (USA)". AI: "We partner with leading AI providers" (not named; no region). Tickets: "All messages are stored in Slack". **Missing:** backup location not stated (DPA gives only a deletion schedule); AI provider and processing region not stated; ticket messages sit in the customer's Slack workspace, outside Suptask's hosting.

28.n: No customer-set retention period or automatic deletion for tickets or attachments was found. Found only: manual deletion, a vendor-side policy (kept while the account is active, deleted after 24 months of inactivity), and a Free-plan limit.
28.e: "You can delete tickets from the Tickets overview … Be aware that deleting tickets is a irreversible operation." Privacy: "Data related to Suptask tickets created in your account is retained as long as your account is active." "Data is retained for 24 months for any inactive accounts before it is deleted." Free plan: "Limited to 3 months retention of tickets".

29.e: "An employee, user or a customer that can submit a ticket is considered a ticket requester. You can have an unlimited amount of this in Suptask without any additional cost." "Suptask do not charge for your Slack workspace users. Only those users who are identified as Agents."

30.n: A chat entry point in Slack (Messages tab) opens tickets, and users see the status of their own tickets in App Home. Missing: knowledge-base answers and conversation handling come from AI Assistants (beta, Custom per the help center). Pointing users to the right form is not documented.
30.p: Starter (Suptask App, Slackbot AI). Growth or Custom (KB answers, see header)
30.e: "Messages tab Send a message directly to the Suptask app in Slack. Suptask confirms the message and asks if a ticket should be created." "App Home … the service desk where requesters browse their tickets and submit to any Inbox." Auto-answer: "Requester can either continue their conversation with Suptask, resolve the ticket or escalate to an Agent."

31.n: in Slack, not a web portal; "Web Forms" are ticked on Custom only
31.p: Starter (App Home, every Inbox). Custom (customized App Home with links to other systems)
31.e: "Every Form in your Inbox is offered on the Suptask App." App Home: "the service desk where requesters browse their tickets and submit to any Inbox". "The content shown on the Suptask App home in Slack can be customized. Link to your internal wiki and policies". "Customization of Suptask App Home is a Custom feature."

32.n: Each client can have its own Slack Connect channel (the client must use Slack) or its own email address. Missing: per-client branding. Branding (app name, email layout) is account-wide. No client portal exists ("Web Forms" are Custom only). Setup from existing data (HubSpot) is not documented.
32.p: Professional (Slack Connect channels, Custom Email Branding)
32.e: "Each customer gets their own shared Slack Connect channel. This is where they will submit tickets and communicate with your team." "Your customers do not need to install anything." Email: "the email layout has your branding".

33.n: On-call works only through a partner Slack app (Tellspin) or the PagerDuty integration (a managed integration, see add-ons). Alerts reach people through Slack notifications. Push to Slack's mobile app was not verified on Suptask pages.
33.p: Professional (Automations, needed for the Tellspin setup). PagerDuty: managed integration (plan not stated)
33.e: "Tellspin and Suptask have established a technical partnership". "Suptask can automatically tag @Tellspin when a new ticket is created. Making the Agent who is on-call aware". PagerDuty: "Automatically create PagerDuty incidents when high-priority tickets are created." "On-call / on-duty rotation schedules can be enabled using one of our integrations".

34.n: the follower removes themselves with Unfollow; removal of a follower by an agent is not described
34.e: "Agents can add one or many users as a follower from across the Slack workspace". "The user will be able to reply in the ticket, as well as read the replies and the content of the ticket." "The user can select to Unfollow the ticket, which will stop the user from seeing any updates on the ticket".

35.n: GitHub, GitLab and Jira issues can be created from a ticket and linked to it. The API can link external tickets. Missing: structured links to Notion items (the Notion connector is for AI reading). Issue-tracker integrations are Custom plan, extra cost possible.
35.p: Custom ("Issue Trackers (Github etc)"). API "Link an external ticket": Professional
35.e: "After creating a related ticket in GitHub, the ticket message thread in Slack will receive the GitHub issue url, linking the both tickets together." GitHub guide: "Integrations is a part of the Custom plan. Additional cost might apply." "Link existing GitHub issues to Suptask tickets for full context."

36.e: "Conditional selection list is a Form field that enables dynamic, guided ticket submission through nested choices. Based on a user's selection, relevant follow-up fields automatically appear, while irrelevant options stay hidden." "Multiple nested levels are supported".

37.n: the business-team user needs the Suptask Admin role
37.e: Steps in the web app: "Create a new Form by selecting New form" → General → Intake sources → Fields → Ticket layout → Preview → "Save your Form and it will automatically be published and available in Slack". "Users who should have access to create and manage Inboxes and Forms will need to have the Suptask Admin role assigned."

38.n: A Form can be limited to the members of one Slack channel, but only as a "Public" Form, whose tickets are then visible in that channel. Missing: a "Private" Form limited to a group (Private Forms are available to everyone).
38.e: "Public - tickets are posted in the channel they were submitted from. The Form is only visible to that channel's members." "Private - tickets are sent to the requester in a DM … The Form is available to all requesters".

39.n: Missing: native checklists with an owner and due date per step. The documented workaround is one selection field per task. Ready-made forms can be imported.
39.e: "You can create effective task lists within a submitted ticket by utilizing custom fields within your form." "Create a new custom field with the field type Single-selection field … add the following values: Completed and Not completed". "Import industry-standard Forms into an Inbox with one click."

40.n: Access is per Inbox: separate Inboxes per team. Missing: limiting a ticket to its assigned agent and a manager within one Inbox.
40.e: "Only Agents that are added to an Inbox can access the tickets that have been submitted or moved to that Inbox." Private Form tickets "are only accessible to the requester and the Agents in the Inbox".

41.n: No CSV import of tickets was found. The only route is a custom build: a script reading the CSV and calling the API "Create a ticket" (POST /ticket).
41.e: API: "Create a ticket … Scope: tickets:write … Creates a ticket through a form." The bulk feature found covers editing only: "Assignee, priority, tags and status can all be changed in bulk."

42.n: Recurring tickets come from a Slack Workflow (Slack's own scheduler) posting into an auto-creation channel. Missing: a scheduler inside Suptask. One-off dates (for example a month before a renewal) and yearly frequency are not described.
42.e: "Slack Workflow will trigger the task on a set frequency (daily, weekly etc) and Suptask will pick up the task from the channel and turn it into a ticket." Article "Scheduled and recurring ticket creation": "Slack workflow that triggers on a schedule".

43.n: A native Google Sheets integration (built by Suptask, set up by Suptask staff) exists. Missing: sending on close is not documented (the example sends on creation). Custom plan, extra cost possible. Alternative: an automation with a webhook action to your own endpoint (custom build).
43.p: Custom (Google Sheets integration). Webhook action: Professional (pricing)
43.e: "Integrations is a part of the Custom plan. Additional cost might apply." "Ticket is created in Suptask … Suptask automatically pushes the ticket with all its options to the Google Sheet". "This integration can be customized to your needs where certain fields and syncing options can be adjusted."

44.n: Monitoring tools that post to Slack (or send email) create tickets automatically through an Automatic intake channel. Missing: "points to a solution" relies on AI Assistants (beta, Custom per the help center). The connection to client-hosted systems depends on each monitoring tool's Slack or email output (not verified).
44.e: "Errors and incidents - Sentry, PagerDuty, Opsgenie or an uptime monitor post a new issue and a ticket tracks the follow-up work after the pager stops." "That channel is an intake source on a Suptask Inbox with the creation mode Automatic." "For apps that only send email, use the Email source".

45.n: Filters on custom fields and date range exist. Missing: (a) there is no number or currency field type, so filtering by an amount (range) is not supported as documented; (b) a requester filter in the Tickets overview is not named (requester search is documented only through the MCP).
45.e: "Apply filters to display only the tickets matching your criteria, such as status, assignee, form or Inbox. This includes your Custom Fields." "Date range Limit the list to a time period". Field types: text, selection lists, Slack user, date, time, file. MCP: "search by text, requester, assignee, tag, priority, form or date".

46.n: Missing: a native time log or timer. The only documented route is a manual custom field filled at closing. The "Actual Time to Resolution" metric is elapsed time, not effort.
46.e: "Required on close - only required for Agents before the ticket can be closed, useful for data captured at resolution such as time spent or root cause". "Mark a form field as Only required on close … suited to time reporting".

47.n: SLA alerts, time-based rules and daily digests exist. Missing: a reminder that an agent sets on an individual ticket.
47.e: SLA: "Send a notification prior to a threshold breach", "Send an escalation notification". Time-based: "Time Since Last Reply Triggers when a ticket has not received a new reply within a specified amount of time." Digest: "how many tickets you have and when the tickets were last updated".

48.n: A person's requests can be listed through the MCP (Claude) or by asking @Suptask. Missing: a requester filter or person view in the Tickets overview is not documented. Requesters see only their own tickets.
48.e: MCP: "search by text, requester, assignee, tag, priority, form or date, without building a filter". Ask @Suptask: "Customer history - How many tickets from this customer were created last month?" Users: "You see only the tickets you have submitted."

49.n: The requester's manager can be found in Google Workspace for approvals. Missing: this is an AI Assistant lookup (beta, Custom plan), not a synced company structure. Approvals without AI use a fixed user or a Slack-user field picked on the form.
49.p: Custom ("AI Assistants are a part of the Custom plan"; "User Directories (Google Workspace etc)")
49.e: "It reads the request, looks up who should approve it - the requester's manager in Google Workspace". Sources: "Google Workspace Admin, Microsoft Entra, Okta, BambooHR, HiBob, HaileyHR". Automation approvers: "fixed users, the person selected in a Single Slack user field on the Form, or both".

50.n: No official Suptask app on Zapier (the Zapier page returned 404; a WebSearch found none). Routes: (a) Zapier's Slack action posts a message with field markers into an Automatic intake channel (documented by Suptask); (b) Suptask webhooks to a Zapier webhook (not described by Suptask).
50.e: "Zapier, Make, n8n or similar The app has no Slack integration but is supported by an automation platform. Add markers in the platform's Slack message action." "Integrations do not require any external product, such as Zapier or Make.com … You can optionally use an external product."

51.n: No Outline integration found. Routes: (a) upload Outline documents to Suptask as AI knowledge (AI Assistants, beta); (b) link Outline instructions in a "Static text" form field or the App Home; (c) a custom build on the API or webhooks. Outline's side was not verified.
51.p: Starter (static text). Growth or Custom (AI documents)
51.e: Outline is absent from the integrations page and the help center. AI knowledge: "Upload documents directly to Suptask, such as internal guides, policies, or FAQs." Field type "Static Text" for instructions.

52.n: A native HubSpot connector (built by Suptask) gives contact and company data on tickets. Missing: (a) it works only through AI Assistants in the Custom plan (beta), extra cost possible; (b) setting up a client's support space from HubSpot data is not documented.
52.e: "This integration is a part of AI workflows in the Custom Enterprise plan. Additional cost might apply." "HubSpot is connected through the Suptask app for HubSpot, built and maintained by Suptask." "see who the requester is, which company they belong to, who owns the account".

53.n: No Productive integration found. Route: a custom build on the Suptask API or webhooks. Productive's side was not verified.
53.e: Productive is absent from the integrations page, the list of integrations and the help center. Webhooks fire on "Created Ticket Updated Ticket New Reply/Comment on a Ticket".

54.n: Inbound from Zendesk is documented (a Suptask-built Zendesk app). Missing: for ServiceNow, only "sync" is listed, and inbound ticket creation is not explicit. It is a managed integration on the Custom plan. Email from a client's tool works as for any email.
54.e: Zendesk app: "Create tickets in Suptask directly from a Zendesk ticket." "Automatic links between Zendesk and Suptask tickets." ServiceNow: "Create ServiceNow incidents and tickets." "Sync ticket data between ServiceNow and Slack for consistent records." API: "Sync a message from an external ticket".

55.n: Tickets have a Due Date field. Missing: no calendar sync of deadlines was found. Route: a custom build (API and webhooks to the Google Calendar API, not verified).
55.e: "Add a Due Date field to a Form to give every ticket a deadline from the moment it is submitted." The Google Workspace connector covers access to "a shared drive, calendar or group alias", not ticket deadlines.

56.n: No Aboard integration found. Route: Aboard (or Zapier or Make on its behalf) posts a Slack message with field markers into an Automatic intake channel, which is the documented HRIS pattern. Alternatively, the API. Aboard's side was not verified.
56.e: "HRIS onboarding and offboarding - new hire or termination events from Rippling, HiBob, BambooHR or Personio become provisioning and offboarding tickets for IT." "Nobody in HR or IT typed anything. The ticket exists because the HRIS said so."

57.n: GDPR rights are handled manually by email to the DPO. Tickets can be deleted one by one (UI or API) and exported to CSV. Missing: an automated per-person erase and export.
57.e: "Contact us at dpo@suptask.com to delete, transfer or access your data." "Under GDPR, you have the right to: - Access … - Delete your data … - Data portability". "We will respond within 30 days." API: "Delete a ticket … Scope: tickets:delete".

58.n: Only one hosting location is stated, and no region choice was found. The ticket conversation is stored in the customer's Slack workspace, so it depends on Slack's data residency (not verified).
58.e: "Our technical solution is hosted within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Ireland (EU)". "Tickets are stored within your Slack Workspace, with minimal amount of data managed by Suptask."

59.n: list views; no kanban board found
59.p: Starter ("Ticket overview in Web", "Ticket overview in Slack")
59.e: "Agents will see all the unassigned tickets, or the tickets assigned to them." "You can save a combination of filters and columns as a preset view". "From the Tickets overview you can share a link with the applied filter of the current view."

questions: #4: Is the requester notified automatically at each approval step (e.g. "manager approved, waiting for Head of Finance")? Does an email requester get an email on every status change, not only on replies and closing?
#6: Is there a native task object inside a ticket (with assignee and due date), beyond the custom-field task list?

#13: Is one Inbox per client the supported way to restrict a client's tickets to the agents on that client's project? Is there a limit on the number of Inboxes? When a ticket moves between Inboxes, who keeps access to its history?

#17: What exactly does "Audit & Compliance" (Custom plan) include? Is there a log of every field change (assignee/owner, status, priority) with user and timestamp, and can entries be edited or deleted? Since ticket messages live in Slack, are message edits and deletions recorded?

#26: Does Suptask (Happyning AB) hold its own ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, and for which scope? Which CSA level is held (STAR Level 1 or Level 2)? Can you share the SOC 2 Type II report and NIS2 supply-chain documentation (trust.suptask.com was blocked for us)?
#27: Where are backups stored? Which AI providers process ticket data, and in which region? Apart from AWS Ireland and Slack, is any ticket content stored elsewhere?

Data in Slack: ticket messages are stored in the customer's Slack workspace. Can Slack workspace owners or admins read private Responder channels and requester DMs? How do Slack retention settings affect the ticket history?
People data: the DPA forbids "health data, racial/ethnic data, or other sensitive data without prior agreement". What does that prior agreement involve for HR requests?
Pricing: is the "$" price in USD? Is EUR billing available?
AI: are the Growth-plan AI features generally available, or still beta?
#7: Does Suptask keep a per-ticket history of assignee changes (who, when, old and new value)? On which plan, and is it part of "Audit & Compliance" (Custom)?
#11: Can one ticket create several linked child tickets in other Inboxes that run in parallel, with their status visible on the parent ticket?

#18, #19, #22, #30, #44, #49: Are AI Assistants (auto-answer, auto-tag, connectors such as Notion, dynamic approvals) generally available? Are they included in Growth (as the pricing page shows) or only in Custom (as the help center says: "Custom plan and available in beta")?
#19: Is AI email routing generally available on Growth, or only switched on by a Suptask Integrations Specialist on request?
#20: When will "AI Learnings" (knowledge from resolved tickets) leave alpha, on which plan, and can it write into Notion?
#21: When will the Suptask MCP support creating and updating tickets? Is the MCP part of Professional (MCP article) or Custom/alpha (AI overview page)?
#24: Are webhooks available on Professional (pricing page) or only on Custom (webhook guide)? Are more webhook events planned (status change, assignment, approval)?
#25: How do agents log in with Google Workspace SSO and enforced 2FA? Is it only through Slack's own SSO and 2FA, and what does "Single Sign-On" on Growth add?
#28: Can an admin set a retention period after which tickets and attachments in Suptask (and the related Slack threads) are deleted automatically?
#35: Can tickets hold structured links to Notion pages (not only AI reading), and on which plan?
#43: Can the Google Sheets integration (or an automation) send ticket data when a ticket is closed, and what does it cost?
#45, #48: Can the Tickets overview filter by requester, and can a number or amount field be added and filtered by range?
#52: Can a client's channel or Organization value be created from HubSpot company data, and on which plan?
#54: Can a ticket created in a client's ServiceNow create a Suptask ticket automatically (inbound), and what does the integration cost?
#57: Is there a tool to find, export and delete all data of one person, beyond an email request to dpo@suptask.com?
#58: Can Suptask store data outside AWS Ireland (for example the US or India), per client or per account?
Trust Center (https://trust.suptask.com) was blocked: please send the SOC 2 report scope, the subprocessor list and the DPA, and say whether AI processing stays in the EU.
checks: Re-checked the sequential approvals quote on the Suptask help centre. #10 Meets stands; the manager is chosen in a form field (automatic manager lookup is requirement #49, assessed separately).
Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 10 / Partial 6.
Re-checked: the Suptask MCP "cannot create, update, reply to or close" tickets (help centre export, support.suptask.com/llms-full.txt). #21 Partial stands (read-only, same rule as TOPdesk #21).
Counts recomputed by script: Meets 8 / Partial 33 / Unknown 2; Musts: Meets 3 / Partial 9 / Unknown 1. Beta and alpha features (#18, #19, #20, #22) are Partial under the generally-available rule.

1.e: "Email (your current support email account) HelpSpot is optimized for email-based exchanges". "Every request has a complete log of all actions taken and messages sent." "HelpSpot appends the request ID to every outgoing message for the logging replies in the request history." Request history also logs "request detail changes".

2.e: "Unlimited Mailboxes Connect as many email accounts as you need. No limits, no extra charges." Per mailbox: "Default Category — The category assigned to new requests received through this mailbox." "the Inbox is home to all unassigned requests … Users can take a request from the Inbox by simply clicking on the Take It button".

3.e: Mailbox setting: "Enable Auto Reply — Send an automatic reply when a customer creates a new request through this mailbox." Trigger-based auto-replies can add conditions, e.g. separate "business hours" and "outside business hours" replies.

4.e: Replies: "Customers receive email notices only when a public note is used." Status changes: triggers run "anytime a request is created or updated" and can "Send email notifications to staff, customers, and/or external recipients" (must be configured, not default). **Missing:** no approval flow was found (#10), so there are no approval-step notifications.

5.e: "Private Note … These notes are logged within the request history however, no email is sent to the Customer (nor is there an option to send the note via CC or BCC)." On the portal, customers see "public update entries and the initial request".

6.e: "@ Allows staff members to be tagged by name in a request note. Tagged staff members will receive a notification." Staff can "subscribe to notifications on future updates" and set reminders. "Real-time collision detection". **Missing:** no tasks inside a ticket and no threaded comments documented. Single-owner model: "every ticket is either unassigned or owned by exactly one person".

7.n: changes are recorded in the request history; the Audit Log does not list assignment changes
7.e: "Reassign. Users can opt to assign a new category and Staffer to the selected requests." "Every action completed on a request is logged within the request history", each entry with "User name" and "Description of request detail change". Filter conditions: "Reassigned from/to … Reassigned by". Audit Log covers admin settings, logins, reports and "merging, trashing, marking as spam, and deleting".

8.e: "HelpSpot offers the flexibility of creating customized status type … By default, HelpSpot provides 5 status types." Statuses are added in one system-wide list ("Add a New Status box"). **Missing:** a separate status set per process or category is not documented (category settings cover staff, auto-assignment, reporting tags and custom fields only).

9.e: Field types include "Predefined List", "Drill Down List", "Date Field", "Date and Time Field", "Numeric Field". "you can attach the custom field to particular categories. The requests in the categories selected will be the only requests that present those custom fields." "You can also choose to make a custom field required." Fields can be made public "on the public customer portal". Secondary portals (per department, group or brand) can include or exclude "Public Categories" and "Public Custom fields", which supports per-client forms.

10.e: No approval feature found in the Admin, Users or API Manuals, the llms-full.txt feature list or the pricing page. The vendor KB search returns "Search: approval (0)". This is missing documentation, not a vendor statement that approvals are absent.

11.e: "Converting creates a new request and links it to the original history item so context is preserved." One instance can serve several departments "when teams may need to share workflows or pass requests between departments". **Missing:** automatic creation of a linked request for another team (e.g., by a trigger) and the status of sub-requests shown in the parent are not documented.

12.e: "Once logged in, Customers will see a list of all requests they have (opened and closed)". CC'd people: "the recipient will continue to be included on all public updates until the address is removed." Caveat: one request can also be opened with "the request access key, which is provided by default in the emails". Access keys can be disabled with SAML forced on the portal (Admin Manual §17.1).

13.e: Desks: "Create limited permission groups so department staff only see requests in their assigned categories." Moving tickets between desks is supported ("passed back and forth between departments"). **Missing:** "Any admin in the system can access all requests." No documented per-client visibility rule inside the Platform desk (one category per client would be a workaround; not documented). Stronger separation needs a "separate HelpSpot instance per department" (price per instance not stated).

14.e: "Mail Rules are run when an incoming email is read"; "Triggers are run anytime a request is created or updated"; Automation Rules "are run periodically". Zapier: "Actions can be triggered from HelpSpot and requests can be created and updated based on other Zapier apps."

15.e: No SLA policy object documented. SLAs are built from filters and automation rules. Examples: an escalation where requests "must be responded to within 24 hours", and "Notification: Request due tomorrow" (custom date field). Docs: "There is no business-hours condition. First Response Speed (biz hours) exists as a display column and a sort option, but not as something you can filter on." B2B page (marketing): "SLA timers start automatically." **Missing:** first-response and resolution targets per priority as a policy. Business-hours targets cannot be used in rules.

16.e: "Productivity Overview … first response and closing speeds". "First Response Speed". "Resolution Speed Time taken (in hours) for a request to be closed". Both can use "business hours or 24 hour period". Also a Todayboard, saved and scheduled reports, CSV export, and queue views (Inbox, My Queue, filters with "Display count in Workspace"). Direct SQL access only on self-hosted.

17.e: "Every action completed on a request is logged within the request history", including "Description of request detail change". The Audit Log covers admin setting changes, logins, and merge, trash, spam and delete actions, with "The user name and IP address associated with every logged change". **Missing:** entries are not stated to be immutable. The Audit Log "can be turned off" and keeps entries for at most "730 days (2 years)". Customer Tools deletions are "permanent", and "detailed information about the deleted item is not logged". No approvals exist to log.

18.e: AI Composer: "Reviews the current ticket conversation Pulls in relevant customer information References any linked knowledge base articles"; agents "Optionally link one or more knowledge base articles." "AI features are included with every HelpSpot subscription." **Missing:** suggestions drawn from past tickets and a flag that a similar problem came up before are not documented; KB context is only what the agent links.

19.e: "HelpSpot AI will train on your own request history to then automatically categorize requests in selected categories." "Once a request is auto categorized it can also be auto assigned to a staff member." Needs "at least 10 closed requests in any selected category"; "Works best with 50 or fewer categories".

20.e: "This feature allows an agent to transform a public response within a request into a structured knowledge base article ready for review and publication." The draft is saved "as a private (unpublished) draft". **Missing:** connecting the result with the existing scattered KB (Notion, Outline) is not documented (see #22).

21.n: vendor MCP server, GA since v5.8.0, included
21.e: "HelpSpot MCP connects your existing AI agents, such as Claude or ChatGPT, directly to HelpSpot." Write tools: "create-request-tool (write) — Create a new request"; "update-request-tool (write) — Add notes, change status, reassign, and more." "JUN 09 2026 v5.8.0 … HelpSpot now ships a built-in MCP server". Guides for Claude Desktop and Claude Code. Off by default ("Default: Off").

22.e: No Notion integration found on helpspot.com or in the manuals; the Zapier pair page returned 404 and the HelpSpot Zapier app has no KB actions (actions: "Create a New Request", "Update an Existing Request"). Route: an agent that reads Notion and writes to the HelpSpot KB through MCP: "create-book-page-tool (write) — Create a new page in a chapter." AI Composer uses only "linked knowledge base articles" from HelpSpot.

23.e: No native Slack app. Route 1, Zapier: the official HelpSpot Zapier app has triggers "New Request" and "Updated Request", actions "Create a New Request" and "Update an Existing Request", and the template "Get Slack channel notifications for new HelpSpot requests". Intake: the vendor guide builds a custom Slack slash command, then Zapier Webhooks, then "Create a New Request". Route 2, custom build: webhooks, with an example "to send notifications to Slack on GitHub". **Missing:** two-way sync of replies and status to Slack, a private requester–agent thread in Slack, and requester notifications in Slack. Zapier needs "a publicly accessible URL" (relevant if self-hosted).

24.e: API: "Full CRUD access to tickets, users, categories, custom fields, and more." Webhooks: "Webhooks can be called when a set of conditions are met in a trigger, automation rule or a mail rule … HelpSpot sends all the information it has about the request". **Missing:** no app marketplace found. Ready integrations listed are Zapier, Formstack ("maintained by Formstack"), Thermostat and sample scripts.

25.e: "SAML SSO Azure AD, Google Workspace, Okta, or any SAML 2.0 provider." Google guide: "Google Suite SAML Authentication … Within Google admin for your organization: … SAML Apps". "Helpspot supports native 2fa authentication for staff members when using HelpSpot's internal authentication." 2FA is switched on per user; admin enforcement is not documented.

26.e: "Our SOC 2 work is in progress. We have not completed our SOC 2 examination. The AWS reports described below apply to our hosting infrastructure, not to a completed HelpSpot examination." The listed SOC 1/2/3 and ISO 27001/27017/27018 belong to AWS. No ISO 27001 for UserScape found. In business since 2005. Certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. NIS2 documentation: not found. DPA: not found (KB search "DPA" returns 0 results). Self-hosting does not change this verdict.

27.e: Hosting and backups: "EU Cloud is hosted on AWS Frankfurt (eu-central-1) … Your database, files, and all backups are completely contained within the European Union." "Database backed up every 5 minutes, all within EU region". **Missing:** where AI is processed. "Text is processed through AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic)", with no region stated. AI request summaries and out-of-office detection are "turned on by default for new customers". The privacy policy (scope: "www.helpspot.com (the "Services")") says: "we transfer the information, including Personal Information, to United States and process it there". If self-hosted, hosting and backups are under our control, but AI still goes to "HelpSpot AI Services", so the verdict is unchanged.

28.e: "Requests in the Trash are deleted automatically after the number of days set in Admin > Settings > System > Delete requests after this many days in the trash." "Administrators can choose from 1 day-never." **Missing:** a retention period for open or closed tickets and their attachments (automatic move to Trash) is not documented; no Trash action was found in the automation docs. Self-hosted only: CLI "php hs request:delete --id=1234" (per ID), which does not change the verdict.

29.e: "Agents are staff members who log into HelpSpot to manage tickets, run reports, or administer the system. Customers never need licenses and there are no limits on ticket volume."

30.e: Vendor: "HelpSpot is an email/portal-first platform. Teams that need Intercom-style inline messenger widgets as their main channel should pick a chat-first tool." AI feature list: "AI Composer, categorization, summaries, translation, knowledge base drafts, and the MCP server" (no requester-facing assistant). Slack only via Zapier. Only route: a custom build on the public API ("request.create … customer.getRequests … kb.search").

31.e: Category "Visibility: This setting will control whether a category is available on public request forms." "The HelpSpot portal is fully customizable to allow integration with any website or intranet." On a hosted trial "you'll need to contact support to enable editing of portal templates". **Missing:** no service catalog feature; links to requests handled in other systems (Aboard) only by editing HTML/PHP templates.

32.e: "Support multiple brands, departments, or clients from a single HelpSpot installation. Each brand gets its own portal, mailbox, email templates, and design." "Separate portal with unique URL per brand (subdomain or custom domain)". Limit: "Secondary portals currently all share logins with the primary portal." **Missing:** quick setup reusing existing data (e.g., from HubSpot) is not documented.

33.n: SMS; push not stated; on-call tool only via Zapier
33.e: "HelpSpot allows Users to send all notification (that would typically go to an email account) to an SMS enabled device. Users can opt to select to send all notifications or only urgent ones." "HelpSpot has both iOS (iPhone / iPad) and Android mobile applications available." Zapier: "so Slack, Jira, PagerDuty, and other Zapier apps can join the workflow".

34.e: "As the assigned user of a request you can also subscribe another user to the request using the option in the staff notification area of the request." "Subscription and reminders can be removed from this screen." API: "private.request.subscribe", "private.request.unsubscribe". Note: whether a subscriber outside the request's category can open it is not stated.

35.e: Request Push: "push a request out of HelpSpot into another system … bug trackers, CRM tools, Intranets"; "If a unique ID is provided HelpSpot will make available a link in the request where an update can be retrieved". It needs custom code ("Once you've created a Request Push API file"). **Missing:** no native Notion or GitHub link integration; GitHub appears only as a Zapier pair app.

36.e: "Drill Down List - Creates multiple levels of dropdown lists that are dependent on the parent selection." "When creating a custom field you can attach the custom field to particular categories. The requests in the categories selected will be the only requests that present those custom fields." Fields can be public on the portal.

37.e: Categories and custom fields are set up in the Admin UI (Admin > Categories, Admin > Custom Fields). External no-code form: "Formstack's HelpSpot integration is maintained by Formstack". **Missing:** letting a business team edit only its own forms is not documented; "Any admin in the system can access all requests"; portal form layout is edited in HTML/PHP templates.

38.e: Secondary portals are for "custom portals for different departments, groups or brands"; per portal admins "can choose to exclude/include: … Public Categories Public Custom fields". **Missing:** restricting who can open a portal or form: "Secondary portals currently all share logins with the primary portal … use Black Box logins to enforce your own login logic" (custom code).

39.e: Responses act as templates: "Insert a response and watch the ticket transform. Status, category, custom fields, note type, CC recipients, email subject." Recurring requests come "with category, assignee, and status preset". **Missing:** a checklist inside a request with per-step owners and due dates was not found.

40.e: "Can view own requests ONLY This is a very limiting permission allowing a user to only view their own requests". "Create limited permission groups so department staff only see requests in their assigned categories." **Missing:** a visibility setting on an individual ticket; control is per permission group and category, and "Any admin in the system can access all requests."

41.e: No CSV import of requests found. Route 1, API: "private.request.create … You can use this method to import requests from other systems by making sure you set email_from to 0". Route 2, Zapier action "Create a New Request" fed from a spreadsheet app.

42.e: "Turn a saved response into a scheduled ticket: daily, workdays, weekly, monthly, quarterly, twice a year, or yearly, with category, assignee, and status preset." Date-based: "By combining a custom date field with an automation rule … requests automatically return to your queue when they need attention" (reopens an existing request).

43.e: Route 1: a trigger on status change with a webhook: "HelpSpot sends all the information it has about the request to the URL you specify" (needs a receiving endpoint). Route 2: Zapier ("Google Sheets logging"; trigger on request update). **Missing:** no native spreadsheet or register action.

44.e: Mail rules: "Categorize system alerts automatically." Email parser: "If you need to create requests in remote systems you can add a few basic tags to an email you generate". Zapier template: "Generate HelpSpot requests from new down alerts in Updown.io". **Missing:** no native monitoring integration; pointing to a solution automatically is not documented.

45.e: Filter conditions: customer "Email"; custom fields "Number, Decimal Is / Less than / Greater than"; dates "Opened Before Date, Opened After Date, Closed Before Date, Closed After Date". CSV export: "There is no row limit". Self-hosted adds direct SQL access.

46.e: "Each request (after it's created) will now have a time tracking bar at the top for managing that requests time." "2 new reports will be available … time reporting by customer and staff". Must be enabled in Admin > Settings.

47.e: Column "Age … How long ago the request was opened"; condition "Wait Time Since Last Customer Update (minutes)". "Automation Rules can be used to identify stale or inactive tickets and automatically send reminders to staff." "Reminders are emailed at the designated date/time to selected Users".

48.e: "HelpSpot automatically checks for other open tickets from the same customer and surfaces their complete history. Search by email address, company domain, or customer ID". "See all past requests from the same person".

49.e: "Live Lookup can show it in the ticket: a user's department, manager, assigned computer, and office. It calls a small script you configure". "Can fill custom fields when a request arrives". Sample script: Azure AD. **Missing:** no ready connector for Google Workspace or Aboard; using the manager for approvals is not documented.

50.p: Single plan (needs the private API enabled)
50.e: Zapier app triggers: "New Request", "Update … Triggers when a request is updated"; actions: "Create a New Request", "Update an Existing Request". "You can add the HelpSpot app here (https://zapier.com/apps/helpspot/integrations)".

51.e: No Outline integration found on helpspot.com or in the manuals. Route: webhooks plus the HelpSpot API, or Zapier. The Outline side was not verified.

52.e: No HubSpot integration found; Zapier pair page 404. Route: Live Lookup script against the CRM ("Live Lookup pulls account data from CRM"; "HelpSpot sends all available customer information and custom field values to a script written by an Administrator"). **Missing:** setting up a client's support space from HubSpot data. The HubSpot side was not verified.

53.e: No Productive integration found. Route: API time methods "private.request.getTimeEvents", "private.timetracker.search" plus webhooks. The Productive side was not verified.

54.e: No ServiceNow integration found. Route 1, email: "your remote system can email requests with tags to the same accounts you already use for support". Route 2, API "private.request.create". The client-tool side was not verified.

55.e: No calendar integration found; Zapier pair page for Google Calendar 404. Route: date custom fields plus a webhook ("HelpSpot sends all the information it has about the request to the URL you specify") or Zapier to a calendar API. The calendar side was not verified.

56.e: No Aboard integration found. Route: an Aboard event calls "private.request.create" or the Zapier action "Create a New Request". The Aboard side (API, Zapier app) was not verified.

57.e: "GDPR Data Export Export all data relating to a customer with one click." "Right to Erasure Delete all data related to a customer ID or email." Docs: "Customer Deletion … This will delete all requests and attachments found for this customer". Note: the export covers "all request details and public notes as well as public attachments" (private notes not stated).

58.e: "US Cloud CLOUD US-EAST REGION"; "EU Cloud CLOUD FRANKFURT REGION"; "Self-Hosted". "Every customer gets a dedicated server in their chosen datacenter, with isolated database and storage." One region per instance, so per-client regions need separate instances. No India cloud region. Self-hosting allows any location but is still a separate instance, so the verdict stays Partial.

59.e: "Once a User clicks My Queue, the request grid … will load all the open requests assigned to that User." Team view: "A team wants an inbox-style queue of unassigned requests in their category that members can claim directly." Filters can be shared with permission groups.

questions: #10: Does HelpSpot have a native multi-step approval workflow on requests, for example the requester's manager and then the Head of Finance, with the business justification and each decision recorded? If not, what pattern do you recommend, and does an approver need an agent licence?
#4: If approvals exist, does the requester get an automatic notification at each approval step?

#23: Is there a native Slack app, or one on the roadmap, that lets a non-agent employee raise a private ticket from Slack and syncs replies and status changes both ways? Is anything beyond Zapier or a custom webhook build supported?

#27: For EU Cloud customers, in which region do OpenAI and Anthropic process AI requests (translation, summaries, composer, auto-categorization)? Can all AI features be switched off so that no data leaves the EU?

#27: The privacy policy says personal information is transferred to and processed in the United States. Does this apply to help-desk data in EU Cloud, for example US support staff access, outbound email delivery or Cloudflare? Please send the subprocessor list and the DPA.

#26: When will the SOC 2 examination be completed, and is it Type I or Type II? Do you plan ISO 27001 certification? What supply-chain documentation can you give a NIS2 "important entity" (security questionnaire, incident-notification terms, DPA)?

#15: Is there an SLA policy feature with first-response and resolution targets per priority, business hours and a warning before a breach? Or are SLAs only built with filters and automation rules? The B2B page says "SLA timers start automatically".

#17: Can administrators edit or delete request-history or Audit Log entries? Can the Audit Log be kept longer than 730 days or locked so it cannot be switched off? Are ownership changes recorded in the Audit Log or only in the request history?
#13: Can visibility inside one desk (Platform) be limited per client project, other than one category per client? Can administrators be prevented from seeing People/HR requests?
#6: Can a ticket have tasks or sub-tasks assigned to other agents, or threaded internal discussions?
#8: Can a status list be limited to one category or process, or are statuses always global?
#11: Can a trigger or rule create a linked request in another category (e.g., HR onboarding → IT equipment), and can the parent show the status of linked requests?
#18: Does any built-in AI feature search past resolved requests to suggest a solution or flag a similar earlier issue, beyond the KB articles an agent links?
#20 / #22: Can HelpSpot AI use an external knowledge base (Notion or Outline), or must content be copied into HelpSpot knowledge books?
#24: Is there a catalogue or marketplace of ready-made integrations beyond Zapier, Formstack and Thermostat?
#28: Can an automation rule move requests (with attachments) to Trash after a set age, so that Trash auto-deletion gives a retention period? How long do deleted requests stay in EU Cloud backups?
#30: Is any requester-facing chat or AI assistant (portal or Slack) available or planned?
#31 / #32 / #38: On EU Cloud, can admins create secondary portals and edit portal templates themselves, and can a portal or category be restricted to a group of requesters (e.g., managers via SAML)?
#33: Does the mobile app send push notifications, and how is SMS delivered to staff in the EU?
#37: Can a non-admin business user (e.g., People) manage the categories and custom fields of their own team only?
#39: Is there a checklist inside a request with steps, owners and due dates?
#40: Can visibility be set on an individual request (assigned agent plus a manager only)?
#49 / #52: Are there ready Live Lookup scripts for Google Workspace directory and HubSpot, or must we write them?
#58: Can one subscription run several cloud instances in different regions (US, EU), and is any other region (e.g., India) available?
checks: Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 7 / Partial 8 / Unknown 1.
#10 is Unknown, not "Does not meet": no approval feature was found in the manuals and the KB search returned 0 results, but no page states that approvals are absent (same rule as other vendors).
#26 Partial: HelpSpot's own SOC 2 is "in progress" and the listed ISO 27001 belongs to AWS (Notes #13: "Immature vendors without certifications are out").

Re-checked: "HelpSpot MCP connects your existing AI agents, such as Claude or ChatGPT, directly to HelpSpot", with write tools "create-request-tool" and "update-request-tool" (KB article 921). #21 Meets stands.

#30 "Does not meet" accepted: the vendor itself says teams that need a messenger widget "should pick a chat-first tool", and its AI feature list has no requester-facing assistant (same logic as Atomicwork in the filter).

1.e: "Connect Zammad to your email provider so that it can watch your inbox"; Filters: "Make sure new tickets show up in the right place … for all incoming email"; "working on existing tickets means keeping up with a customer correspondence in a thread/conversation in the ticket detail view"; History: "comprehensive list of updates to the ticket, performed by any user, since its creation".

2.e: Pricing table: "Email unlimited addresses yes yes yes". Filters: "Make sure new tickets show up in the right place with automated, if-this-then-that rules for all incoming email." Overviews work as a shared queue, for example "Unassigned and open".

3.e: "Zammad ships one active trigger by default: an auto reply trigger which sends an email to the customer after a new ticket is created."

4.e: Triggers can "Send an email or SMS Either to the customer, the agent who owns the ticket, or every agent in the system" when conditions match (e.g. a state change). Agent replies go to the customer by email ("Reply: … The recipient is automatically pre-filled"). Missing: the only trigger shipped by default is the auto reply, so status-change notifications must be built as triggers. Approval-step notifications are not possible because there is no approval feature (#10).
