5.e: "Note: Write a reminder for yourself and other agents … The default visibility is “internal”, which means the customer can’t see the note."

6.e: "Mention colleagues by typing @ @ followed by their name to ask a question or notify them"; internal notes to "ask a colleague a question"; checklist: "Use a checklist in tickets to keep track of the tasks to be completed"; History "Useful to check who did what and when". Note: the conversation is one chronological list of articles, with no nested threads. The checklist is not listed on the pricing table.

7.p: Starter v2 ("Ticket history" on all plans)
7.e: "Owner This is the person who is currently responsible for the ticket. In case you need information from another colleague, you can either change the owner to this person or mention the person". History: "See a comprehensive list of updates to the ticket, performed by any user, since its creation. Useful to check who did what and when."

8.n: Custom states are documented, but states are global. Limiting the states offered per process (for example per group) is not documented. Core Workflows can "Set available options for select fields" (Plus v2), but no page shows this for the State field.
8.p: Not stated for states (Professional v2 lists "Individual ticket objects"). Plus v2 for Core Workflows
8.e: "If the pre-configured states aren't enough for you or you want to change them, you can do so by clicking on the cogwheel icon in the state row". "In the state configuration screen, you can add new states, disable states or change states."

9.p: Plus v2 (Core Workflows; "Individual fields For tickets, user and organization" from Professional v2)
9.e: Field types: "Date Field", "Date & Time Field", "Single Selection Field Provides a field with pre-defined values". Core Workflows: "Show and hide fields", "Adjust if fields are mandatory or not", "Set available options for select fields", "distinguish between different roles or groups". Caveat: on Professional v2 (custom fields without Core Workflows), per-group required or hidden fields are not documented. Forms per client: not documented, possible only through group conditions (my inference).

10.e: A Zammad collaborator closed community PR #6264 ("Feature: Ticket approval workflow") with: "There may be a dedicated approval workflow engine in Zammad in the future" and "Many of these can be met through the clever use of triggers, custom attributes and core workflows." The admin docs have no approvals page. A do-it-yourself build is possible (Core Workflows need Plus v2), but no recipe is documented.

11.n: Parent/child links are manual. Missing: automatic creation of a ticket in another team's group (for example onboarding → IT), the status of sub-tickets shown in the parent, and linking across groups an agent cannot access.
11.e: "There are different types of links between tickets … parent/child links and normal links." "If you have a main issue and want to create sub tasks, you could link to the main one as a parent of the sub tickets."

12.e: "Shared Organization If you set this option to yes, all organization members will be able to view and update tickets of their organizational members in addition to their own." "The default value on creation dialogs is yes." Missing: there is no explicit statement on default customer visibility. Seeing only own tickets requires Shared Organization = no for internal employees. Access for people added to a ticket (CC) is not documented.

13.p: Starter v2 (user-based group permissions; "Individual roles" from Professional v2)
13.e: "Use the group permission table to grant per-group privileges"; "Read: View, search for and find tickets"; "Create: Create new tickets and move existing tickets into the group". Caveat: separating clients means one group per client project. This is a configuration choice, not a separate client object.

14.n: for built-in if/then rules. The Zapier complement is weak: no official Zapier app was found (see #50).
14.e: Pricing table: "Trigger & Schedulers yes yes yes". Trigger example: "Activated by: Action … Conditions for affected objects: Action is created Execute changes on objects". Scheduler: "Zammad's scheduler performs time-based automated actions."

15.e: Multiple SLAs, each with a "Ticket Selector … filter tickets by checking their attributes, e.g. customer, organization or group"; "First Response", "Solution Time"; "Zammad will warn agents roughly 15 minute before escalation"; there is a trigger event "Escalation warning is reached". Missing: no configurable warning lead time (e.g. one day earlier) is documented. SLA by priority is not named explicitly (the examples list customer, organization and group).

16.p: Plus v2 ("Zammad Standard Reporting" is listed only under Plus v2)
16.e: Reporting: "You can filter by status (“Ticket Count”), “Creation Channels” and “Communication” types"; download "in a .xlsx spreadsheet" (max "6.000 entries"). Agent dashboard: "∅ Waiting Time Today", "Mood How many escalated tickets", "Reopening Rate". Default overview "Escalated Tickets" (queue view). Missing: no first-response-time or resolution-time report is documented in standard reporting. Deeper reporting needs "Elasticsearch access via Grafana" (Plus v2).

17.p: Starter v2 ("Ticket history"); plan for the Audit Logs page not listed
17.e: Ticket History: "comprehensive list of updates to the ticket, performed by any user, since its creation. Useful to check who did what and when." Audit Logs: "The audit log is read-only. It does not record day-to-day ticket updates." Missing: the docs do not say that ticket history cannot be edited. Owner changes are not named explicitly. Authors can delete own articles "not older than 10 minutes". Audit log entries are deleted after "12 months. This retention period is not configurable."

18.n: Suggestions come from the knowledge base only. Missing: suggestions from past tickets and a "similar problem came up before" flag. Paid per use: Zammad AI costs €0.03 per AI call; a bring-your-own provider is billed by that provider.
18.p: Professional v2 ("Possibility of using AI features (optional)")
18.e: "Zammad's knowledge base assistant helps your agents find existing knowledge base answers for incoming tickets". "Zammad shows existing knowledge base answers whose content matches the ticket in the Related Knowledge section of the ticket sidebar."

19.n: Paid per use: €0.03 per AI call with Zammad AI. Agents run only when a trigger, scheduler job or macro invokes them.
19.e: "Ticket Categorizer This AI agent is capable of assigning categories to tickets." "Ticket Group Dispatcher This AI agent is capable of assigning tickets to different groups." "AI agents don't run on their own. They have to be invoked by a trigger, a scheduler job or a macro".

20.n: Drafting KB answers from a ticket is documented. Missing: connecting the result to the existing scattered knowledge base (Notion, Outline). No such integration was found (see #22, #51).
20.p: Professional v2 (monolingual KB; multilingual on Plus v2)
20.e: "The agent can ask the AI to draft a new knowledge base answer from the ticket's content". "The knowledge base answer is generated as a draft and is not published automatically."

21.n: reviewer correction: was "Meets"; Claude can only be the provider for Zammad's built-in AI agents, which change category, group, priority and tags; there is no vendor MCP server, and connecting an own external agent needs a custom build on the REST API, so rule 7 is not met in full
21.p: Professional v2 (AI features). Use of a non-Zammad provider on SaaS is implied by the FAQ, not stated outright
21.e: Provider "Type … Available options: Zammad AI OpenAI Ollama Anthropic Azure AI … Mistral AI Custom (OpenAI Compatible)". AI FAQ: "Supported models and providers: Zammad AI OpenAI Ollama Anthropic". "If an AI agent applies changes to a ticket, you can find an entry in the ticket history". API: "REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

22.n: (custom build on the public API). No Notion integration in the integrations list. Route: sync Notion pages into the Zammad KB through the REST API. The KB assistant answers only from the Zammad KB. No official Zapier app was found (#50).
22.e: Integrations list: phone systems, "Clearbit Exchange LDAP / Active Directory PGP S/MIME", monitoring, "GitHub GitLab", "i-doit Elasticsearch (SaaS)". No Notion. API: "REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

23.p: Starter v2 (triggers; webhooks not listed on pricing)
23.e: Notifications to Slack only, set up as "a webhook for receiving Zammad notifications in a Slack channel" through Slack's "Incoming WebHooks" app and a pre-defined webhook: "whenever a ticket is escalated or has reached escalation warning … a suitable notification will be posted". The integrations list has no Slack entry. zapier.com/apps/zammad/integrations returned 404. Missing: no ticket intake from Slack, no private Slack tickets and no two-way sync. Route for those: a custom build on the Zammad API.

24.n: REST API and webhooks are documented. Missing: no app marketplace was found, only a fixed list of built-in integrations.
24.p: Not stated on the pricing table (API and webhooks)
24.e: "Zammad provides a powerful REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well." Authentication by token or "OAuth2 (token access)". Webhooks: "allowing them to subscribe to live updates about tickets"; "Webhooks have to be triggered by Trigger or Scheduler jobs" (conditions make them fine-grained); "possible to further customize the webhook payload".

25.n: No separate SSO subscription is listed, but the plan for SSO is not stated.
25.p: 2FA: Starter v2. SSO (Google, SAML): not stated on the pricing table
25.e: "Your users can log in with an account they already have, for example their Google or Microsoft account". Login providers include "Google … OpenID Connect SAML SSO". 2FA: "Security Keys Authenticator App"; enforcement "by selecting specific user roles in the Enforced for user roles setting". Pricing table: "Two-factor authentication (2FA) yes yes yes".

26.p: Starter v2 (pricing table: "ISO27001 certified yes yes yes")
26.e: "Zammad GmbH has been awarded ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification" (2026-06-18); scope: "The certification applies to Zammad's ISMS and the infrastructure it operates". Missing: no SOC 2 found. No NIS2-specific documentation found. DPA (AVV) available. Conflict: an older FAQ (published 09/2025) says "The Professional and Plus tariffs are also ISO27001 certified". Self-hosted: the vendor certificate does not cover our own infrastructure.

27.p: Starter v2 (hosting); AI from Professional v2
27.e: "With all Hosted rates, only data centres in Germany are used." Zammad AI: "Hosted in the EU and compliant with GDPR". Missing: backup location is not stated separately (the pricing page says only "we take care of … backups"). The country and sub-processor for Zammad AI are not stated. Self-hosted would change this: we choose the location, and AI can run on Ollama ("your data is not transferred to a third party").

28.n: Automatic deletion is possible with a scheduler job (conditions plus "Delete immediately"). Missing: there is no dedicated retention-period setting, and attachments are not covered separately. That deleting a ticket also deletes its attachments is not stated.
28.e: "You can delete only tickets if you choose Ticket as object in the scheduler task. This gives you an additional action named Delete immediately". "Delete immediately will delete the ticket at the runtime of the job without any hint in the UI."

29.e: Plans are priced "per agent". "An agent is an employee of your company who has the rights to edit tickets and customers"; "Every user who is supposed to view or edit tickets must be registered as an agent". There is no explicit statement that customers (requesters) are free or unlimited. Approvers: no approval feature (#10).

30.n: Live chat with agents is documented. Missing: an AI assistant that answers requesters from the KB, points them to forms, checks status or opens tickets; nothing in Slack. The KB assistant is for agents only.
30.e: Professional v2 channels: "Email, Web Form, SMS, Chat, Telegram". KB assistant: "When the feature is enabled, agents see related knowledge base answers in the Related Knowledge section".

31.n: The customer web interface offers ticket creation with group selection, and there is a KB. Missing: a service catalog, and links to requests handled in other systems (for example Aboard).
31.e: "Configure the ticket creation by your customers via web interface." "You can select a set of groups you want to be selectable by your customers."

32.n: Each client's contacts can see their organization's tickets. Missing: branding per client. Branding is one setting for the whole instance (one name, one logo), so per-client branding would need separate instances. Quick setup from existing data is not documented.
32.e: Branding: "Product Name Defines the name of the application"; "Logo Defines the logo of the application". Overviews: "whether you want one of your customer's contacts to see all of their organization's tickets."

33.n: (SMS). It needs an account with an SMS provider (Massenversand, MessageBird or Twilio). Push notifications and on-call tool integrations were not found. The mobile view is a PWA.
33.e: "It's also possible to use the SMS channel to send notifications from the system (e.g. from trigger or scheduler)." "Users must have a mobile phone number to get notified by SMS." Mobile view: "Progressive web app (PWA) support".

34.n: Mentioning someone subscribes them to the ticket. Missing: giving temporary access to a person outside the ticket's group and removing it later; unsubscribing is not described in the pages read.
34.e: "Mention the person in an article by typing @ @ and selecting the user. In the latter case, the user gets notified and is automatically subscribed to receive notifications on ticket updates."

35.n: GitHub and GitLab issues only (read-only, issues but not PRs). Missing: Notion and other systems.
35.e: "You can link GitHub and GitLab issues to a ticket and follow their state while you work on it." "Nothing is written back to the tracker. Issues only".

36.e: "Show and hide fields Adjust if fields are mandatory or not Set available options for select fields Apply these adjustments based on conditions". Web channel: "For a fine-grained control over the fields visible to customers, consider using core workflows."

37.n: Fields and logic are built in the admin UI without code. Missing: letting a business team (People) edit only its own forms is not documented. Changes to objects need "Update Database".
37.p: Professional v2 (individual fields); Plus v2 (Core Workflows)
37.e: "On the upper right you can add new attributes." "Changes on objects require you to update the database to apply these changes."

38.n: Core Workflows can show or hide fields by role (an example uses "Role is not Approval Person"). Missing: separate forms shown only to a group of requesters. Group selection on the web channel applies to all customers.
38.e: Core Workflows let you "distinguish between different roles or groups". Example condition: "Role is not Approval Person".

39.n: Checklist templates and ticket templates exist. Missing: owners and due dates per checklist item. Only one checklist per ticket. Checklist items cannot drive triggers.
39.e: "You can create one or more templates with predefined checklist items." "It is only possible to add one checklist per ticket." "You can't access the items or state of the checkboxes from other places in Zammad like triggers or workflows."

40.n: Visibility is set per group (for example an HR group that only HR agents and a manager can read). Missing: restricting visibility per ticket.
40.e: "Use the group permission table to grant per-group privileges." "Read: View, search for and find tickets." "Overviews only show tickets for which the user has at least viewing permission."

41.n: (custom build on the public API). The admin docs navigation lists CSV import only for organizations, users and text modules, not for tickets.
41.e: "Zammad provides a powerful REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well." Admin docs navigation: "via CSV import" (Organizations); "Import of Text Modules via CSV File".

42.n: A ticket created in advance can resurface on a date (Pending Reminder), and agents can use templates for recurring tickets. Missing: automatic creation of tickets on a date or schedule. The scheduler only changes existing objects.
42.e: "Pending Reminder: State for open tickets which you want to get reminded to a certain date and time." Scheduler: "Which objects should be modified based on conditions". Templates: "pre-defining a ticket template for recurring tickets".

43.n: (custom build). A trigger on close sends a webhook with a custom payload, but the register (for example a spreadsheet) needs its own receiving endpoint. No official Zapier app was found (#50).
43.p: Starter v2 (triggers); webhooks: plan not stated
43.e: "Webhooks have to be triggered by Trigger or Scheduler jobs." "It is possible to further customize the webhook payload to your own needs."

44.n: Native integrations for Checkmk, Icinga, Monit and Nagios, plus a Zabbix guide. A client-hosted monitor must be able to reach Zammad by email or REST API. The "points to a solution" part relies on KB suggestions (AI, Professional v2, per-call fee).
44.p: Not stated for the integrations; Professional v2 for KB suggestions
44.e: Checkmk "can send real-time status alerts to Zammad via email or REST API. … Zammad will automatically create, update and close tickets based on the health of your system." Integrations: "Integrations for Monitoring Systems … Icinga Monit Nagios … Zabbix … Checkmk".

45.n: Filtering by requester and by period is documented. Missing: filtering a custom amount field by range was not verified. Deeper reporting via Grafana requires Plus v2.
45.p: Starter v2 ("Zammad Standard Reporting"); Plus v2 (Grafana)
45.e: Reporting: "get an overview of the number of tickets (e.g. tickets of a specific customer) and to download ticket data"; "Time interval/period switcher"; "The download feature provides the tickets in a .xlsx spreadsheet." Overviews: "The conditions can be seen like a filter."

46.p: Not stated (not on the pricing table)
46.e: "Zammad supports detailed time accounting to help administrators keep track of how much time you spend on any given ticket, customer or client organization." "Activity Types are used for grouping accounted time entries together."

47.p: Starter v2 (pending reminders, schedulers); Professional v2 (SLAs)
47.e: "Pending Reminder … Requires you to enter a date and time at which you want to get notified." SLA: "Zammad notifies you by default when tickets approach or exceed their deadlines." Scheduler: "scheduler jobs can be used to send periodic reminder emails."

48.e: "Click the 👨 tab in the ticket sidebar to see the customer's profile. If the customer has other tickets too, you can see a summary". Link dialog: "If the customer has an existing ticket, it will show up under Recent customer tickets."

49.n: LDAP/AD syncs users and maps groups to roles. Missing: a manager field or automatic filling of the manager, and approvals. Organizations cannot be synced. A Google Workspace directory sync was not found. Whether LDAP works on hosted was not verified.
49.e: "Zammad comes with a powerful LDAP integration that allows you to have a single source of truth." "Mapping / synchronizing organizations is not possible". "Zammad's LDAP sync is one way."

50.n: (custom build). No official Zapier app was found: zapier.com/apps/zammad returned 404, and a web search found Zammad only on other iPaaS sites (Make, Integrately, Pipedream; not fetched). Route: Zammad webhooks to a third-party URL plus the REST API. The Zapier-side steps were not verified.
50.e: Webhooks: "a way to integrate Zammad with other web services or applications". API: "allows all operations that are available via UI".

51.n: (custom build on the public API). Not in the integrations list. The Outline side was not verified.
51.e: Integrations list contains no Outline entry. API: "REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

52.n: (custom build on the public API: create organizations and users from HubSpot data). Not in the integrations list. The HubSpot side was not verified.
52.e: Integrations for customers list only "Clearbit Exchange LDAP / Active Directory PGP S/MIME". API: "allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

53.n: (custom build on the public API). Not in the integrations list. The Productive side was not verified. Zammad has its own time accounting (#46).
53.e: Integrations list contains no Productive entry. API: "allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

54.n: (custom build). No ServiceNow or other ITSM connector in the integrations list. Routes: the client's tool sends email to a client-specific address (#2), or calls the Zammad REST API.
54.e: Pricing table: "Email unlimited addresses". API: "REST-API which allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

55.n: iCal feed of ticket deadlines, per agent
55.e: "Calendar Add your ticket deadlines to your own favorite calendar app with the iCal link listed on this page."

56.n: (custom build on the public API: an Aboard event calls the Zammad API to create a ticket). No Aboard integration found. The Aboard side was not verified.
56.e: Integrations list contains no Aboard entry. API: "allows all operations that are available via UI as well."

57.n: Deletion is documented: manual, via API, or automatic via a scheduler. Missing: exporting a copy of a person's data. Deletion also leaves the person's references in other customers' tickets and in internal notes.
57.e: "You can delete users and their tickets by creating a deletion task. This can be required for compliance with GDPR". "You can create data privacy deletion task via API." "If there are references to a user's name … this information will not be removed".

58.n: (hosted: German data centres only). Self-hosted changes the verdict to Partial: a separate instance per region, run by us.
58.e: Pricing: "secure and powerful on our servers in German data centers". Support article (quoted in analysis/market_scan/filter_C.md, same day): "With all Hosted rates, only data centres in Germany are used."

59.n: overviews as worklists; no kanban board found
59.e: "Overviews can be used as a kind of worklist of tasks that the agent is supposed to work on." They "can be assigned to roles and restricted to specific users"; "Grouping by".

questions: #29: Are customers (internal employees and external clients with the Customer role) free and unlimited on all hosted v2 plans? Is there a cap?

#10: Is a native approval feature on the roadmap? What is your recommended setup for a two-step approval (requester's manager, then department head) with the decision recorded, and which plan does it need?
#4: Apart from custom triggers, is there a built-in way to notify the customer about every state change?
#12: With Shared Organization = no, can a customer see only their own tickets? Can CC'd persons see the ticket in the customer interface?
#15: Can the escalation warning lead time be configured (for example 1 day before breach)? Can SLAs be selected by ticket priority?
#16: Is Standard Reporting really only on Plus v2? Is there a built-in first-response-time and resolution-time report?
#17: Can anyone (including admins) edit or delete ticket history entries? Are owner changes recorded? What is the history retention period?
#23: Is there an official Slack app or Zapier app for creating tickets from Slack and syncing replies both ways?

#26: Do you hold SOC 2? Can we get the ISO 27001 certificate and its Statement of Applicability, and does the scope cover the SaaS platform on all plans (including Starter v2)? Do you have NIS2 supplier documentation?
#27: In which country are backups stored? Where does Zammad AI process data (country and LLM sub-processor)? Where is the current sub-processor list?
#8: Can Core Workflows limit the State field to different state sets per group or process? On which hosted plan can admins add custom ticket states?

#11: Can a trigger automatically create a linked child ticket in another group (for example HR onboarding → IT)? Does the parent ticket show the status of its child tickets, including ones in groups the agent cannot access?
#18: Can the AI suggest solutions from similar past tickets, not only from KB answers? Does anything flag that a similar problem came up before?
#20 / #22 / #51: Is there any supported way to use an external knowledge base (Notion, Outline) as a source for KB suggestions and AI drafts, or is only the Zammad KB used?
#21: On hosted SaaS, can customers configure the "Anthropic" provider (own API key) on Professional v2? Is the €0.03 per call fee charged then? Is a vendor MCP server planned?
General AI: which Zammad version does hosted SaaS run today? Are the Knowledge Base Assistant and AI Agents generally available there?
#24: Is there an app marketplace, or only the built-in integrations? Are the API and webhooks available on all hosted plans?
#25: Are Google login and SAML SSO available on all hosted plans (including Starter v2) at no extra cost?
#28: Does deleting a ticket (scheduler "Delete immediately") also delete its attachments permanently, including backups, and when? Is a retention-period setting planned?
#34: Can an agent add a person without group access to one ticket temporarily and remove them later? How does a user unsubscribe?
#39: Can checklist items have owners and due dates?
#42: Can Zammad create new tickets on a schedule (recurring tickets)?
#44 / #49: Are the monitoring integrations (Checkmk, Icinga, Monit, Nagios) and LDAP available on hosted SaaS? Can a requester's manager be stored and filled in automatically?
#46 / #55: Are time accounting and the iCal calendar feed available on all hosted plans?
#50: Does Zammad maintain or endorse a Zapier app? Is there a recommended Zapier route?
#57: Can all data about a person be exported (a subject access request) in one step?
#58: Is any hosted region outside Germany available, for example the US or India?
checks: Re-checked: in Zammad's official GitHub repository, PR #6264 "Feature: Ticket approval workflow" was closed with "There may be a dedicated approval workflow engine in Zammad in the future" (https://github.com/zammad/zammad/pull/6264). #10 "Does not meet" stands: no native approvals today; a build with triggers and Core Workflows is possible but not documented.
Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 6 / Partial 8 / Does not meet 1 / Unknown 1.

Corrected #21 from "Meets" to "Partial": rule 7 needs a vendor MCP server or a documented native way for an external agent (Claude or our own) to read and act on tickets. Zammad lets Anthropic power its built-in AI agents (limited actions) but has no vendor MCP server; community MCP servers are SECONDARY.
#58 "Does not meet" applies to hosted SaaS (Germany only); self-hosting separate instances per region would be Partial.

1.e: "OTRS manages polling one or multiple email mailboxes of any internet standard type."; queue follow-up option "possible: The follow up will reopen the already closed ticket."; "Reply via Email: This action allows you to reply via email to the article."; ticket history "contains all operations that happened with the ticket in the past, along with timestamp and username". Note: "When fetching mail, OTRS deletes the mail from the POP or IMAP server."

2.n: Any number of system addresses, each linked to a queue; incoming mail is sorted into the queue linked to the To: address. Any agent with access to the queue can take the ticket; optional automatic allocation to the least-loaded agent (Ticket Allocation feature). On Managed, mailbox setup is done by the vendor team.
2.p: Starter (core Ticketing). Ticket Allocation: a feature package in the Features Manual, apparently merged into the framework later (2026.3.1 fix: "Generic Agent Default Settings Changed After Ticket Allocation Merge"); package not stated
2.e: "OTRS manages as many email addresses for your teams as needed."; "The system checks if a queue is linked with the address in the To: field of the incoming mail."; "New tickets are automatically assigned to agents with the smallest number of tickets to work on"

3.e: Auto response types: "auto reply: A newly raised ticket will trigger this auto response."; "auto reply/new ticket: This message informs the customer of the new ticket number." Set per queue: "Use this screen to add automatic responses for use in queues."

4.e: Built-in notifications: "Customer ticket article notification", "Customer ticket create notification", "Customer ticket state update (other than closed)"; recipient option "Customer user of the ticket". External interface: notifications cover "Responses from agents" and "State changes of a ticket". Missing: notifying the requester at each approval step is not documented. The process e-mail action (TicketSendEmail) lists only "Send to these agents" and "Additional recipient email addresses".

5.e: "Add Note: This action allows agents to create a note for ticket and to add the note as article to the ticket. Notes are only visible to agents by default."

6.e: Group permission "note: Permission to add notes to tickets and inform agents in this group/queue."; the sidebar shows "which agents are watching the ticket"; chat: "Allows you to append this chat as an article to a selected ticket."; feature list: "Inter-Agent Communication", "Handover to Other Teams". Missing: @mentions are not documented, and neither are tasks inside a ticket. The documented options are splitting an article into another ticket and linking tickets.

7.n: Owner can be set and changed (per-queue permission); owner changes are written to the ticket history with user and timestamp.
7.e: permission "owner": "Permission to set the owner of new tickets or change the owner of existing tickets in this group/queue."; history type "HistoryOwnerUpdate"; "The history contains all operations that happened with the ticket in the past, along with timestamp and username"

8.n: Admins add states in the States screen; ACLs can match the process (ProcessEntityID) or queue and limit the possible states, so each process gets its own status set. Managed page also offers vendor help for "new statuses".
8.e: "Nine states are pre-defined. More states can be added"; ACL reference, Properties: "# the process that the current ticket is part of"; Possible: "# Possible ticket options (white list)", which include "State: - some state"

9.p: Starter ("Ticket Forms" is listed as a feature "now included in every OTRS contract level")
9.e: "display different ticket masks and forms in the agent and external interfaces"; "You can define required fields for forms"; dynamic fields handle "texts, integers, drop-down lists, multi-select fields, date-time, checkboxes and more". Per client: pre-filled fields "based on the customer group settings".

10.p: Starter (Process Engine is in every contract level)
10.e: Process Management example "Approval by manager": "In case of a denial, a reason should be recorded by the manager. In case of approval, the order is passed to the purchasing department."; ACL example with two approval dialogs: "Approval from Sales" (Head of Sales) and "Approval from Marketing" (Head of Marketing). Missing: there is no ready-made approval feature, so an admin has to model each flow in Process Management. Automatic routing to the requester's own line manager is not documented; the approvers in the example are fixed agent roles.

11.n: A process step can create a child ticket in another team's queue; linked tickets show in a Linked Tickets widget; data can be pulled from / pushed to linked tickets; an ACL can block closing a parent until its children are closed. Missing: that the child's status and history are shown in the parent view is not stated (the linked-items pop-up lets agents "set the columns for each object"; a state column is not named).
11.e: TicketCreate module example: "LinkAs Child", "Queue Postmaster", "Title Subtask of: <OTRS_TICKET_Title>"; "To allow closing parent tickets only if all its children are already closed, an additional ACL has to be added"; "Linked Tickets Widget" – "This widget shows the linked tickets"

12.e: "My Tickets": "shows tickets that have been created by the currently logged in customer user." But "Company Tickets": "All customer users assigned to this certain customer can see the content in this list." Turning that off takes the setting "CustomerDisableCompanyTicketAccess" plus a file edit: "Copy the $Self->{CustomerUser} section from Kernel/Config/Defaults.pm into Kernel/Config.pm." Missing: by default, company-wide visibility applies to every customer user of the same customer. On SaaS the file edit would be done by OTRS (not documented). Visibility of tickets a requester was added to (Cc) is not documented. On-premises we could edit the file ourselves; the verdict does not change.

13.e: Queue: "It is possible to limit access to the selected group. The group creates a permission link between the queue and an agent or a customer user."; "rw: Full read and write access to the tickets in this group/queue."; tickets can move between desks: "move_into: Permission to move tickets in this group/queue". Missing: separating agents per client (only agents on a client project see its tickets) is not documented. A queue/group per client is my inference, not documentation.

14.n: for built-in if/then rules: Generic Agent (time- and event-based), Process Management, ACLs, notifications. The Zapier complement is weak: no official Zapier app (see #50).
14.e: "simple or compound time and event-based tasks are configurable in the OTRS front end without the requirement to learn a scripting language. Depending on search criteria, and time or event criteria, tickets will automatically be acted upon."

15.p: Starter (basic escalations); Advanced Escalations: contract level not stated
15.e: SLA settings "Escalation - first response time (minutes)", "Escalation - update time (minutes)", "Escalation - solution time (minutes)"; built-in "Ticket escalation warning notification"; tag "If true, notify - x% of escalation has reached." Missing: targets are set per SLA/service or per queue, and targets by priority are not documented. A fixed lead time for the warning (for example 1 day before) is not documented. "Advanced Escalations … are only available in certain contract levels" (the levels are not named).

16.p: Starter ("Extended Ticket Stats" is in every contract level)
16.e: "Reports are automatically generated statistics in PDF format, which can be sent via email."; statistic fields "FirstResponseInMin: The time in minutes from ticket creation to first response" and "SolutionInMin"; "Keep on top of KPIs such as the number of requests, service issues, SLA risks, expenses and more." Note: agents need the group "stats".

17.e: Ticket history has every operation "along with timestamp and username"; history types include "HistoryOwnerUpdate"; system configuration changes "can be audited (who changed a setting and when, what was the old and what is the new value)"; "OTRS offers audit security". Missing: no statement that history entries cannot be edited. The Data Privacy Protection feature can anonymize or delete data, and "The data classification supports history types". Generic Agent "will delete the matched tickets". On SaaS that feature "is taken care of by the Customer Solutions Team".

18.n: OTRS AI Services include "response suggestions" / "response generation" (Azure OpenAI GPT-4o, run by BOTfriends GmbH in Germany). Missing: analysis of past tickets and the knowledge base, and a "similar problem came up before" flag, are not documented. AI is included in Advanced and Pro (Pro: "12,000 AI Credits"); otherwise paid AI Credits, price not listed.
18.e: "AI Credits … can be flexibly used across all available AI services, such as ticket classification, summaries or response suggestions."; "Azure OpenAI GPT 4o is used for most active AI functionalities such as ticket classification and response generation."

19.n: AI Ticket Classification sets the service category of incoming tickets automatically, based on historical data, so tickets reach the right team. Included in Advanced and Pro; otherwise AI Credits (price not listed).
19.e: "The AI Ticket Classification Service analyzes incoming tickets in real time. Based on historical data and learned patterns, it automatically assigns the right service category. This reduces manual triage, speeds up routing and ensures that tickets reach the right team from the first interaction."

20.n: The only related AI feature is AI Ticket Summary, which adds a summary as an internal note (for example on closure). Drafting knowledge base articles from tickets, and connecting to Notion/Outline, are not documented.
20.e: "The service generates AI‑powered ticket summaries and automatically attaches them as internal notes during workflows (e.g., upon ticket closure or status change)."

21.n: Vendor-provided MCP server (since 2026.5.1, disabled by default) with 23 tools, including write tools (create_ticket, update_ticket, add_note, close_ticket, link_objects); Claude Desktop and Claude Code are named as clients; auth by API key or Bearer token; not labelled beta. Needs a contract that includes the MCP feature (package and price not stated).
21.p: Contract with the "MCP feature" (package not stated)
21.e: "AI agents and MCP-compatible clients, for example Claude Desktop or Claude Code, connect to one HTTP endpoint of an OTRS web service"; "The tools cover ticket handling (search, read, create and update tickets …)"; "Each of the 23 MCP tools carries annotations that state whether it only reads data or changes it"; "create_ticket, update_ticket, add_note and close_ticket return a shared receipt"; "On systems whose contract does not include the MCP feature, every MCP request is answered with the JSON-RPC error -32000"

22.n: (custom build). No Notion connector in the integrations catalogue (3 pages). Route: sync Notion pages into the OTRS knowledge base through the FAQ REST operations (FAQCreate, FAQUpdate; since 2026.5.1), or an external AI agent over MCP that also reads Notion. The Notion side was not verified.
22.e: Catalogue: "Use ready-to-use connectors … and extend anything with our REST API"; no Notion entry. "Full Create, Read, Update, Delete, and Search support for FAQ articles has been added to the OTRS GenericInterface."

23.p: Advanced ("Webservices"; the REST API = Web Services link is my reading)
23.e: The only route is a custom build on the API: "extend anything with our REST API for complete flexibility and secure integration". There is no Slack entry in the integrations catalogue (3 pages). An otrs.com search for "slack" returns 4 blog posts only. Slack Marketplace, query "otrs": "No apps matching your selected filters". zapier.com/apps/otrs/integrations returns 404, so there is no official Zapier app. Two-way sync and private Slack tickets are not documented.
23.s: https://otrs.com/integrations/ ; https://otrs.com/integrations/2/ ; https://otrs.com/integrations/3/ ; https://otrs.com/?s=slack ; https://slack.com/marketplace/search?q=otrs ; https://zapier.com/apps/otrs/integrations ; https://otrs.com/how-to-buy/

24.n: REST/SOAP Generic Interface (inbound operations; outbound invokers fired by configurable events, which act as fine-grained webhooks); a vendor catalogue of about 45 connectors. Missing: a public API reference with the endpoint list was not found (doc.otrs.com returned 502; manuals describe only configuration); the catalogue is a list of connectors ("Request A Demo"), not a self-install marketplace. Webservices are listed from Advanced.
24.e: "OTRS reacts on incoming REST or SOAP requests and create objects or provides object data to other systems"; invoker "Event Triggers": "This invoker will be triggered by the configured events."

25.n: SAML or Kerberos SSO on Managed; since 2026.8.1 OIDC with any standard provider; agent 2FA with an authenticator app. Missing: Google Workspace is not named as an identity provider; the package for SSO is not stated. SSO "is not supported with the mobile app". On-premise: same verdict.
25.e: "Single sign-on is possible with SAML or Kerberos."; "works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, not only Keycloak"; "The agent can use an authenticator application for two-factor authentication."; "Two-factor authentication can be configured as a default."

26.n: rule 8: only the hosting providers are certified; the vendor itself holds neither
26.e: "OTRS currently does not maintain ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certification."; "The respective datacenter operators maintain independent certifications and controls"; managed page "Highest Infrastructure Standards: ISO 27001" (infrastructure). NIS2: "OTRS security processes are informed by: NIS2, BSI IT-Grundschutz, ISO/IEC 27001 Controls…". I found no NIS2 supplier documentation. Public: DPA, TOMs (Oct 2026), sub-processor list (Sep 2026); OTRS is a CVE Numbering Authority. On-premises does not change the verdict.

27.e: "By default, data is stored on servers in Germany (on request in USA or Canada) according to the latest GDPR standards."; AI: "All AI services are hosted exclusively within the European Union. The infrastructure is located in Germany"; sub-processors: "Hetzner Online GmbH, SaaS infrastructure, Germany, Finland"; AI sub-processors are in Germany, France, Ireland and Luxembourg. Missing: the backup location is not stated (TOMs: "Backup of relevant systems up on a cross-site basis"). Support sub-processors are outside the EU: "Resolve IT, Service and Support, Serbia" and "Zen Networks, Service and Support, Morocco" (both under EU SCC). On-premises would change this to Meets: hosting and backups in our own EU environment, and AI documented in Germany. On-premises still requires "A connection to cloud.otrs.com via HTTPS".

28.n: Building blocks exist: a scheduled Generic Agent job can delete matched tickets; attachments of tickets closed within a set time span can be deleted automatically by a daemon task; Data Privacy Protection rules filter by close time. Missing: no single retention-period setting; on Managed, attachment deletion and privacy rules are run by the vendor team, not by us. On-premise: we can run them ourselves; verdict unchanged.
28.p: Not stated (Data Privacy Protection: feature package, SILVER+ in the Features Manual)
28.e: Generic Agent "Delete tickets": "If Yes is selected, the generic agent job will delete the matched tickets."; "This feature enables the automatic deletion of ticket attachments that were closed in a definable time span."

29.e: Pricing step 1: "Select the number of licensed users"; GTC: use "for the contractually agreed number of users". There is no statement on whether customer users (requesters) or approvers count as licensed users.

30.n: Built-in live chat between agents and customers or public users. Missing: a native AI assistant that answers from the knowledge base, checks status and opens tickets is not documented. Routes: partner AI connectors in the catalogue (BOTfriends, Melibo, Marvin; third-party) or a custom AI agent over MCP, which supports acting as a customer user (customer impersonation). Slack is not in the catalogue.
30.e: "The chat feature allows for chats between agents and customers using the OTRS front end."; MCP: "Customer impersonation through the MCP tool interface now requires an OTRS-issued identity token"

31.n: The external interface has a configurable service catalogue; each item can link to an internal or external URL (for example an Aboard page).
31.e: "Use this screen to add categories and items for use in external interface."; item field "Link *": "A link to an internal or an external URL."

32.n: One external interface with editable layout (logo, favicon, colours); ticket templates can be limited per customer group. Missing: a separate branded space per client is not documented (likely a separate instance per client; not verified).
32.e: "Use this screen to edit the layout displayed in external interface."; "The logo is a small image that is displayed in the top left corner of the external pages."

33.n: (SMS). Ticket notifications can go by SMS through the vendor's SMS cloud service, limited to selected roles; an iOS/Android agent app exists. Push notifications and on-call tool integrations were not found. "SMS Alert" is a paid extra (price not listed).
33.e: "A notification method can be email, web view with browser notification support or SMS."; "An on-call duty should be alarmed about incidents … OTRS provides SMS as a cloud service"

34.n: Agents can put tickets on personal watchlists with notifications. Missing: adding another person to one ticket for a while and removing them is not documented (access is per queue/group); shared watchlists need a special STORM licence.
34.e: "A ticket agent defines watchlists and assigns tickets to a watchlist."; shared watchlist: "This feature requires a special license currently only available for STORM customers."

35.n: Native links between tickets, configuration items, knowledge base articles and appointments; a vendor GitHub connector; an inbound Link Object web service; article meta filters that turn text into external links. Missing: Notion (no connector).
35.e: GitHub connector: "linking tickets to development workflows and artifacts"; "OTRS can accept requests from external systems to interact with the link object."

36.n: ACLs restrict a field's values based on another field; Hide/Show Dynamic Fields controls visibility. Configured by an admin (ACL).
36.e: "restrict the selectable values of the dynamic field CarModel to Polo, Golf and Passat, if a user has selected the value VW in the dynamic field CarManufacturer"; "build flexible and dynamic forms by hiding or showing fields based on ticket information, permissions and more"

37.n: Admin GUI screens for Dynamic Ticket Templates and graphical Process Management. Missing: form layouts are edited as YAML in System Configuration and behaviour via ACLs (admin work); editing by business teams without admin rights is not documented. On Managed the vendor offers to make "additions to the input masks".
37.e: "Processes are designed completely and efficiently within the OTRS front end"; "disable the specific dynamic fields in the YAML configuration of this form"

38.n: Dynamic ticket templates can be assigned to customer groups, so only those requesters see them in the external interface.
38.e: "Assign the Peugeot Customer group to the Peugeot Template template."; "display pre-filled fields … in the external interface based on the customer group settings"

39.n: Process templates with steps, approvals and sub-tickets with owners exist; the HR solution page claims "Checklist-driven processes". Missing: a ticket checklist where each item has an owner and due date is not documented in the manuals.
39.e: HR page: "Onboarding and Offboarding Coordination … Task assignment and tracking Cross-team coordination Checklist-driven processes"; "Process templates allow you to automate workflows"

40.n: Visibility is set per group/queue (ro, rw and other permissions), so HR tickets can sit in a queue only HR and a manager can read. Missing: per-ticket visibility (only the assigned agent) is not documented.
40.e: Permission "ro": "Read-only access to tickets in this group/queue."

41.n: Missing: no CSV import of tickets documented; the Import/Export module does not list tickets as an object. Routes: a script on the web services or the MCP tool create_ticket (custom build).
41.e: MCP: "create_ticket has a new optional argument customer_id"; Import/Export: "Select the object type you want to import to or export from." (objects not listed)

42.n: Admin module "Recurring Tickets" creates tickets from a template on a schedule and can start processes.
42.e: "The admin will be able to create reoccurring tickets based on a template. A new Admin Module Recurring Tickets was created for this purpose. Also processes can be triggered."

43.n: (custom build). Outbound web-service invokers fire on chosen events (for example a state change to closed) and send ticket data to a remote REST/SOAP endpoint; the Ticket Invoker feature adds TicketCreate/TicketUpdate invokers. Missing: no ready connector to a spreadsheet; the register's API side was not verified.
43.p: Advanced (Webservices); Ticket Invoker: GOLD+ in the Features Manual
43.e: Invoker "Event Triggers": "This invoker will be triggered by the configured events."; "This package adds the functionality of two new invokers TicketCreate and TicketUpdate for web services."

44.n: Monitoring tools create tickets by email (Nagios, Icinga2, HP OpenView or similar); vendor connectors listed for Checkmk, Icinga, Nagios, Zabbix, Grafana. A client-hosted monitor must reach OTRS by email or web service. Missing: pointing to a solution is not documented.
44.e: "it works by receiving email messages sent by a network monitoring suite. New tickets are created in case of component failures."

45.n: Ticket search covers customer user, created/closed dates and dynamic fields (for example an amount field); statistics export to CSV or Excel.
45.e: Search attributes: "CustomerUserID", "Created", "DynamicFields.*.*"; statistics "Possible formats are CSV, Excel, Graph and Print"

46.n: Time units per article, optional automatic timer; separate from SLA times. No Productive connector (see #53).
46.e: "Time Units" – "Enter any amount of time that is to be used in time accounting."; "When an agent opens these screens, a timer starts counting"

47.n: Pending reminder state with a reminder time; escalation warning and escalation notifications; reminder widgets. Advanced Escalations (custom escalation types) only at "contract level platinum".
47.e: state "pending reminder": "The ticket should be worked on again upon reaching the pending time."; notifications "Ticket escalation warning notification", "Ticket pending reminder notification"

48.n: The customer user detail view lists all tickets of that person (employees are set up as customer users).
48.e: "Ticket List Widget" – "This widget lists all of the tickets related to the customer user."

49.n: LDAP customer back end can show attributes such as a manager name; since 2026.6.1 customer-user fields can come from an OIDC identity provider. Missing: filling in the requester's manager as approver automatically is not documented (the approval example uses a fixed "Manager" agent); Google Workspace directory not named. On Managed, back ends are set up by the vendor team.
49.e: "If additional customer user attributes are stored in your LDAP directory, such as a manager name … this information can be displayed in OTRS."

50.n: (custom build). No official Zapier app: zapier.com/apps/otrs/integrations returned 404 and a web search found none. Route: Webhooks by Zapier plus OTRS web services.

51.n: (custom build on web services). No Outline connector in the catalogue. The Outline side was not verified.
51.e: Catalogue has no Outline entry; "extend anything with our REST API"

52.n: Vendor-listed HubSpot connector with customer synchronization (plus ticket mirroring). Delivery model (packaged connector or project), sync direction and price are not stated.
52.e: "Customer Synchronization: Synchronize customer records to keep contact data consistent across service and business systems."

53.n: (custom build on web services). No Productive connector in the catalogue. OTRS has its own time accounting (#46). The Productive side was not verified.

54.n: Vendor-listed connectors for ServiceNow (incident synchronization), Jira, Zendesk, Freshdesk and SAP Solution Manager. Price and plan not stated.
54.e: ServiceNow: "Keep incidents aligned between OTRS and the connected system by synchronizing key ticket fields and updates."

55.n: Calendar rules create appointments from ticket data (for example pending or escalation dates) automatically; calendars can be subscribed to in an external calendar app by URL. Google Calendar is not named.
55.e: "Define rules for creating automatic appointments in this calendar based on ticket data."; "Go to your calendar application and paste the URL."

56.n: (custom build). The catalogue lists HR connectors for Personio, SAP SuccessFactors and Workday, not Aboard. Route: Aboard events call OTRS web services to create tickets. The Aboard side was not verified.
56.e: Catalogue: "Personio … HR Systems", "Workday … HR Systems"; no Aboard entry.

57.n: Data Privacy Protection rules delete, anonymize or pseudonymize data per object (customer user, customer, ticket and articles). Missing: exporting a copy of a person's data is not documented; rules run by console command, and on Managed the vendor team runs them.
57.p: Not stated (feature package, SILVER+ in the Features Manual)
57.e: "Deletion or PrivacyByDeletion" – "The deletion rule type is used to delete data sets"; "The customer user driver provides the functionality to search and modify the information for customer users."

58.n: Managed hosting is in Germany by default, USA or Canada on request: one region per system, so per-client regions need separate instances; India not offered. On-premise: any region in our own data centre, still one instance per region; verdict unchanged.
58.e: "By default, data is stored on servers in Germany (on request in USA or Canada) according to the latest GDPR standards."

59.n: Ticket lists with saved filters and dashboards; Kanban view by any select-like ticket attribute (Advanced).
59.e: "Tickets can be displayed in Kanban view by various ticket attributes."; "Being able to pick any select-like attribute as Kanban Columns"

questions: #29: Are customer users (employees and client contacts who raise tickets by email or portal) free and unlimited, or do they count as "licensed users"? Does a customer user who approves through the external interface need a licence?

#26: Does EasyVista-OTRS GmbH plan ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2 certification, and when? Does any EasyVista group certificate cover OTRS SaaS in scope? Can you provide NIS2 supplier documentation (security questionnaire, incident notification terms)?
#27: In which country are SaaS backups for an EU (Germany) instance stored? Do the support sub-processors in Serbia and Morocco access customer data, and can support be limited to EU staff?
#23: Is there an official or partner Slack integration with two-way sync and private tickets from Slack? Does the REST API require the Advanced package (Web Services)?

#10: Can an approval step be routed automatically to the requester's line manager (for example from a customer-user or LDAP attribute)? Is there a ready-made approval template, or must each flow be built in Process Management?
#15: Can SLA targets differ by ticket priority? Can the escalation warning use a fixed lead time (for example 24 h before breach)? Which contract levels include "Advanced Escalations"?
#12: On Managed SaaS, will OTRS set CustomerDisableCompanyTicketAccess / CustomerUserExcludePrimaryCustomerID so requesters see only their own tickets? Can customer users in Cc see the ticket?
#13: What is the recommended setup so that only agents assigned to a client see that client's tickets (a queue/group per client, or something else)?
#17: Can admins or the vendor edit or delete individual ticket history entries? Is there a tamper-proof audit log?
#6 and #4: Are @mentions and sub-tasks within a ticket available? Can the requester be notified automatically at each approval step?
Pricing: what are the list prices per licensed user for Starter, Advanced and Pro (currency, billing period, minimum term) and the price of AI Credits?
Trial: how long does the free trial last, and on which package?

The HTML docs at academy.otrs.com/doc/ were blocked ("NinjaFirewall 403 Forbidden"). The PDF manuals on the same host returned HTTP 200 to a plain request through the browser context with no header changes, and they were used instead. doc.otrs.com returned 502 ("upstream request failed").
otrs.com showed a "One moment, please..." check on one URL. It cleared by waiting; nothing was clicked.
The trust-centre tab text was read from the page DOM (hidden tab panels) without clicking.
#20: Does OTRS AI draft knowledge base (FAQ) articles from resolved tickets, and can it use an external knowledge base (Notion, Outline)?
#18: Which sources do AI "response suggestions" use (past tickets, knowledge base)? Is there a "similar ticket" detection? What does an AI Credit cost, and how many credits does each AI call use?

#21: Which package includes the MCP feature, and at what price? Is the MCP server enabled on Managed (SaaS) systems, and can Claude (claude.ai connector) authenticate with the API key or Bearer token?
#24: Where is the public API reference (list of REST operations)? doc.otrs.com returned HTTP 502 on 2026-11-18. Can Starter use any API, or only Advanced ("Webservices")?
#25: Is Google Workspace supported as SAML or OIDC identity provider for agents on Managed, in which package, and at extra cost? Can 2FA be enforced for all agents?
#28: On Managed, can we set a retention period ourselves (Generic Agent delete job with a close-time filter, attachment deletion), or must the Customer Solutions Team run it, and at what cost?
#11: Does the parent ticket show the status and history of its child tickets (Linked Tickets widget columns)?
#22: Is there any ready Notion connector, or only a custom web-service build?
#2: Is mailbox setup on Managed self-service, or a request to the vendor each time we add a client address? Is Ticket Allocation included in Starter?
#32: Can one Managed system offer a separately branded external interface per client, or does each client need its own instance?
#34 / #40: Can an agent grant another person temporary access to one ticket, and can a ticket be visible only to its owner and a manager?
#37: Can a non-admin business user (People team) create and change forms and templates without System Configuration (YAML) access?
#39: Is there a ticket checklist feature with an owner and due date per item, or only process activities?
#41: Can tickets be imported from CSV through the Import/Export module?
#49: Can the requester's manager be filled in automatically from Google Workspace (or another directory) for approvals?
#52 / #54: Are the HubSpot and ServiceNow connectors packaged products or service projects? Price, package, sync direction?
#57: Can a person's data be exported (data subject access request), and who runs privacy rules on Managed?
#58: Can different clients' data be hosted in different regions within one contract (separate instances), and is India available?
#33: Does the mobile app send push notifications for new or escalated tickets? What does "SMS Alert" cost?
Package mapping: how do the Features Manual packages (SILVER, GOLD, TITANIUM, PLATINUM) map to Starter / Advanced / Pro?
checks: Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 5 / Partial 10 / Unknown 1.

Access: the HTML docs at academy.otrs.com/doc/ returned 403 (firewall); the official PDF manuals on the same site (Admin 2025.6.1, User 2025.8.1) are separate public files that returned HTTP 200 to a plain request without header changes. Using them is not treated as circumventing a block.

#26 is Partial under the uniform rule (only data-centre operators certified), but OTRS states it "currently does not maintain ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certification". Under Notes #13 ("Immature vendors without certifications are out") this is a likely knockout in practice.

#8 Meets kept: the ACL reference documents limiting possible states per process (ProcessEntityID); comparable to Halo #8 (allowed statuses per ticket type) and Zendesk #8 (statuses per form). It is configuration work, not a ready setting.
#21 Meets kept: vendor MCP server since 2026.5.1 with write tools (create_ticket, update_ticket), not labelled beta; needs a contract that includes the MCP feature.
Counts recomputed by script: Meets 19 / Partial 23 / Unknown 1; Musts: Meets 6 / Partial 6 / Unknown 1.

1.e: "The Email tab allows you to create email aliases by using your custom ticketing domain and automate ticket creation from emails sent to those addresses." Replies: "ticketing matches emails to tickets using the in-reply-to header and message ID". "Technician email response: This option creates either a public response to the requester or a private internal note when a ticket response is sent via email". **Note:** mail from unknown senders goes to "the Pending Emails board" unless "All Unmatched Senders" is allowlisted.
1.s: [Email and Notification Management](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/ticketing/ticketing-email-notification-management/); [Configure General Settings](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/ticketing/ninjaone-ticketing-getting-started/configure-general-settings/); [Automation Triggers and Templates (FAQ)](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/ticketing/ninjaone-ticketing-automation/)

2.n: Many inbound addresses, each with its own form/tags (tags drive boards); domain allowlist can route to an organization (client). Unknown senders go to a Pending Emails board unless allowlisted.
2.e: "You can add as many inbound email addresses as necessary for your ticketing management." "Use tags to dictate which boards a ticket applies to". Allowlist: "Optionally, select an organization to which these emails are routed." Pick-up: "Unassigned tickets" board; "technicians can quickly assign the ticket to themselves by clicking Assign to me."

3.e: End User / Contact "…if set as the requester when a ticket is created by email… …will receive a notification at the moment the ticket is created." You can "send the default email preconfigured by NinjaOne, use a custom email template created by your organization, or opt out".

4.e: The requester is notified "at the moment the ticket is created", "when the ticket is marked resolved" and "when a public comment is posted". For status changes the table lists only "…if in the CC list when the ticket status is updated…". Workaround: event-based triggers on "Status … changes to" with an "Email (Template)" action "to the specified email address". **Missing:** a native notification to the requester on every status change. No source says the requester is notified at each approval step. No source says the email action can target the requester dynamically.

5.e: "The response panel allows technicians to publish public responses and private notes. … Only technicians can view private responses."

6.e: "Technicians may tag other technicians within ticket responses. Tags will automatically send an email notification". "Use the Additional Assignees field to add multiple technicians to the ticket for visibility and collaboration." **Missing:** tasks within a ticket. FAQ: "Can I create a 'parent' or top tier ticket to which I can add tasks? NinjaOne Ticketing is not designed for product management at this time; however, 'incident' tickets can be attached to a ticket labeled as a 'problem' for a workaround." Threaded discussions are not documented.

7.n: Manual, self and automatic assignment; changes shown in ticket activity. Immutability of the log not stated.
7.e: "technicians can quickly assign the ticket to themselves by clicking Assign to me." "You can click the X to the right of the current assignee's name to remove them". Auto: "assigns to the technician with the fewest open tickets or the longest time since they were last assigned a ticket". Audit: "This panel displays all information about changes to the ticket"; "In the ticket, you can filter to view "System Activity.""

8.n: Custom statuses exist, but as one global list (children of the 6 system statuses). Missing: status sets per process / form are not documented.
8.e: "create new custom statuses that display as children of existing system statuses (New, Open, Waiting, Paused, Resolved, Closed). You can assign these custom statuses to any ticket and apply them to board conditions, board filters, and automations."

9.e: "Forms use your custom ticketing fields". "You can make the field required or optional for either technicians or end users." Each inbound email address has a "Form" setting. The generic custom field types include "Drop-down" and "Date". **Missing:** the ticketing doc warns "Some custom fields available in other areas of NinjaOne may not be compatible with NinjaOne Ticketing" and does not list which types work. Forms per client (organization) are not documented; the only form visibility setting is "End user visible".
9.s: [Configure Custom Fields and Forms](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/ticketing/ninjaone-ticketing-configure-custom-fields-and-forms-for-tickets/); [Custom Fields: Types and Functionality](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/custom-fields/custom-field-types-functionality/); [Email and Notification Management](https://www.ninjaone.com/docs/ticketing/ticketing-email-notification-management/)

10.e: "the approvers will receive a notification that allows them to approve or deny the request via email." "You can designate any account type (technician, user, contact)". "All: All selected types must approve". "Optionally, add a description to explain why approval is required." Release notes: "routing it to a manager, device owner, role, or ad hoc list … Everything is logged right in the ticket." **Missing:** ordered steps (requester's manager first, then a department head) are not documented; the doc describes Any/All and an approval count. A "manager" approver type appears only in the release blog; the approval doc does not list it or say where the manager comes from.

11.n: Manual linking and parent/child with custom relationship types; parent responses go to children. Missing: automatic creation of a sub-ticket for another team (no "create ticket" automation action); child status view on the parent not documented. Limits: parent cannot be resolved with open children; the doc also says children cannot be edited until the parent is resolved.
11.e: "The Related Tickets tab allows you to link tickets or assign them to a parent (top-level) ticket." "When you add a Public Response to a parent ticket, it is published to all linked tickets." "You cannot resolve a parent ticket and leave related child tickets open. You cannot edit child tickets until you resolve the parent ticket." FAQ: "NinjaOne Ticketing is not designed for product management at this time"

12.e: "If the field is set to 'No access,' the end user can only view tickets that they reported". With "Allowed" they "will be able to view all tickets under a specific organization regardless of who reported it." **Note:** the default value of this setting is not stated. Another doc says a user with Ticketing permissions in an organization "will see all tickets for that organization", so the setting must be checked. Portal visibility of tickets where the user is only CC'd is not documented.

13.e: "Access to tickets is based on organization access, meaning a technician with access to an organization will have access to all tickets for that organization, regardless of the permissions set in the Ticketing section." Board access: "Technicians can still access the tickets from the Ticketing tab on the organization dashboard." **Exists:** separation per client, if each client is an organization. **Missing:** watertight team desks (IT, People, Finance) inside one organization; restricting boards only hides them from the sidebar.

14.n: Event-based and time-based if/then triggers with ANY/ALL conditions and actions (update ticket, assign, CC, comment, email, notification, approval).
14.e: "Event-based: These automation rules trigger when any or all of the specified conditions are met. Conditions can include actions (ticket created), business hours, ticket type or status, assigned organization, associated custom fields, and more." Actions include "Update Ticket", "Auto assign ticket", "Send Notification", "Assign approval process".

15.e: "For each target, define the agreed-upon Response time and Resolution time values" under "Priority targets". The assignee is notified "if assigned to a ticket that has exceeded 80% of its allotted SLA time" and when it "has breached its SLA". Time-based condition: "Before SLA target time: Perform a specified action during a specified time before the SLA target time occurs."

16.e: The ticketing summary report includes "Mean Time to Resolve", "First Response Time", "Ticket Volume", "Technician Ticket Efficiency", "Ticketing - SLA Compliance Summary" and "SLA Breach Detail". Queues: "Default boards include Unassigned tickets, All tickets, My tickets".

17.e: "Is there an audit feature in each ticket …? In the ticket, you can filter to view 'System Activity.'" The activity panel "displays all information about changes to the ticket". Comments can be edited, with "View edit history". **Missing:** no source says entries cannot be changed. "Allow users to edit comments … This setting is active by default", and "end users in the end-user portal do not see that a comment has been edited."

18.n: Katana AI on the ticket page recommends a solution and finds related tickets, but Katana AI is in early access (rule 5). Uses similar tickets, NinjaOne KB and NinjaOne's own Dojo articles. Price not listed.
18.e: "This feature is in early access." "The Recommend solution button provides a suggested course of action to resolve or troubleshoot the issue. It will use information from similar tickets and Dojo articles and include links to references." "The AI assistant will search the system for similar tickets, Knowledge Base articles, and scripts"

19.n: No AI categorization or AI routing of tickets found. Routing is rule-based (triggers, board conditions, round-robin style auto-assign). Katana AI lists only "Problem triage (recommending what you should work on next)".
19.e: "Auto assign ticket … assigns to the technician with the fewest open tickets or the longest time since they were last assigned a ticket"; Katana features: "Ticket summaries", "Problem triage (recommending what you should work on next)"

20.n: Katana AI reads the NinjaOne KB; drafting KB articles from resolved tickets is not documented.
20.e: Katana features: "Knowledge base access to understand specific processes and procedures"; ticket options are only "Summarize the Ticket", "Suggest a Response to the Ticket Reporter", "Recommend a Solution for the Ticket", "Find Related Tickets"

21.n: Vendor MCP server announced 2026-10-13 ("take action directly in the NinjaOne platform"), but its MCP guide is behind login (blocked), ticket tools and GA status are not verified, and Katana AI is early access. Public REST API can create and update tickets.
21.e: Press: "It lets external AI agents interact with NinjaOne data and take action directly in the NinjaOne platform." Product page: "Bring your own AI with NinjaOne Model Context Protocol (MCP) … Any compliant AI agent can reach NinjaOne's data, tools, and actions in real time". API: "POST /v2/ticketing/ticket Create ticket", "PUT /v2/ticketing/ticket/{ticketId} Update ticket"

22.n: No Notion integration found (not on the integrations page; no Zapier app). Route: custom build syncing Notion into the NinjaOne KB (NinjaOne Documentation) through the KB API. Notion side not verified. Katana AI reads only the NinjaOne KB.
22.e: KB API: "POST /v2/knowledgebase/articles Create knowledge base articles"; FAQ: "You can create a shareable link to a KB and include it to a response template."

23.e: Native Slack notification channel: "push these alerts to designated Slack channels". In ticketing automations, "Send Notification enables users to have the automation send a notification to a configured Notification Channel." **Missing:** creating tickets from Slack, private requester–agent tickets in Slack, and two-way sync of replies and status. None of these is documented. Routes: custom build on the ticketing API ("Yes. We do have APIs for ticketing") or a third-party Pipedream workflow (SECONDARY, not verified).

24.n: Public REST API with ticketing endpoints: Meets. Webhooks: one webhook configuration filtered by organization and activity type; finer filtering is "reserved for future"; the documented filter values do not list NINJA_TICKETING (ticket events appear in payload status codes). Marketplace: a curated integrations list (mostly MSP/security tools), no open app marketplace, no Zapier app.
24.e: "NinjaOne Public API 2.0 2.0.9-draft OAS3"; ticketing: "Create ticket", "Add comment to ticket", "Update ticket", "List ticket log entries". Webhooks: "Webhooks provide instant notifications about activities and other events via HTTP requests to your web services." Filter: "organizationIds … List of organization id to be filtered"; "This is reserved for future more granular activity filtering. You can use * for now." Status codes include "NINJA_TICKETING_TICKET_CREATED", "NINJA_TICKETING_UPDATED".

25.n: SAML 2.0 SSO for technicians with a vendor guide for Google Workspace (caveat: NinjaOne has "only tested and verified Azure, OneLogin, and Okta"). NinjaOne MFA applies to technicians and end users. No separate SSO subscription found.
25.e: "Configuring NinjaOne SAML in Google Workspace … navigate to admin.google.com → Apps → Web and mobile apps → Add app → Add custom SAML App." "Any IdP that supports SAML 2.0 may be used. However, we have only tested and verified Azure, OneLogin, and Okta." MFA: "all NinjaOne technicians and end users should still have a NinjaOne MFA configured. They will still be required to perform MFA for security-sensitive operations after logging in."

26.e: The Trust Center lists "ISO 27001:2022", "SOC 2", "NIS 2 Directive" and "GDPR", plus resources "NinjaOne ISO 27001 Certificate" and "NinjaOne – SOC2 Type 2 – 2026". The ISO page says: "As an ISO 27001-certified provider". **NIS2:** a "NIS2" resource is listed, but its content is behind "Request Access". **Not verified:** whether the ISO 27001 certificate scope names Ticketing.

27.e: "Data is stored within AWS in the region you choose." An EU instance exists: "app.ninjarmm.com, eu.ninjarmm.com, oc.ninjarmm.com, or ca.ninjarmm.com". AWS sub-processor locations: "USA, Canada, Germany, Australia". **Missing:** which country hosts the EU instance. Backups: "Backup Frequency: Nightly" with no location given. AI processing location is not documented (Katana AI is Early Access). Some sub-processors are outside the EU: "Sentry … USA", "Exypnox Technical Support Services Philippines", and "Anthropic Enterprise AI Services for Technical Support USA, …".

28.n: No retention-period setting for tickets or attachments found. Only manual deletion; deleted tickets are purged after a fixed 30 days. The ticketing API lists no delete-ticket endpoint, so scripted deletion is not documented either.
28.e: "NinjaOne stores deleted tickets in the Deleted Tickets board for the next 30 days, after which they are permanently deleted."

29.e: No official statement found that requesters or end users are free. Pricing is per device: "We use per-device pricing". Approvers can be any account type, and "Approvers without a NinjaOne login can clear it straight from the email, no sign-in required". This shows that approvers do not need a login. It does not show what anyone's licence costs.

30.n: No end-user chat or AI assistant answering from the KB found. NinjaOne Chat is technician-initiated on managed Windows devices (needs the endpoint agent); Katana AI is a technician tool; Slack is a notification channel only.
30.e: "Chat is technician-initiated and available for Windows devices at launch." Slack channel: "push these alerts to designated Slack channels". End users: "submit, track, and update their own tickets" in the portal.

31.n: End-user portal with the forms made visible to end users. Missing: a service catalog and links to requests handled in other systems (e.g. Aboard) are not documented. End users must be added via End User Sharing with Ticketing permission.
31.e: "The end user can choose from any ticket template forms that have been made visible to them" "End users added to your NinjaOne account via End User Sharing can submit tickets directly through their self-service portal."

32.n: The portal is brandable; branding per client (organization) and quick setup from existing data are not documented.
32.e: "A customizable, brandable portal lets end users submit, track, and update their own tickets"

33.n: Ticket automations can send to notification channels, which include PagerDuty and SMS. Note: "If SMS has been turned off in your environment, the option will not be available." Technician mobile app (NinjaOne Assist) exists; push for tickets not verified.
33.e: Action: "Send Notification: Sends notification based on pre-configured notification channels." Channels: "Slack Microsoft Teams PagerDuty Webhook Email SMS". Integrations page: PagerDuty "automatically notifying on-call technicians".

34.n: CC (technicians, end users, contacts) and additional assignees; both can be removed. Caveat: CC does not grant access; a technician still needs access to the ticket's organization.
34.e: "Use the Additional Assignees field to add multiple technicians to the ticket for visibility and collaboration." "Add CC: Adds a carbon copy (CC) to the ticket"; "Set CC: Clears all current CCd emails on the ticket and replaces them." Notification "when removed from a ticket they were previously assigned to". "The mentioned technician must have permission to view tickets assigned to the organization related to the ticket."

35.n: Tickets link only to other tickets. The API has generic "related items" endpoints, but whether tickets can hold structured links to Notion or GitHub items is not documented.
35.e: "Link Other Tickets within a Response … using the hash (#) function followed by the ticket number"; API: "POST /v2/related-items/entity/{entityType}/{entityId}/relation Create entity relation" (entity types not listed)

36.n: The forms guide covers field selection, order and required/optional only; no conditional or dependent fields documented.
36.e: "You can make the field required or optional for either technicians or end users." "Select the fields you would like to include on the form."

37.n: Forms are built in the UI without code. Missing: forms are configured in Administration → Apps → NinjaOne Ticketing; a permission that lets a business team manage only its own forms is not documented.
37.e: "Select the fields you would like to include on the form." "Drag and drop the fields to create a custom order, and then click Save." "Navigate to Administration → Apps and select NinjaOne Ticketing."

38.n: Only an all-or-nothing end-user visibility toggle per form is documented; restricting a form to a group (e.g. managers) is not.
38.e: "End user visible: Click this box to make the form visible to end users"

39.n: Checklist templates with per-task owners and due dates exist in NinjaOne Documentation (separate module), attached to organizations. Missing: ticket templates with checklists, or checklists attached to tickets, are not documented.
