39.e: "Creating checklist templates ensures easy replication". "You can assign an entire checklist to one technician, or you can assign each task within the checklist to separate technicians. Additionally, you can assign a due date to the whole checklist or each task."

40.n: Access is controlled per organization, not per ticket. A separate organization for HR tickets is a possible workaround (my inference, not documented or tested).
40.e: "Access to tickets is based on organization access, meaning a technician with access to an organization will have access to all tickets for that organization, regardless of the permissions set in the Ticketing section."

41.n: CSV import exists for contacts only; ticket import not found. Route: script on the public API ("Create ticket").
41.e: "You can import contacts for the organization in bulk by copying and pasting from a CSV file." API: "POST /v2/ticketing/ticket Create ticket"

42.n: The vendor FAQ says no; the only workaround is scheduled scripts (device policies, needs the endpoint agent).
42.e: "Do we have the ability to use scheduled or reoccurring tickets? No. Nothing outside of the scheduled script workaround."

43.n: Route: event-based trigger (status changed to Closed) → "Send Notification" to a Webhook channel or "Email (Manual)" with placeholders; or API webhooks. The receiving register needs a custom build; the ticket fields in the notification payload are not documented. No Zapier app.
43.e: "Status: Perform an action if Ticket Status equals, does not equal, changes to, or changes from the selected Ticket Status." "Email (Manual): Sends an email to the specified addresses with the option to use placeholders". Channel: "Webhook … Add the Webhook URL to which you would like the notification(s) to be sent."

44.n: Tickets are created automatically from NinjaOne conditions (needs the NinjaOne agent/policies on client-hosted systems, Endpoint Management) or from emails sent by third-party monitoring systems. Pointing to a solution relies on Katana AI (early access) or linked procedures; automatic linking not documented.
44.e: "Condition-based ticket creation from NinjaOne alerts generates a tracked work item before the end user even notices the issue." "Currently, NinjaOne conditions and scheduled scripts can be configured to create tickets." "network monitoring systems, can be configured to send email notifications to NinjaOne Ticketing when an event is detected."

45.n: Board filters by requester and created date; custom fields usable as board conditions; ticketing report template; CSV export. Missing: numeric range comparisons (e.g. amount above X) are not documented (operators are equals/includes).
45.e: Board filters: "Status Organization Requester More filters Created". Board conditions: "Custom Fields: Custom fields you create within a NinjaOne division". FAQ: "Go to Reporting and create a new summary report with the Ticketing template."

46.n: Ticket timer (auto or manual), time added by automation, report of time per technician. Separate from SLA timers.
46.e: "The timer in the response window indicates how long the ticket has been worked and either starts automatically when you click inside the response or can be manually started". "Add Time: Adds time to the ticket timer if configured." FAQ on time spent by technicians: "create a new summary report with the Ticketing template."

47.n: Time-since conditions on boards and time-based automations send alerts; SLA at-risk notifications. Missing: a reminder set by an agent on an individual ticket is not documented ("Follow-up time" appears only as a board condition).
47.e: "You can use time-based automations to send notifications when a ticket has been open or paused for a set period." Board conditions: "Time since end user/contact responded", "Follow-up time: The amount of time between now and when an update on the ticket is due".

48.n: Recent tickets by user in the ticket view (last year) and board filter by requester.
48.e: "User: See other tickets requested by this user." "Recent tickets will track data from one year before the current date". Board filter: "Requester".

49.n: Approver types do not include the requester's manager, and with Google Workspace users are created manually (no SCIM).
49.e: "If you select User, Technician role, Contact, or End user role from the Type drop-down menu"; "Since Google does not have SCIM, you will need to create your users manually before they can use SSO in NinjaOne."

50.n: No official Zapier app found (zapier.com/apps/ninjaone returned 404; not on the NinjaOne integrations page). Route: Webhooks by Zapier plus the NinjaOne public API and webhooks (custom build).
50.e: zapier.com: "404 Not Found"; NinjaOne API: "Webhooks provide instant notifications about activities and other events via HTTP requests to your web services."

51.n: No Outline integration found. Route: custom build on the NinjaOne KB API (or KB shareable links in response templates). Outline side not verified.
51.e: "POST /v2/knowledgebase/articles Create knowledge base articles"; "You can create a shareable link to a KB and include it to a response template."

52.n: No HubSpot integration on the integrations page and no Zapier app. Route: custom build creating organizations and contacts through the NinjaOne API from HubSpot data.
52.e: API: "POST /v2/organizations Create new organization", "POST /v2/contacts Create a contact"

53.n: No Productive integration found. Route: custom build on the API (tickets and log entries); Productive side not verified.

54.n: The ServiceNow integration sends NinjaOne alerts out as ServiceNow tickets and syncs CMDB; receiving tickets from a client's ServiceNow is not documented. Inbound routes: the client tool emails an inbound address, or a custom API build.
54.e: "If you have other ticketing applications enabled, such as ServiceNow, you will notice an option to create a ticket through that integration." Integrations page: "Accelerate service desk operations and CMBD sync with the NinjaOne + ServiceNow integration"

55.n: No calendar sync for ticket deadlines found. An "Appointment" ticket type exists inside NinjaOne only.
55.e: "You can use appointment tickets to set reminders for meetings."

56.n: No Aboard integration found. Route: custom build where an Aboard event calls "Create ticket" on the NinjaOne API. Aboard side not verified.

57.n: Building blocks only: ticket export with all comments, manual ticket deletion (purged after 30 days), contact and end-user deletion via API. No DSR tool or one-step person deletion/export found.
57.e: "Clicking Export provides the options to: Export tickets only Export tickets with public comments Export tickets with all comments". API: "DELETE /v2/contact/{id} Delete a contact", "DELETE /v2/user/end-user/{id} Delete end user"

58.n: Region is chosen per account/instance (regional hostnames), so per-client regions would need separate instances (rule 13). Hosting locations listed: USA, Canada, Germany, Australia; India not listed.
58.e: "Data is stored within AWS in the region you choose." "Amazon Web Services Cloud Infrastructure/Hosting USA, Canada, Germany, Australia". Webhook hostnames: "It depends on which instance your Ninja account is located in." (North America, EMEA, APAC)

59.n: Default "My tickets" and "Unassigned tickets" boards plus custom filter-based boards (e.g. by assignee). List views; kanban not documented.
59.e: Default boards: "My tickets" – "Tickets assigned to the logged-in technician"; "Unassigned tickets". "A ticketing board is a filter-based saved view of your tickets." Conditions include "Primary assignee" and "Additional assignees".

questions: #29 / licensing: Are technicians, end users and contacts (requesters and approvers) free of charge, with the price based only on managed devices? Is there any per-technician fee for Ticketing?

Licensing: Can NinjaOne Ticketing be bought without RMM / endpoint management licences? If so, how is it priced when few or no endpoints are managed (for example a desk that mostly answers client email)? Is there a minimum contract?

#27: Which AWS region and country host the EU instance (eu.ninjarmm.com)? Are platform backups and DR copies kept in the EU? Where is Katana AI processing done? Which sub-processors outside the EU (for example Sentry, Exypnox, Anthropic) can access ticket data?

#23: Is there a NinjaOne Slack app, current or on the roadmap, that creates tickets from a Slack channel or command, keeps them private between requester and agent, and syncs replies and status both ways?

#26: Does the ISO 27001:2022 certificate scope cover NinjaOne Ticketing? What does the "NIS2" document in the Trust Center contain?
AI: When does Katana AI become generally available, and what will it cost? Is NinjaOne MCP generally available?
#19: Does Katana AI (or any NinjaOne feature) categorize incoming tickets and route them to a board or technician automatically? Is it GA, and at what price?
#20: Can Katana AI draft knowledge base articles from resolved tickets? If yes, GA or early access, and price?
#28: Can we set a retention period after which tickets and attachments are deleted automatically? Is there an API endpoint to delete tickets?

#18: When will Katana AI be generally available, is it included in the licence or priced separately, and where is Katana AI processing done (EU)?
#8: Can a set of custom statuses be limited to one form or process (e.g. only People forms)?

#11: Can an automation create a child ticket for another team (e.g. onboarding ticket → IT equipment ticket)? Does the parent show child status? Is it correct that child tickets cannot be edited until the parent is resolved?

#22 / #51: Is any Notion or Outline integration planned or available beyond the KB API?
#30: Is there an end-user chat or AI assistant (portal or Slack) that answers from the KB and opens tickets? Can NinjaOne Chat be used without the endpoint agent?
#31 / #32: Can the end-user portal show a service catalog with links to other systems, and can each client (organization) have its own branded portal?
#35: Can tickets hold related items linking to Notion pages or GitHub issues?
#36: Do ticket forms support conditional / dependent fields?
#37: Can a non-admin technician (e.g. People team) be allowed to build and edit only their own forms?
#38: Can a form be made visible only to a selected group of end users (e.g. managers)?
#39: Can a checklist template be attached to a ticket or ticket form (onboarding/offboarding)?
#40: Can a single ticket be hidden from technicians who have access to its organization?
#49: Can approvals target the requester's manager, and can user/manager data sync from Google Workspace?
#55: Can ticket due dates or tasks sync to Google Calendar?
#58: Can one account keep different clients' data in different regions (US, India), or does each region need a separate instance and licence?

Pricing: how is Ticketing priced for an organization using it mainly as a helpdesk (per technician, per device, or bundled), and which modules (Documentation, Katana AI, Endpoint Management) are needed for the features above?
checks: Format and counts checked by script: 16 rows; Meets 7 / Partial 8 / Unknown 1.
